threads.title: 中断工具调用后重试会复用旧 seq，导致会话日志损坏无法打开（seq gap in committed region）
threads.bodyText:
## 问题描述

当工具调用在执行途中被中断（interrupt/cancel），随后用户恢复会话并重试该工具时，重试产生的事件会**复用崩溃恢复占位事件的 seq**，而不是从 `lastSeq + 1` 继续。结果会话日志出现 seq 回退，下次加载直接失败，整个会话无法打开：

Error: corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region at line 1649
(expected 5259, got 5255)

## 复现步骤

1. 启动一个会话，让 Agent 执行一个耗时较长的工具（例如 `bash` 跑 `curl` / `sleep 30` 等几秒以上的命令）。
2. 工具执行到一半时中断当前 turn（取消 / 停止）。此时触发崩溃恢复路径 `interruptedTurnClosers()`，它会合成并持久化一批"关闭事件"：

tool/result  (isError: "The tool call was interrupted...")  → seq N
step/end                                                    → seq N+1
turn/end    (reason: "interrupted")                         → seq N+2
session/end-seed                                            → seq N+3
3. 恢复会话，让 Agent 重试同一个工具调用。重试得到的工具结果事件被写成了 `seq = N`（复用了占位事件的 seq），而不是 `N+4`。

## 预期行为

重试事件应继续严格递增的 seq 序列（`seq = lastSeq + 1`），即重试的 `tool/result` 应该是 `N+4`，保持日志单调递增、可正常回放。

## 实际行为

重试事件复用了 `N..N+3` 四个 seq，产生 seq 回退。下一次加载时，`SessionLogScanner` 在 committed region 检测到 seq 断层即抛 `seq gap`，会话无法打开。手工修掉这个 seq 断层后，还会连锁触发下游投影层的错位：

- `surface replace: start seq ... not found in surface`
- `sourceEventSeqs must include every shadowed surface node; missing ...`
- `token surface: replace ... has no adjacent shadow price (armed claim covers ...)`

## 实测到的损坏 seq 序列（来自一个真实损坏的 `session.jsonl.zstd`）


index 5254  seq=5254  tool/call           (工具开始)
index 5255  seq=5255  tool/result         isError=true   ← 崩溃恢复占位
index 5256  seq=5256  step/end
index 5257  seq=5257  turn/end            (interrupted)
index 5258  seq=5258  session/end-seed
index 5259  seq=5255  tool/result         isError=false  ← 重试：seq 复用 5255 ✗
index 5260  seq=5256  step/end                          ← 复用 5256 ✗
index 5261  seq=5257  step/start                        ← 复用 5257 ✗
index 5262  seq=5258  assistant/chunk                    ← 复用 5258 ✗
index 5263  seq=5259  assistant/chunk                    ← 从此之后 seq = index - 4

正确的应该是：重试的 4 个事件为 `5259..5262`，之后所有事件 `seq == index`。

## 环境

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.0-rc.7 / 0.1.0-rc.8
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session` 0.1.0-rc.8
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` 0.1.0-rc.8
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter` 0.1.0-rc.8
- 存储压缩：zstd（多 frame 拼接）

## 根因分析

`Session.append()` 里 `seq = this.log.length`，并强制 `seq === index` 的连续契约（`SessionLogScanner.consumeEventLine` / `assertSessionEventEnvelope` 都在校验）。所以正常 append 流程不可能产生回退。回退只有在「重试路径使用了恢复前的 stale seq 计数器」时才会发生。

具体链路：

1. 中断时最后 turn 是 open turn（写了 `turn/start`、没写 `turn/end`）。
2. 下次加载时 `interruptedTurnClosers()` 扫描 tail，合成 error `tool/result`、`step/end`、`turn/end{interrupted}`，并让 backend durably commit 这批合成 closers。
3. resume 后重试工具时，重试路径似乎使用了一个 **resume 之前 / 合成 closers 之前**的 seq 值（即原 `tool/call` 被记录时的 seq N），而不是 resum 后 live `log.length`，于是又写出了 `N..N+3`。

另一个相关点：`interruptedTurnClosers()` 合成的占位 `tool/result` 是 `surfaceOp: "append"`。如果重试结果也以 `append` 进入 surface（而不是 replace 掉那个中断占位），同一个逻辑工具调用就会在 surface 上留下两个节点——这正是修掉 seq 断层后还会出现 `sourceEventSeqs` / token-meter 投影错位的原因。

> 附：仓库内设计笔记 `.agents/notes/rejected/simplification/2026-06-20-truncate-interrupted-turns.md` 讨论了这套「合成 closers」机制，但方案最终被 rejected（保留现有机制），因此该 bug 在最新 tag `dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2` 中仍然存在（我对比过 rc.7 → rc.2 的源码，`interruptedTurnClosers` 的 `seq = last.seq + 1`、`Session.append` 的 `seq = this.log.length`、closers 的 `surfaceOp: 'append'` 均未改变，207 个 commit 中也无针对此回归的修复）。

## 建议修复方向

1. **让 resume/重试路径严格从 live `session.log.length` 派生每一个新事件的 seq**（统一走 `Session.append`），不要使用缓存或中断前的 seq 计数器。
2. **考虑把「中断后重试」的结果表示为对中断占位 `tool/result` 的 surface replace**（同 callId），而不是再 append 一次，避免同一逻辑工具调用在 surface 上留下重复节点。
3. **（防御性）** 加载时检测到 committed-region seq 回退时，除了报当前 line/seq 冲突，再识别是否为「interrupted-tool-retry」模式（周围事件符合 `session/end-seed` 后紧跟同 callId 的 `tool/result`），以区分「瞬时崩溃产物」和「真实损坏」，给用户更可操作的提示。

## 临时恢复手段（供参考）

已成功恢复损坏会话：把 4 个重试事件 renumber 为 `N+4`，将其后所有 seq 值 +4，并同步 +4 修正所有 surface 引用（`surfaceOp.start/end`、`sourceEventSeqs`、`compaction/prune` 的 `shadowedRange/shadowedSeqs`），再按「首帧一行 header、每事件独立 frame + checksum」重建 zstd 文件。这印证了损坏纯粹是 seq 计数器回退，而非数据丢失。

threads.title: ox alpha 直接配置不支持多模态！！！
Bug report draft: native read_image tool fails with "cannot get property 'fs' without inject" (all presets)
threads.bodyText:
Environment: dsh 0.1.0-rc.6, Windows, web profile. Reproduces on freedom (user preset) and should reproduce on every preset mounting @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs, since the defect is in the package itself.
Symptom
Calling the native read_image tool fails immediately:
Error: cannot get property "fs" without inject

read, write, and edit work normally — only read_image fails. The image file is irrelevant.
Root cause
In @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs/lib/index.js, apply() registers read_image
inside an attachments-gated sub-context and passes that sub-context down:
const inject = ["tools", "fs", "systemPrompt"]; // plugin-level declarations

function apply(ctx, config) {
  applyReadTool(ctx);                            // fine: outer ctx declares fs
  ctx.inject(["attachments"], (imageCtx) => {
    applyReadImageTool(imageCtx);                // ← imageCtx only declares "attachments"
  });
  ...
}
But applyReadImageTool's execute body dereferences ctx.fs.readBytes(...)
(and registers through ctx.tools.register(...)) as a property access. Cordis's
guard throws on undeclared service-property access, so execution dies with
cannot get property "fs" without inject.
The function's own doc comment states the intended contract:
@param ctx - the registration scope; execution uses its `fs` service plus
  the optional `attachments`/`llm` services.

i.e. the caller was supposed to pass the outer scope; the call site passes the
narrowed accessor instead. Note the body already handles the optional services
correctly via runtime lookups (ctx.get("attachments"), ctx.get("llm")) —
only the declared-service property accesses (fs, tools) are affected.
Suggested fix (one line at the call site)
-	ctx.inject(["attachments"], (imageCtx) => {
-		applyReadImageTool(imageCtx);
-	});
+	ctx.inject(["attachments"], () => {
+		applyReadImageTool(ctx);
+	});
The outer ctx declares tools + fs; attachments remains a runtime
ctx.get(). Registration timing is unchanged (still gated on attachments
becoming available). Alternatively, widen the inner inject to
["attachments", "fs", "tools"] — either satisfies the guard.
Workaround in the wild
Routing image reads through an external vision CLI (e.g. modlens) sidesteps the
DSH tool pipeline entirely, which is how we noticed only read_image was
affected while sibling fs tools stayed healthy.

threads.title: Could a sticky max-tokens state cause the agent loop to skip a required tool-result step?
threads.bodyText:
ImportantWhile reading the DSH 0.1.1-rc.1 code, I noticed a potential control-flow issue in the agent loop. A sticky max-tokens value may cause a later tool-calling step to end the turn before the model can read the tool result, even though step() returns null to request another step.

The same logic appears to still be present in DSH 0.1.1-rc.2.
The relevant code is in packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts, around lines 285–299.
The code intentionally keeps max-tokens sticky at the turn level. Once a step reaches the token limit, a later step that completes normally does not downgrade the final turn outcome. Lines 285–290 implement this by retaining the earlier max-tokens value in turnEnds.
However, lines 295–299 also use turnEnds to decide whether the step loop should stop.
The potential failure sequence is:


Step 1 ends with max-tokens. Before the turn stops, a steer message causes the same turn to continue.


Step 2 then makes an ordinary tool call. The tool executes successfully, and step() returns null, indicating that another step is required so the model can read the tool result.


Because turnEnds already contains max-tokens, the null returned by Step 2 does not replace it. If the tool result is stored in the Session history but the tool does not add any additionalContexts, inbox.nextStep may be empty.


The condition on line 299 would then still see a truthy turnEnds value and an empty nextStep inbox, causing the loop to break immediately after Step 2. The tool result would exist in the Session history, but the model would not receive the next step needed to read it.



Is there another mechanism that guarantees continuation in this sequence, or can the sticky turn-level max-tokens state incorrectly terminate a step that explicitly returned null?

threads.title: Produced-file chips bypass the canOpenPath/isLoopback gate that 'show in folder' correctly respects
threads.bodyText:
Summary
On a headless server accessed remotely (browser connects over an SSH tunnel to a loopback-forwarded port, but the actual DSH host process has no display), clicking a produced-file chip crashes with a native-command failure instead of being disabled/hidden like the adjacent "show in folder" affordance.
Repro

Run dsh web --host 127.0.0.1 on a headless Linux server with no DISPLAY/WAYLAND_DISPLAY, no desktop browser installed.
Access it from a different machine via an SSH local port-forward (ssh -L 3080:127.0.0.1:3080 ...), so the browser sees localhost (loopback) but the actual filesystem/host process is remote and headless.
Have an agent turn produce a file (e.g. an .svg).
Click the produced-file chip in the turn tail.

Actual result
path open failed: path open failed: Command failed: xdg-open /path/to/file.svg
/usr/bin/xdg-open: 882: www-browser: not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: 882: links2: not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: 882: elinks: not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: 882: links: not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: 882: lynx: not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: 882: w3m: not found
xdg-open: no method available for opening '/path/to/file.svg'

(Before installing xdg-utils at all, the failure is instead spawn xdg-open ENOENT.)
Root cause
In packages/client/ui-deliverables/src/client/ProducedFiles.tsx, canOpenPath is computed correctly:
const canOpenPath = isLoopback && hostCanOpenPath
and it correctly gates the "show in folder" button:
{hidden > 0 && canOpenPath && (
  <button type="button" className={css.showFolder} onClick={() => { openFile('.') }}>
    {t('produced.showInFolder')}
  </button>
)}
But the per-file chip buttons rendered just above are not gated by canOpenPath at all — they always render as clickable and always call openFile(path) regardless of whether the host can actually open a path natively:
{shown.map(path => (
  <button
    key={path}
    type="button"
    className={css.file}
    title={path}
    aria-label={t('produced.open', { name: path })}
    onClick={() => { openFile(path) }}
  >
    {basename(path)}
  </button>
))}
This is inconsistent with packages/host/apiproxy/src/native-path-opener.ts's own canOpenNativePath(), whose doc comment says headless detection exists precisely "which lets a surface show a path as text instead of offering a button that would spawn xdg-open into nothing." The per-chip buttons don't honor that.
Suggested fix
Gate the chip's clickability (or render it as inert text with a title tooltip showing the full path, matching the doc comment's stated intent) behind the same canOpenPath used for "show in folder", so a non-loopback/headless session degrades gracefully instead of surfacing a native-command failure to the user.
Environment

Deployment: dsh web --host 127.0.0.1, no desktop environment, accessed via SSH port-forward from another machine.
OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (server), xdg-utils installed after the fact to test the fallback path (still no method available, as expected on headless).

threads.title: [Bug]？ goal 功能开启后 agent 无法被动等待后台任务：每次进入 idle 即被强制注入 <goal_round>，空转消耗轮次与 token
threads.bodyText:
在使用DSH进行一个长任务时，中间agent需要等待运行结果，但是目标功能不断启动goal上下文注入，只能通过手动暂停goal功能以停止。请问这是DSH本身问题还是我使用的问题？下面是DS总结的具体内容。
环境
DSH 本地 npm 安装版，涉及包：@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal、@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver、@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs
版本号：v0.1.1 rc.2
问题描述
开启 goal（目标默认 active + armed，续行启用）后，当 agent 需要"等待后台任务完成"并采用工具文档推荐策略——结束回合、不轮询、等完成通知——goal 会在 agent 每次进入 idle 时强制注入 <goal_round> 目标上下文并开启新一轮：
agent 无法停留在 idle 被动等待，每回合结束都被立即注入唤醒；
每一轮被迫产出"还在等待"之类的空转回合；
roundsStarted 逐轮递增（默认上限 256），每轮重发完整会话历史 + 目标块，token 持续消耗；
空转回合中 agent 甚至出现对"已过去多久"的幻觉式估计（无新信息却自称 ~15/20/25 min in）。
预期行为
agent 按工具指引被动等待后台任务期间，goal 不应注入/强制续行；任务完成通知到达后再继续（或由用户显式 resume）。
实际行为
回合记录中每回合均带"上下文注入 goal"标记，Round 连续出现"等待中 / End round"，数分钟内多个空转回合，目标上下文被反复注入。如下图：

复现
创建目标（保持 active + armed，如 maxGoalRounds: 2 即可）；
启动一个较长后台任务（如 pwsh 循环 Start-Sleep，约 2.5 分钟）；
指示 agent"等待完成通知、不轮询"，结束回合；
观察：几秒内注入 <goal_round>（Round 1/2，含完整目标），此时任务仍在运行（才到第 1 个 tick），roundsStarted 由 0 变为 1。
对照：回合内用 job_output(wait: true) 阻塞等待则无注入（roundsStarted 保持 0）——触发条件是 idle 检查点，与是否调用等待工具无关。

threads.title: [bug] Spawn-backed subagents drop reasoningEffort; endpoints that require thinking reject every delegation
threads.bodyText:
Summary
Fresh spawn-backed subagents silently drop reasoningEffort while inheriting the parent's provider/model route, producing requests without a thinking parameter. Endpoints whose models always think then hard-reject every delegation.
Real-world failure (z.ai GLM glm-5.3-flash, reasoningEfforts low/high/max):
400 {"code":"1210","message":"This model always engages in thinking and cannot be disabled; please use low, high, or max"}

The parent tool only sees Error: subagent run failed — no diagnostic — because the in-process driver never populates SubagentResult.diagnostic.
Evidence
Two child sessions, same parent, same provider/model (glm/glm-5.3-flash):



backend
request/header config
outcome




subagent_fork
{provider, model, reasoningEffort: "max"}
✅ completed


subagent (spawn)
{provider, model} — no effort
❌ 400 / 1210



Root cause chain (v0.1.1-rc.2 sources):

AgentOptions (packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts) has no reasoningEffort field at all;
resolveChildAgentOptions (packages/subagent/subagent/src/child-agent.ts) documents inheriting "the parent's provider/model/maxTokens route" — effort cannot even ride along;
In-process children install no installModelSelection, and a fresh loop has no persisted request/header to restore effort from (agent-loop/src/agent.ts buildRequest seeds {provider, model} only);
Adapter omits the thinking parameter when effort is undefined (dsh-llm-pi-ai translates absence as provider-default) → z.ai rejects.

Fork is unaffected because it clones the full session header including the persisted effort.
Proposed fixes (PR incoming)

Add optional reasoningEffort?: ReasoningEffortId to AgentOptions; inherit it in resolveChildAgentOptions; fall back to it when building a fresh loop's seed config (persisted header keeps precedence).
Populate SubagentResult.diagnostic in the in-process driver from the child terminal turn/end error (LlmFailure.message) so parents see endpoint detail instead of a bare headline.

Environment
DSH 0.1.1-rc.2 · agent preset gamedev · tool-subagent provider spawn (backgroundMode continuable)
Filed here because the repository issue tracker is disabled.

threads.title: 【BUG】DSH底层问题详细Bug报告
threads.bodyText:
DeepSeek Harness / DSH Desktop Bug Report
1. 报告摘要
本报告记录在 DSH Desktop 中观察到的两个相关但相互独立的问题，供 DeepSeek Harness 官方维护者定位和修复：

工具调用参数兼容性问题：普通调用因空字符串 justification 被错误拒绝。
Windows/Synology Drive 工作区中的文件版本误报：内容未被用户修改时，write / edit 可能错误抛出 FS_STALE_VERSION。

其中，第一个问题已经通过当前官方源码确认仍然存在，且能够从源码直接推导出稳定复现路径；第二个问题的源码机制也仍然存在，但“本机实际触发是否由 Synology Drive 元数据变化导致”需要在运行中的 Desktop 重启后通过集成测试最终确认。
本报告不要求官方接受现有用户级 workaround 作为长期方案，重点请求官方确认参数归一化、版本 token 语义及对应回归测试策略。
2. 报告环境与源码基线
2.1 用户环境

操作系统：Windows
DSH Desktop：2.0.1
DSH runtime：0.1.0-rc.7
当前工作区：D:\SynologyDrive\Obsidian
工作区由 Synology Drive 管理；D:\SynologyDrive 带 Windows ReparsePoint 属性。
Synology Drive 相关进程在现场观察时处于运行状态：cloud-drive-connect、cloud-drive-daemon、cloud-drive-ui。
对照现象：同一 Synology Drive 目录在 Codex 与 Hana 中可以正常编辑。

2.2 官方源码仓库

仓库：deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
本地完整源码副本：E:\CodeFile\DSHsource
分支：master
分析时远端 master 与本地副本一致。
提交：b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e
提交时间：2026-08-21T20:03:37+08:00
对应 release 合并提交：0.1.1-rc.2

2.3 运行实例与源码的关系
运行实例位于：
D:\Program Files\DSH\DSH Desktop\resources\app.asar.unpacked\
其中可以看到打包后的 @deepseek-ai\dsh-sandbox\lib\index.js。该目录仅用于对照确认 Desktop 当前运行代码的行为，不应作为正式源码修复位置，因为安装更新可能覆盖其中的修改。
3. 问题 A：空 justification 导致普通工具调用失败
3.1 用户可见症状
新建 DSH 对话后，普通工具调用失败，返回：
Error: invalid justification: expected a non-empty sentence

该调用没有请求权限升级，也没有意图访问工作区外资源。现场推断工具适配层在序列化可选字符串字段时，将未填写的 justification 传成了空字符串 ""。
3.2 预期行为
普通工具调用不携带权限升级参数时，应当正常执行。例如：
{
  "command": "Get-Location",
  "description": "Show current workspace location"
}

如果适配层因为 schema 或序列化原因传入：
{
  "command": "Get-Location",
  "description": "Show current workspace location",
  "justification": ""
}

在没有 sandbox_permissions 的情况下，空字符串应当被视为“未提供”，而不是被当作一次真实的权限升级理由校验。
3.3 实际行为
官方当前源码中的共享校验函数位于：
E:\CodeFile\DSHsource\packages\sandbox\sandbox\src\escalation.ts
当前实现：
export function validateEscalationArgs(
  sandboxPermissions: string | undefined,
  justification: string | undefined,
): void {
  if (sandboxPermissions !== undefined && justification === undefined) {
    throw new Error('invalid escalation: sandbox_permissions requires a justification')
  }
  if (justification !== undefined && sandboxPermissions === undefined) {
    throw new Error('invalid escalation: justification is only valid together with sandbox_permissions')
  }
  if (justification !== undefined && justification.trim().length === 0) {
    throw new Error('invalid justification: expected a non-empty sentence')
  }
}

当输入为：
validateEscalationArgs(undefined, '')

执行结果为：
invalid justification: expected a non-empty sentence

原因是 justification !== undefined 对空字符串成立，随后 ''.trim().length === 0 也成立。也就是说，当前实现区分了 undefined 与 ""，但工具参数适配层可能无法稳定保持这种区分。
3.4 影响范围
该共享函数被以下工具链调用：
packages/shell/tool-pwsh/src/index.ts:99
packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:67
packages/fs/tool-fs/src/sandbox.ts:88

因此问题潜在影响：

pwsh 普通调用；
bash 普通调用；
文件系统 write / edit 等调用在其 sandbox 参数处理路径上的普通调用。

这是一个跨工具共享的参数处理问题，不应只在某一个工具包中添加临时特判。
3.5 当前测试覆盖情况
测试文件：
E:\CodeFile\DSHsource\packages\sandbox\sandbox\tests\escalation.spec.ts
当前已经覆盖：
validateEscalationArgs(undefined, undefined)
validateEscalationArgs('workspace-write', 'because the workspace needs it')
validateEscalationArgs('workspace-write', undefined)
validateEscalationArgs(undefined, 'orphan reason')
validateEscalationArgs('workspace-write', '   ')

但没有覆盖关键输入：
validateEscalationArgs(undefined, '')

因此当前测试不会捕获普通调用因空字符串字段失败的问题。
3.6 建议修复方向
优先建议在工具参数归一化层统一处理：
const sandboxPermissions = args.sandbox_permissions?.trim() || undefined
const justification = args.justification?.trim() || undefined
validateEscalationArgs(sandboxPermissions, justification)

同时，dsh-sandbox 的共享校验入口建议保留防御式兼容，至少使以下输入满足预期：
validateEscalationArgs(undefined, undefined) // 允许
validateEscalationArgs(undefined, '')        // 允许，按未提供处理

如果选择只在校验函数中兼容，也应明确其行为等价于：
if (
  sandboxPermissions === undefined &&
  (justification === undefined || justification.trim() === '')
) {
  return
}

但不建议仅修改某个 Desktop 打包后的 lib/index.js，因为这无法修复源码构建产物以外的部署方式，也无法提供正式回归保护。
3.7 必须保持的安全语义
修复不能把空字符串兼容扩大成无条件允许权限升级。以下规则应保持：



sandbox_permissions
justification
预期结果




未提供
未提供
允许普通调用


未提供
"" 或仅空白
按未提供处理，允许普通调用


未提供
非空
拒绝：理由不能脱离升级目标单独出现


非空
未提供
拒绝：升级目标必须有理由


非空
"" 或仅空白
拒绝：升级理由必须非空


非空
非空
进入原有严格权限阶梯和 approval 流程



5.2 NAS stale-version 验证

完全退出 DSH Desktop；
确认 C:\Users\lucif\.dsh\profiles\desktop\cordis.patch.yml 内容仍正确；
重启现有 Desktop，不启动替代 Web 服务器；
创建新会话；
read 一个 Synology Drive 工作区中的已有文本文件；
对同一文件执行精确 edit；
记录是否仍出现 FS_STALE_VERSION；
同时测试工作区外读取/写入；
确认越界访问仍受 sandbox 和 approval 控制；
如要确认源码根因，记录 read 与 edit 前后各 stat token 分量，尤其是 ctimeNs。

6. 建议官方关注的最小修复范围
对问题 A
最小正确修复应包括：

统一参数归一化；

threads.title: tool-cordis inspect providers are process-global: two cordis-based presets cannot coexist in one process
threads.bodyText:
tool-cordis inspect providers are process-global: two cordis-based presets cannot coexist in one process
Environment

@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.1-rc.2, web profile (dsh web via launchd)
macOS

Summary
Any two agent presets that both mount tool-cordis (i.e. a user preset copied from the shipped cordis preset via the official copy() authoring path, plus the built-in cordis preset) cannot both mount in the same process. The second one fails with:
agent-presets: preset "<name>" failed to mount:
failed to apply loader entry tool-cordis (@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-cordis):
Host Cordis inspect provider "Service" is already registered

Only a process restart resolves it, and only if the other cordis-based preset's standing mount is never triggered first.
Steps to reproduce

Create a user preset by copying cordis (the "创造模式" / creator-mode preset) through the Agent Preset settings page (agentPresets.copy).
Keep tool-cordis in the copied preset (it is copied verbatim).
Restart dsh web.
In the same process, mount the built-in cordis preset first (e.g. create a session with it, or merely select it on a blank session), then try to create/select a session with the copied preset.
The copied preset fails to mount with Host Cordis inspect provider "Service" is already registered. Swapping the order flips which preset fails.

Root cause

tool-cordis registers four Host inspect providers — Service, Event, Builtin, Tool — unconditionally at mount time (in apply: for (const provider of hostInspectProviders(ctx)) ctx.effect(() => ctx.cordisInspect.register(provider), ...)).
CordisInspectRegistryService.register() (in @deepseek-ai/dsh-cordis-host-runner) keeps a process-wide singleton providers Map and throws Host Cordis inspect provider "<id>" is already registered on any duplicate id.
Preset standing mounts are process-lifetime: once a preset's standing mount is created (by any session creation, select, or even a cold transcript read via standingKeyFor), it is never disposed while the process lives (ensureStanding; recompose only re-binds, it does not unmount the previous preset).
Therefore the first cordis-based preset to be mounted in a process permanently owns all four provider ids, and every other cordis-based preset fails forever until restart.

Impact

The official authoring path (copy() from a shipped preset) silently produces presets that are mutually exclusive with the shipped cordis preset. The UI gives no hint: the preset merely shows as failing to select / the session falls back to the default preset, while the real error is only visible in the backend.
Debugging cost is high because the failure looks unrelated to the actual cause: deleting cordis sessions from the UI does not help (standing mounts are in-memory and are not unmounted when sessions are closed/archived), and only a restart followed by mounting the desired preset first works.
This blocks legitimate use cases such as "a custom cordis-based preset for my workflow, plus the built-in creator mode, in one process."

Community confirmation
The same issue is independently documented by a third-party preset plugin, KannaKuron/dsh-ptc-cordis-preset:

"宿主面 runner 的 inspect 注册表遇重复 provider id 即抛错，是'一个进程只能开一个 cordis 模式会话'的唯一根源"
"关闭/归档会话并不卸载 standing 挂载，所以'现在没有创造模式会话'不代表竞争消失"
"根治仍建议上游把 runner 按会话多实例化"

That plugin ships a shim that monkey-patches the registration to replace duplicates (same-manifest), which confirms the pain is real and widespread.
Suggested fixes (any one)

Make the runner per-session / per-preset — instantiate the cordisInspect registry (or at least the host-inspect providers) per preset scope instead of process-global, so multiple cordis-based presets can coexist. (This is the "根治" the community plugin author recommends.)
Make registration idempotent — when a provider with the same id and an equivalent manifest is registered again, replace it (returning a disposer that only removes if it is still the current entry) instead of throwing.
At minimum, surface the error in the UI — when a preset fails to mount, show the mount error in the preset picker/session creation flow instead of silently falling back to the default preset, so users can diagnose instead of guessing.

Workaround (current)

Restart dsh web, then create/select the desired cordis-based preset before any other cordis-based preset's standing mount is triggered in the process.
Do not expect cordis-based presets to coexist; treat them as mutually exclusive per process.

threads.title: dsh-token-meter: messageTokens can underflow below 0 (Zod nonnegative fails)
threads.bodyText:
Symptom
Chat turns fail with a Zod validation error:
Too small: expected number to be >= 0

at path: ["messageTokens"], surfaced to the user as a failed turn.
Root cause
In packages/llm/token-meter, contextBreakdownProjectionDefinition.apply accumulates:
messageTokens: state.messageTokens + fold.deltaTokens,
foldSurfaceProjection returns a negative deltaTokens when a surface message is replaced/compacted (surfaceOp === "replace" → deltaTokens = tokens - claim.tokens). When the magnitude of that negative delta exceeds the currently accumulated state.messageTokens, the sum goes below zero and trips the tokenCount = z.number().int().nonnegative() schema on the next checkpoint/validation.
systemTokens / toolsTokens are always non-negative from their estimators; only messageTokens can underflow via the signed fold delta.
Suggested fix
Clamp the accumulator to a non-negative floor:
messageTokens: Math.max(0, state.messageTokens + fold.deltaTokens),
or make the shadow-price claim accounting resilient to a claim whose shadowedTokenCount exceeds the live accumulated total (the two should never disagree, but a mismatch currently hard-crashes the turn instead of degrading the heuristic figure).
Version
@deepseek-ai/dsh-token-meter@0.1.1-rc.2
Note: this figure is a heuristic context-composition estimate (display/metering only), so flooring it at 0 is safe and does not affect the actual request payload.

threads.title: 【BUG】edit 工具调用层错误地把同级权限当成了权限升级请求
threads.bodyText:
是的，这基本可以判定为一个 bug，具体在 文件工具与 sandbox 权限参数的衔接层，而不是 Full Access 策略本身。
预期行为应是：
当前文件策略 = danger-full-access
普通 edit/write
=> 直接执行
=> 不传 sandbox_permissions

实际行为却是：
当前文件策略 = danger-full-access
普通 edit/write
=> 自动附带 sandbox_permissions = danger-full-access
=> 被误判为“请求升级到同级权限”
=> 在执行文件操作前失败

关键证据是错误发生在工具参数处理阶段：
sandbox escalation to "danger-full-access"
is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode

文件系统甚至没有机会尝试写入，所以不是文件路径、权限位或 Full Access sandbox 后端拒绝。
更具体地说，可能存在以下一个或两个问题：

sandbox_permissions 被错误地作为文件工具的常规必填参数处理，而不是仅用于“sandbox 实际拒绝后的重试”；
工具执行器没有判断“请求权限是否已经等于当前生效权限”，直接把同级权限当成非法升级。

修复方向应是：
if (requestedPermission === currentPermission) {
  // 直接执行，不走 escalation
}
或者更彻底地：
普通文件工具调用不生成 sandbox_permissions；
只有收到真实 sandbox denial 后，重试调用才附带该字段。

另外，之前我在调用中主动传入这个参数，也放大了问题；按照官方文档和当前运行时规则，Full Access 下不应主动传递它。这个问题值得在 Harness 的文件工具参数适配或工具执行管线中加一个回归测试，覆盖：
danger-full-access + approval never + edit/write in workspace

预期结果应为成功写入，而不是同级权限升级错误。

threads.title: 【bug】Compaction leaves dual session files (.jsonl + .jsonl.zstd) → entire subagent subsystem fails
threads.bodyText:
Environment:

DSH version: 0.1.1-rc.2
OS: macOS (arm64)
Session persistence: zstd compression backend (session.jsonl.zstd)

Summary:
After running the official /compact command on sessions, some sessions end up with BOTH
session.jsonl (uncompressed) AND session.jsonl.zstd (compressed) files. The backend is
configured for zstd compression; when it encounters a .jsonl file it fails hard with:
session artifact ".../session.jsonl" uses .jsonl, but this backend is configured for compression "zstd"

This single session-format inconsistency breaks the entire subagent subsystem:

subagent spawn → "subagent run failed"
send_message (resume) → fails
list_agents (enumerate) → fails with the same error

Reproduction steps:

Configure session storage with zstd compression.
Run the official /compact command on a session.
Attempt to spawn or resume any subagent → failure.

Observed facts:

Two affected sessions had both session.jsonl and session.jsonl.zstd; decompressed zstd
content was byte-identical to the .jsonl (verified via diff) — i.e. a redundant uncompressed copy
was left behind.
Health-check tooling reported "428 sessions healthy, 0 abnormal" while the subsystem was
completely down — file-format consistency is not covered by the health checks.

Impact:

One session's format inconsistency takes down ALL subagent operations (spawn/resume/list) —
single point of failure with uncontrolled blast radius.
No self-healing: the error message states the cause but offers no recovery path.
/compact side-effects are not validated by the read path.

Workaround (what we did):

Archive the redundant session.jsonl files (keeping the .zstd as the authoritative copy),
restart the DSH web process.

Suggested fixes:

/compact should atomically replace / clean up the uncompressed copy when producing the zstd file.
Backend read path should tolerate/ignore .jsonl files (or migrate them) instead of failing hard.
Session health checks should cover file-format consistency, not just event consistency.

threads.title: dsh web freezes (event loop blocked) after sending any message — Windows + Node 22
threads.bodyText:
Summary
After sending any message in the dsh web UI, the whole dsh web process becomes unresponsive: the port keeps listening but every HTTP request (including the page itself) times out. The process never recovers; it must be killed and restarted. This reproduces reliably on a fresh process with no third-party plugins.
Environment

OS: Windows 11 (zh-CN), x64
Node: v22.22.2
dsh: 0.1.1-rc.2 (latest on npm, installed globally via npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh)
Launch: dsh web (also reproduced with --no-open, --port 3081)
Network: direct access to api.deepseek.com works fine (fetch to /chat/completions returns 200 in ~850 ms from the same machine)

Steps to reproduce

Run dsh web (server starts fine, UI loads, balance/usage widgets render normally).
While idle or browsing, the server is stable — 60/60 consecutive HTTP probes return 200.
Send any message (e.g. 1+1等于几？ / hello) in a session.
Within ~6 seconds the server stops answering: curl http://127.0.0.1:3080 times out. Port 3080 is still LISTENING.

Expected behavior
The model replies normally (streamed), like the one successful run observed: 你好，请回复OK两个字 → model answered OK in ~5 s (this single success happened while a Clash TUN proxy was active; the same request hangs when TUN is absent).
Actual behavior

dsh web process stays alive (memory ~150–180 MB, no crash), but the event loop is blocked:

CPU usage is extremely low (0.1 s of CPU in an 8 s window → the process is waiting, not busy-looping).
No child processes are spawned/hanging (checked via WMI; the parent has no children).
Stdout/stderr are clean — no error logged.


Every request to any bound port (3080, 3081) times out until the process is killed.
Repro is independent of:

Plugins (reproduced with all plugins removed from the profile bundles),
Port (3080 and 3081 both),
Workspace directory (exists and is a local path),
Network (direct fetch to api.deepseek.com/chat/completions is 200 in <1 s).



Diagnostics collected

dsh web uses streaming (stream: true) fetch via dsh-llm-deepseek (fetchImpl = globalThis.fetch) — the transport itself is fine (verified separately).
The freeze happens after the message is submitted (server is healthy until then), i.e. somewhere in the agent-loop / tool-scheduling / session-persistence chain.
Session persistence is JSONL + zstd (dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, uses node:zlib zstd APIs).
dsh-subprocess-local / dsh-sandbox-local contain execSync / spawnSync / Atomics.wait usages; node-addon-landlock-run is also bundled (native module — npm i printed safe-delete cleanup warnings for its linux-arm64 variants on Windows).
Watching the frozen process: 13 threads, no children, minimal CPU → strongly suggests a blocked synchronous wait or a native-module deadlock rather than a busy loop.

Suspected area
Freeze occurs after the first LLM turn completes (or while the agent loop starts its first tool-scheduling step). Candidates:

Atomics.wait in dsh-subprocess-local/dsh-sandbox-local if a worker/subprocess never resolves;
node-addon-landlock-run native module behavior on Windows;
session persistence (zstd via node:zlib) during the first post-turn save.

Workaround
Kill the frozen dsh web process and restart. (I wrote a keep-alive watchdog that probes the port and auto-restarts on two consecutive failures.)
Additional notes

The very first LLM call can succeed while a TUN-mode proxy (Clash) is running and deepseek.com traffic is routed through the proxy group; once the proxy is gone (system direct), every subsequent message freezes the process. This hint may matter for the scheduler/subprocess path.
Please let me know if you need a process dump or logs; happy to run instrumented builds.

Thanks for looking into this — the tool is great, this bug makes it unusable on Windows at the moment.

threads.title: Bug: sandbox_permissions/justification break every tool call on Full access - sanitize no-op escalation requests
threads.bodyText:
Hi team,
Bug summary
Under danger-full-access (Full access), models that reflexively fill optional fields (observed with GPT-5.6) pass sandbox_permissions + justification on almost every pwsh/bash/write/edit call. Because the escalation check requires the request to be strictly wider than the call's effective mode, every such call fails with::
Error: sandbox escalation to "workspace-write" is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode
Error: invalid justification: expected a non-empty sentence
The tool schemas are registry-global (built once per composition) while the effective mode is per-session, so a session already at the widest mode is still offered the escalation fields - a Full access session cannot ever widen anything, so any filling of these fields is guaranteed to error.
Proposed fix (safety-neutral)
Treat "requests that cannot widen anything" as a no-op instead of an error:

approveEscalation - if the effective mode is already danger-full-access, return the standing mode without prompting (ignoring any target, including the reflexive first-enum-entry workspace-write, and any blank justification).
Same-mode request under a confined mode (requested == effective) is also a no-op: it widens nothing and never prompts.
Everything else stays verbatim: a different, wider request under read-only/workspace-write still goes through the strict widening check, the approval chain, and the closed fail texts; unknown/invalid effective modes still fail closed.

Changes span packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts plus the tool call sites (tool-bash, tool-pwsh, tool-fs), about 170 lines with tests (151 cases pass locally, including host/client typecheck).
A ready branch exists on my fork for review:

fork: praiseSun-nus/deepseek-harness
branch: sandbox-noop-escalation (1 commit, based on master @ b150a55)
commit: 56fac8d319 fix(sandbox): treat no-op sandbox escalation requests as ignorable

Happy to rewrite it as a PR the moment external PRs are accepted, or adapt the diff to your preferred form. Thanks for this great harness!

threads.title: Code Mode crashes on tool descriptions containing {{ }} — fix included
threads.bodyText:
A tool description containing a literal {{ }} (e.g. Composio's COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH, which documents escaping braces by doubling them) crashes Code Mode with malformed prompt variable reference "{{ }}" in section "tools:sdk".
The description reaches the model through the tools:sdk prompt section, which renderPrompt interpolates for {{variable}} references — an unescaped {{ throws as malformed instead of being treated as literal prose.
I have a fix ready: split {{ into { { at the existing sanitize point in both renderers (ts-types.ts's docLines, py-types.ts's describe()), the same place that already escapes */ and quotes/backslashes for the same reason. Added regression tests for both renderers (64/64 passing), and reproduced live against the Code preset with an MCP server mounted to confirm the crash is gone.
Full diff here since PRs aren't open yet: https://github.com/marcschraepler/deepseek-harness/tree/fix/code-mode-brace-escaping
Happy to open a proper PR once that's available, or paste the diff inline here if that's more useful.

macOS Bash sandbox fails with spawn sandbox-exec ENOENT
threads.bodyText:
OS: macOS
Node: v24.19.0
dsh: 0.1.0-rc.7
The Bash tool previously worked and could read/write files.
Now every Bash command fails with:
BashError: spawn sandbox-exec ENOENT
On the host macOS:

/usr/bin/sandbox-exec exists
which sandbox-exec returns /usr/bin/sandbox-exec
Node spawn("sandbox-exec") succeeds
Node spawn("/usr/bin/sandbox-exec") also succeeds

I also tested the dsh-sandbox-local Seatbelt implementation.
Changing the executable to /usr/bin/sandbox-exec still results in:
spawn /usr/bin/sandbox-exec ENOENT
This appears to be an issue with the Bash sandbox execution environment.

threads.title: build:lib fails — api-proxy.js imports exports removed from dsh-api-remotes and dsh-agent-presets
threads.bodyText:
What's happening
build:lib is failing with 7 MISSING_EXPORT errors from rolldown. lib/types/api-proxy.js imports several named exports from @deepseek-ai/dsh-api-remotes and @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets that no longer exist in those packages' src/index.ts. Wondering if this is a known issue or if a fix is already in flight.
Error
[MISSING_EXPORT] "resolveSessionPreset" is not exported by "../../preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts".
[MISSING_EXPORT] "ApiRemoteSessionNotFound" is not exported by "../../api/remotes/src/index.ts".
[MISSING_EXPORT] "ApiRemoteSubagentSessionOwnership" is not exported by "../../api/remotes/src/index.ts".
[MISSING_EXPORT] "apiRemoteSubagentOwnershipError" is not exported by "../../api/remotes/src/index.ts".
[MISSING_EXPORT] "createApiRemoteAgentResolver" is not exported by "../../api/remotes/src/index.ts".

(2 additional missing-export errors truncated in the original log for hasApiRemoteSubagentOwner / inspectApiRemoteSession.)
What I found digging in
Commit dcddaa1a — "refactor(client): replace legacy Host event carriers" (Aug 22) — removed the re-export block from packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts:
-export {
-  ApiRemoteSessionNotFound,
-  ApiRemoteSubagentSessionOwnership,
-  apiRemoteSubagentOwnershipError,
-  createApiRemoteAgentResolver,
-  hasApiRemoteSubagentOwner,
-  inspectApiRemoteSession,
-} from './agent-lookup.ts'
and replaced the module's public surface with a Cordis-plugin/Gateway event-stream architecture (inject, apply(ctx), remoteEventSource, RemoteEventQueue).
resolveSessionPreset is similarly not present in the current packages/preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts.
Looks like lib/types/api-proxy.js was never updated to match either change, so it's importing symbols that no longer exist on the public API of these packages.
Affected files

lib/types/api-proxy.js (consumer — broken imports)
packages/api/remotes/src/index.ts (exports removed here)
packages/preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts (exports removed here)

To reproduce
pnpm build:lib
Environment

Node.js v25.9.0
rolldown 1.1.1, tsdown 0.22.2
pnpm workspaces (macOS arm64)

Question
Is api-proxy.js expected to move to the new Gateway-based pattern, or is there a re-export planned for backward compatibility?

threads.title: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` fails with a JavaScript heap OOM during npm dependency resolution
threads.bodyText:
Summary
The install path recommended in the README — npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web — reliably crashes with FATAL ERROR: ... JavaScript heap out of memory before any dsh code runs. Installing the same package with pnpm succeeds in under a minute.
Environment









OS
Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200


Node.js
v24.19.0


npm
11.17.0


pnpm
11.24.0


System RAM
14.9 GB


Node default heap limit
2240 MB


dsh version
0.1.1-rc.2



Reproduction
The failure isolates cleanly to npm's resolver. No dsh code is executed in this repro:
mkdir repro && cd repro
echo '{"name":"t","version":"1.0.0","private":true}' > package.json
npm install @deepseek-ai/dsh --no-audit --no-fund
Result: crashes after 379 seconds with 0 packages installed.
<--- Last few GCs --->

[25308:...]   379176 ms: Mark-Compact 2027.6 (2056.2) -> 2019.2 (2072.7) MB, pooled: 0 MB, 298.20 / 0.00 ms  (average mu = 0.729, current mu = 0.811) allocation failure; scavenge might not succeed
[25308:...]   379642 ms: Mark-Compact (reduce) 2035.4 (2072.7) -> 2029.1 (2050.7) MB, pooled: 0 MB, 229.78 / 0.00 ms

FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory

The documented command fails the same way, just later — the process produces no output at all (dsh never gets to run) and dies after ~523 seconds:
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
Likely cause
npm emits large numbers of circular peer-dependency conflicts while resolving the tree. A sample from the install log:
npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
npm warn While resolving: @deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local@0.0.1-rc.1
npm warn Found: @deepseek-ai/dsh-paths@undefined
npm warn Could not resolve dependency:
npm warn peer @deepseek-ai/dsh-paths@"^0.0.1-rc.1" from @deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local@0.0.1-rc.1

npm warn ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency
npm warn While resolving: @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime@0.0.1-rc.1
npm warn Found: @deepseek-ai/dsh-type-meta@undefined
npm warn peer @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime@"^0.0.1-rc.1" from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-agent-preset@0.0.1-rc.1

The package graph is ~500 packages with peer dependencies referencing each other across dsh-* packages. npm's resolver appears to expand this combinatorially until it exhausts the heap.
This is consistent with the project being pnpm-native internally: the repo builds with pnpm, generated profiles contain pnpm-workspace.yaml, and dsh plugin forwards its arguments to pnpm. The npm/npx path appears not to be exercised in CI.
What I tried



Approach
Outcome




npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
OOM after ~523s, no output


npm install @deepseek-ai/dsh (isolated)
OOM after 379s, 0 packages installed


Pinning 0.1.0-rc.6
OOM (SIGABRT, exit 134)


Pinning 0.0.1-rc.1
OOM


NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144
Still unfinished after 400s; I terminated it, so this is inconclusive rather than a confirmed failure


npm install --legacy-peer-deps
Installs in 36s, but the tree is unusable (see below)


pnpm with auto-install-peers=true
Works — 504 resolved, 448 added in ~50s



--legacy-peer-deps installs quickly but produces a broken tree, because the peer dependencies are genuinely required at runtime:
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group'
imported from .../node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js

Working install
mkdir dsh-run && cd dsh-run
pnpm init
PNPM_CONFIG_AUTO_INSTALL_PEERS=true pnpm add @deepseek-ai/dsh
node node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js web
Boots correctly:
dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080

Note that auto-install-peers is required — without it, @deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group is missing and boot fails with the same ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND as the --legacy-peer-deps npm tree. Note also that in pnpm 11, pnpm config set auto-install-peers true is rejected for the global config and must be supplied via pnpm-workspace.yaml or the environment variable.
Suggested fixes

Flatten the peer-dependency graph between the internal dsh-* packages, or convert the circular peers to regular dependencies, so npm can resolve the tree.
Add an npm install to CI so this path stays exercised.
Update the README in the meantime — either document pnpm as the supported install path, or note the auto-install-peers requirement and the npm limitation, so users are not sent to a command that cannot complete.

threads.title: WSL2 下，zenity 对话框无法正常渲染
threads.bodyText:
描述
在 WSL (Ubuntu 24.04) 环境下运行 dsh web，点击「选择工作区」时，未弹出预期的目录选择对话框，而是弹出一个异常的 Linux 应用窗口，显示内容为：warn: COPY mode select xxxxxx。
复现步骤

在 WSL 环境下启动 pnpm dsh web
浏览器打开 Web UI
点击「选择工作区」按钮

期望行为
弹出系统原生的目录选择对话框（zenity/kdialog），用户可正常浏览并选择目录。
实际行为
弹出异常窗口，显示 warn: COPY mode select xxxxxx，无法正常选择目录。
环境信息

OS: WSL Ubuntu 24.04 (/home/wsl-ubuntu24/)
Node: v22+
Zenity: 4.0.1（已安装）
DISPLAY: :0
WAYLAND_DISPLAY: wayland-0
终端: Windows Terminal

根因分析
directory-picker-auto 插件在启动时进行后端解析（packages/host/directory-picker-auto/src/resolve.ts）：
resolveDirectoryPickerBackend():

zenity 已安装 → linuxChooser = true
DISPLAY=:0 → 有显示环境

threads.title: Python SDK cannot resume a persisted session after restart — session/prompt always creates and hits "id collision", existing conversations error on the next turn
threads.bodyText:
Summary
Python SDK (0.1.1rc1) + --profile sdk: after a harness restart, a turn on an existing session id fails with finish_reason: error and no output:
session "" already has a persisted log on disk that does not match this live session (id collision)
Root cause: the SDK JSON-RPC server always calls agents.create() (getOrCreateSession) and never resumes. The persistence layer's createCore rejects ids with an existing log ("load/resume it instead of creating"), and the SDK protocol (session/prompt) exposes no resume path. So any programmatic client loses all conversations on restart.
Reproduction
Run turn 1 with session_id="test-001", close the harness, start a new one (same dsh_home), run turn 2 with the same id:

turn 1 → works, final_response '记住了'
turn 2 → final_response '', finish_reason 'error' (turn/end: id collision, code UNKNOWN)
In-process continuation (same harness + same id) works; only cross-restart resume fails.

Expected
session/prompt should resume the persisted session when a log exists (the persistence layer already implements resume; the SDK just never calls it), or expose an explicit resume/open method, or at least return a recoverable error code.
Workaround
Client-side history replay: on first turn after restart, clear the stale log and feed the conversation history as content blocks. Restores context but loses harness-internal state (tool results, summaries).
Related: #466, #483, #387 (session persistence across restarts, web-host perspective). Reproduced 2026-08-29, SDK 0.1.1rc1 / dsh 0.1.1-rc.2.

threads.title: Programmatic agent creation silently no-ops: prompt variable "{{model}}" has no value, loop swallows the error (dsh 0.1.1-rc.2)
Bug：非扩权（non-widening）的 `sandbox_permissions` 请求未降级处理，而是直接抛出异常——导致在 `workspace-write` 和 `danger-full-access` 会话中，所有工具调用均失败。
threads.bodyText:
Environment

DSH version: @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.1-rc.2 (installed globally via npm, Windows)
OS: Windows 10/11, dsh web
Sandbox mode: workspace-write (session default); also reproduced with danger-full-access
Model: a GPT-family model through the harness adapter

Symptoms
The model attaches sandbox_permissions: "workspace-write" (sometimes with an empty justification) to every tool call — pwsh, bash, fs edits — even though the session's effective mode is already workspace-write. Every call then fails with:
Error: sandbox escalation to "workspace-write" is not strictly wider than this call's current "workspace-write" mode

Making things worse:

Under danger-full-access every escalation request throws, because WIDER_MODES has no key for it, so WIDER_MODES[effectiveMode] ?? [] is always an empty array → fail-closed. In this mode the error is 100% reproducible and nothing can execute at all.
Calls with an empty justification additionally throw Error: invalid justification: expected a non-empty sentence.
Disabling approvals does not help — the throw happens before the approval channel is ever consulted.

Net effect: the agent cannot run commands or write files at all. From the user's perspective this looks like a runtime sandbox fault, not a project issue.
Root cause
In packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/escalation.ts:

The tool schemas advertise the escalation surface globally (ESCALATION_TARGETS = ['workspace-write', 'danger-full-access']) whenever a confining executor is mounted — independent of the call's effective mode. The doc comment itself says "schemas are registry-global while the effective mode is per-call truth."
The tool description instructs the model to only set sandbox_permissions as a same-turn retry after a denial. In practice models do not follow this discipline reliably and set it speculatively on ordinary calls.
approveEscalation then throws on any request that is not strictly wider:

if (!(WIDER_MODES[effectiveMode] ?? []).includes(mode as SandboxMode)) {
  throw new Error(`sandbox escalation to "${mode}" is not strictly wider than this call's current "${effectiveMode}" mode`)
}
So a request that is equal to or narrower than the current mode — i.e. a call that needs no escalation at all — is turned into a hard error instead of being resolved as a no-op. This contradicts the function's own documented stance: "A non-widening request never prompts a human" (it doesn't prompt — it throws at everything).
Suggested fix
Treat a non-widening request as a no-op: grant the call the current effective mode instead of throwing. Genuine strictly-wider escalations keep the existing approval choreography untouched:
const { requestedMode: mode, effectiveMode, justification, subject } = request

// A non-widening request needs no escalation: execute under the current mode.
if (mode === effectiveMode) return effectiveMode
if (!(WIDER_MODES[effectiveMode] ?? []).includes(mode as SandboxMode)) {
  const LADDER: SandboxMode[] = ['read-only', 'workspace-write', 'danger-full-access']
  if (LADDER.includes(mode as SandboxMode) && LADDER.indexOf(mode as SandboxMode) < LADDER.indexOf(effectiveMode)) {
    return effectiveMode
  }
}
// ...original strictly-wider check + approval flow below
This is safe: the granted mode is exactly what the call would have run under had the model simply omitted sandbox_permissions — no privilege is widened, and the approval channel is only engaged for real widenings (verified: read-only → workspace-write and workspace-write → danger-full-access still route through approver.request).
Local workaround (verified)
Patching approveEscalation as above in node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox/lib/index.js (0.1.1-rc.2) fixes all four branches:



effective mode
requested
before
after




workspace-write
workspace-write
throws
executes under current mode


danger-full-access
workspace-write
throws
executes under current mode


read-only
workspace-write
approval flow
approval flow (unchanged)


workspace-write
danger-full-access
approval flow
approval flow (unchanged)



Checked against v0.1.2-alpha.1 source: escalation.ts is unchanged there, so the issue presumably still applies.
Secondary suggestion: consider filtering the schema enum per-session (only advertise targets strictly wider than the session's effective mode), which would stop models from forming invalid escalation requests in the first place.
Happy to provide more details or test a candidate fix. Thanks for the great project!

threads.title: Profile patch targeting a disabled row is a silent no-op (tool read/grep caps unreachable)
threads.bodyText:
Labels: bug config developer-experience
Summary
docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md:125 tells users a patch "can override rows from
earlier layers by id". For tool-fs / tool-fs-search that advice cannot work in the
Web composition, and it fails without an error or a warning: the agent keeps the old
behaviour and the user believes they configured something.
Why the override cannot land

packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml:332-336 disables the host rows:
- id: tool-fs
  disabled: true
- id: tool-fs-search
  disabled: true

Those tools are actually mounted inside the agent-preset composition — e.g.
packages/preset/agent-presets/presets/standard/agent.cordis.yml:56-62 — and patches
never cross an include boundary (stated explicitly in
packages/boot/app-boot/tests/config-reload.spec.ts:346-348).
So a profile-level - id: tool-fs config: matches only the already-disabled host row.
Nothing is configured; nothing reports it.

Reproduction

Web profile, standard preset. Add to ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml:
- id: tool-fs
  config:
    readMaxLineLength: 8000

Restart dsh web.
read a file containing a single line longer than 2000 chars.

Actual: output still ends with ... (line truncated to 2000 chars).
Expected: either the new cap is applied, or boot refuses/warns that the targeted row
is disabled by a later layer.
Note renderConfigDump already warns for patches that match no row
(packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:382-386); matching a disabled row produces no
signal at all, which is the gap.
Suggested fix (either, or both)

Diagnostic: warn when a patch's config target is disabled in the effective
composition, or is shadowed across an include boundary — same treatment as
"matched no row".
Reachable surface: move model-facing tool budgets (readMaxLineLength,
grepMaxLineBytes, readLimit, …) to a host-plane settings namespace so a deployment
can set them without editing shipped preset files. Today the only effective place is a
per-preset agent.cordis.yml, duplicated across standard / ptc / cordis, which a
user must discover from source.

Impact
Any user who reads the documented override advice and tries to tune tool behaviour gets a
silent no-op. This is the second-most-damaging failure class after a crash, because the
configuration looks applied.

threads.title: write: new-file publish uses a hard link, so it fails on exFAT (EISDIR) with no fallback
threads.bodyText:
Labels: bug filesystem windows
Summary
writeFileAtomic publishes a new file with a hard link. exFAT has no hard-link
support, so on any exFAT volume — the common case for removable drives and cross-OS
project shares — the write tool cannot create a single new file. Overwriting an existing
file works, which makes the failure look arbitrary.
Location
packages/fs/fs-local/src/fsio.ts

:546 staging dir .<name>.<pid>.<uuid>.tmpdir
:578-583 new-file path: await linkFile(tempPath, absolutePath) → catch → throwGuardedCreateFailure
:584-594 replace path: ReplaceFileW, with rename fallback → works on exFAT

Measured on this machine (workspace volume = exFAT, harness-home volume = NTFS)



operation
before
after proposed fix




write create new file (on the exFAT volume)
❌ EISDIR
✅


write overwrite a read file (on the exFAT volume)
✅
✅


edit existing file (on the exFAT volume)
✅
✅


raw fs.link (on the exFAT volume)
❌ EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, link '<…>.tmpdir\a.tmp' -> '<target>'
—


raw open(target,'wx') twice (on the exFAT volume)
2nd → EEXIST, first file untouched
—



The errno is itself a hazard: a hard-link-less volume answers link() as EISDIR
("illegal operation on a directory"), which reads like a path/type bug. In
a recorded runaway session the model concluded from it that its own temp filename was malformed and
burned many steps on that theory.
Why the obvious fallback is wrong
Falling back to plain rename breaks the contract of this code path: createIfAbsent
exists to guarantee no-replace, and rename over an existing target silently clobbers
it (measured: target content A → B).
Proposed patch (in use locally, 144 tests + tsc -b clean)
       try {
         await linkFile(tempPath, absolutePath)
       } catch (error: unknown) {
-        await throwGuardedCreateFailure(error, absolutePath, createIfAbsent.displayPath, inspectPublicationTarget)
+        // `link` is the only primitive that publishes staged bytes with no-replace
+        // semantics, but a hard-link-less volume (exFAT) rejects it outright, so a
+        // new file could not be created at all. Claim the name with an exclusive
+        // create, then rename the synced staging file over that own claim: `wx`
+        // still loses to a concurrent creator with EEXIST, so no other writer's
+        // bytes are clobbered. The weakened guarantee is visibility only — a reader
+        // may briefly observe the claimed-but-empty file instead of nothing.
+        if (!isHardLinkUnsupported(error)) {
+          await throwGuardedCreateFailure(error, absolutePath, createIfAbsent.displayPath, inspectPublicationTarget)
+        }
+        try {
+          const claim = await open(absolutePath, 'wx', 0o600)
+          await claim.close()
+        } catch (claimError: unknown) {
+          await throwGuardedCreateFailure(claimError, absolutePath, createIfAbsent.displayPath, inspectPublicationTarget)
+        }
+        try {
+          await rename(tempPath, absolutePath)
+        } catch (publishError: unknown) {
+          // The name is ours alone, having just won it exclusively, so dropping the
+          // empty claim cannot destroy another writer's file.
+          await rm(absolutePath, { force: true }).catch(() => {})
+          throw publishError
+        }
       }
with
function isHardLinkUnsupported(error: unknown): boolean {
  const code = (error as { code?: unknown }).code
  return code === 'EISDIR' || code === 'EPERM' || code === 'ENOTSUP' || code === 'EOPNOTSUPP' || code === 'EINVAL' || code === 'ENOSYS'
}
Semantics preserved: a real collision is still EEXIST → FS_NOT_OBSERVED; a directory
target is still FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE (the wx claim fails and the existing inspection
classifies it). Only regression vs the link path: a brand-new file may be observed empty
for an instant. EPERM/EACCES-style permission faults keep their old classification
because the failed claim falls back into throwGuardedCreateFailure.
Suggested tests

Mock linkFile to throw EISDIR; assert the file is created and contains the content.
Same, but the target already exists; assert rejection is FS_NOT_OBSERVED and the
existing bytes survive.
Same, but target is a directory; assert FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE.
CI tmpdirs are usually NTFS/ext4, so case 1 needs the mock — the existing suite already
uses internals.linkFile, so the seam exists.

threads.title: grep/read: line preview starts at column 0, hiding the match it just reported
threads.bodyText:
Labels: bug tools agent-reliability
Summary
grep reports Found N match and then renders at most GREP_MAX_LINE_BYTES = 2000
(packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/grep.ts:36) of the matched line, starting from the
beginning of the line (previewLine, search-core.ts:318-324), ending with
(line truncated). For a minified JSON file — which is one line — the match can be
past the window, so the tool simultaneously asserts the text exists and shows none of it.
read has the same shape: READ_MAX_LINE_LENGTH = 2000
(packages/fs/tool-fs/src/read-render.ts:11), marker ... (line truncated to 2000 chars).
read's offset/limit count lines, so paging cannot reach the match either: for a
one-line file, any offset yields the same truncated first line.
Consequence observed in production
In a recorded runaway session the agent ran grep '"glm-5' against an 8208-byte single-line
provider catalog whose first match sat at offset 2393 — 393 bytes past the window. The
tool said Found 1 match; the agent wrote "确认 catalog 里根本没有 glm-5.x", then built an
elaborate (false) theory that the settings validator never runs, and told the user their
working configuration "可能根本没真正工作过". The correct fix was already in its hands one
step earlier. That is a 17-step detour caused by output formatting.
Suggested fix

Show the match location, not the line head: start the preview window at/near the
match column, or print offset=<n> alongside the truncation marker so the reader knows
bytes were skipped before the match.
Consider a --around-match window of k bytes centred on the match.
Cheap documentation win: state in the tool description that the line preview is capped
and that a match may be outside the visible window, so Found N match is itself
evidence of presence.

Reproduction
printf '{"a":1,...pad to 2400 bytes...,"glm-5.1":{}}' > one-line.json   # one line, no \n
grep '"glm-5' one-line.json

Actual: Found 1 match + first 2000 bytes + (line truncated); "glm-5.1" not shown.

threads.title: Web profile ships with no clock: dsh-time-context is opt-in and only documented in the Schedule guide
threads.bodyText:
Labels: bug system-prompt model-reliability
Summary
@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context exists and is well designed, but
packages/context/time-context/README.md:12 says: "The plugin is opt-in: default
compositions leave it disabled, and the Schedule Web overlay mounts it." Its only
user-facing documentation is docs/user/guide/schedule.md (a reminder feature), so most
deployments never mount it — and a long-lived agent then has zero temporal anchor.
Evidence (a recorded runaway session, minimax-cn / MiniMax-M3)
Searched the whole recorded request header (6980-char system prompt + every tool schema),
both Current runtime context snapshots, and the DSH_* process environment: the string
2026 appears 0 times, and no date field exists anywhere. The agent had web results
dated 2026-08 while its own priors stopped earlier, and it resolved the conflict by
declaring the sources fake: "但当前是 2026 年初。这两个模型要么是未来的预测，要么是测试/误报内容".
Both models were real and 1-2 days old.
The vendor contract already expects this
MiniMax's shipped chat template has an explicit slot for it
(chat_template.jinja, build_system_message):
{#- Handle current_date -#}
{%- if system_message and system_message.current_date -%}
  {{- '\n' ~ 'Current date: ' + system_message.current_date }}
{%- endif -%}
{#- Handle current_location -#}
i.e. the model family is served on the assumption that the deployment supplies a date. A
harness that replaces the system message but never fills that slot removes the anchor the
vendor expects to be present.
Note on where the anchor belongs
time-context deliberately injects a durable per-step user message rather than system
text — its spec asserts request.system does not contain the reading. That is the
right call (a date in the prompt head breaks prefix-cache reuse and goes stale in a
long-running server), and it is why "put today's date in persona" is the wrong fix. The
gap is discovery, not design.
Suggested fix

Mount time-context by default in the Web profile (apps/cli/config/examples/schedule/cordis.yml:4-6
already shows the two-line insert), or default it on for any composition with a
long-lived interactive agent.
If it must stay opt-in: document it in the system-prompt / runtime-context docs and in
the Web profile guide, not only in the Schedule guide, and have the boot log mention
that no temporal context is mounted.
Consider a timezone fallback: with a browser zone the reading is already local
(Browser time zone for this request: Asia/Shanghai. Interpret otherwise-unqualified dates and times in this zone.) — that sentence alone would have prevented the incident.

Measured cost of defaulting it on
One reading is 246 chars ≈ 62 tokens per step (~4.4k tokens over a 72-step session).
refreshIntervalMs throttles it. In exchange, per-step elapsed time and an auditable
clock appear in the session log with source attribution
({ kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'time-context', form: 'snapshot', … }), validated by the
invariant companion.

threads.title: 磁盘目录带有特殊汉字会导致无法添加至工作区
threads.bodyText:
在 win32-dialog-bindings.ts 的 readUtf16(第 37-42 行):
let end = 0
while (end + 1 < bytes.length && bytes[end] !== 0) end += 2
return bytes.toString('utf16le', 0, end)
它把路径当 UTF-16LE 扫描终止符时,只检查每个字符的第一个字节,遇到任何"低字节为 0"的合法字符就会提前截断——而 销 的 Unicode 码点正好是 U+9500(UTF-16LE 首字节为 0x00)!你的目录叫"营销XXXXXX",路径读到这里就断了,正好停在"营"后面——和报错"…\XXXX析\营"一字不差。任何含 销、一(U+4E00)、万(U+4E07)这类字符的目录都会踩中。

threads.title: Bug: sandbox escalation error occurs when current mode is already danger-full-access
threads.bodyText:
# Bug: Incorrect Sandbox Escalation Error When Current Mode Is Already `danger-full-access`

## 问题描述

当前 DeepSeek Harness 会话已经处于：

```text
sandbox mode: danger-full-access
approval policy: never
但是调用 pwsh、write 或 edit 工具时，工具层仍然把请求识别为 Sandbox 权限升级，并报错：
Error: sandbox escalation to "danger-full-access" is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode

当请求改为：
sandbox_permissions: "workspace-write"

则报错：
Error: sandbox escalation to "workspace-write" is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode

这个问题会导致当前会话无法继续执行普通的文件写入、文件编辑和 shell 命令。
复现环境

项目：deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
DSH 版本：0.1.1-rc.2
操作系统：Windows
当前 Sandbox 模式：danger-full-access
当前 Approval 策略：never
受影响的工具：

pwsh
write
edit



复现步骤


启动一个 DeepSeek Harness 会话。


将 Sandbox 模式设置为：
danger-full-access



将 Approval 策略设置为：
never



在当前 workspace 中执行普通的文件编辑或命令，例如：
Get-Location
或者修改 workspace 内的文件。


工具调用携带以下任意参数：
sandbox_permissions: "danger-full-access"

或：
sandbox_permissions: "workspace-write"



调用失败，并出现：
Error: sandbox escalation to "danger-full-access" is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode

或：
Error: sandbox escalation to "workspace-write" is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode



期望行为
当当前 Sandbox 模式已经是 danger-full-access 时：

danger-full-access 不应被识别为权限升级。
workspace-write 不应被识别为权限升级 downgrade。
普通工具调用应直接在当前 danger-full-access 模式下执行。
如果当前权限已经足够，调用方应该可以省略 sandbox_permissions。
Approval 策略不应阻止已经处于 danger-full-access 模式下的普通操作。
工具层不应要求调用方再次申请与当前模式相同或更窄的权限。

实际行为
当前工具层似乎将所有带有 sandbox_permissions 的调用都当作权限升级请求，并要求：
requested sandbox mode must be strictly wider than current sandbox mode

因此出现以下错误判断：
current mode:   danger-full-access
requested mode: danger-full-access

被错误地当作无效升级。
同时：
current mode:   danger-full-access
requested mode: workspace-write

也被错误地送入 escalation 分支，而不是被识别为当前权限已足够，或者被明确识别为 downgrade 请求。
可能的根因
问题可能位于 Sandbox 工具调用参数处理、权限模式比较逻辑或 escalation dispatcher，具体可能包括：

没有区分普通调用和权限升级调用。
只要请求中存在 sandbox_permissions，就无条件走 escalation 流程。
没有处理当前模式已经是最高权限模式的情况。
没有定义 danger-full-access 与其他 Sandbox 模式之间的等级关系。
工具 schema 可能要求 sandbox_permissions，但运行时逻辑又要求在当前权限足够时不要传入该字段。
danger-full-access 没有被视为无需进一步升级、无需 provider/approval 的特殊模式。

根据 dsh-bash-sandbox 的文档，danger-full-access 是无约束模式，并且不会经过提供方的 Sandbox 限制。因此当前模式下不应再次请求同级或更高权限。
建议的权限判断逻辑
权限处理逻辑可以调整为：
if requestedMode is absent:
    execute using current mode

if requestedMode == currentMode:
    execute normally, not as escalation

if requestedMode is narrower than currentMode:
    execute using current mode, or reject explicitly as an invalid downgrade

if requestedMode is strictly wider than currentMode:
    require approval and perform escalation

也可以抽象为：
requestedMode = undefined

表示使用当前会话模式，而不是触发权限升级。
当：
currentMode === "danger-full-access"

时，应直接执行普通操作，不再进入 escalation 流程。
建议重点检查的代码位置
建议检查以下部分：

pwsh 工具参数 schema
write 工具参数 schema
edit 工具参数 schema
Sandbox mode 比较逻辑
escalation dispatcher
approval policy 与 Sandbox mode 的组合处理
escalation retry 逻辑
当前模式为 danger-full-access 时的特殊处理
是否允许在当前权限足够时省略 sandbox_permissions

与普通 Sandbox 拒绝的区别
这个问题不是普通的文件访问拒绝。
普通访问拒绝应类似：
sandbox: file access denied under workspace-write mode

而当前问题发生在权限升级判断阶段：
sandbox escalation ... is not strictly wider ...

也就是说，命令或文件操作本身可能根本没有执行，调用在 Sandbox 参数解析阶段就被拦截了。
Approval 策略的影响
该问题与 Approval 策略有关联，但根因不应归结为 Approval 策略。
在以下状态下都可能出现问题：
sandbox mode: danger-full-access
approval policy: never

此时权限已经是最高模式，工具调用不应该再依赖审批。
当 Approval 策略切换为 ask 后，如果请求的是从 workspace-write 升级到 danger-full-access，审批流程可以正常存在；但当当前模式已经是 danger-full-access 时，再次请求 danger-full-access 不应被视为升级。
影响
该问题会导致：

无法修改 workspace 内文件。
无法使用 edit 修复代码。
无法使用 write 创建文件。
无法使用 pwsh 运行构建和测试命令。
已授予 danger-full-access 的会话无法继续工作。
自动化开发任务会在工具调用层中断。
用户需要重启会话或重置运行时配置才能恢复。

期望修复结果
修复后，在以下环境中：
sandbox mode: danger-full-access
approval policy: never

执行：
Get-Location
以及 workspace 内的文件编辑操作时，应当直接执行成功，不再出现：
not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode

同时，从：
workspace-write

升级到：
danger-full-access

的真实权限升级请求仍应保留正常的审批流程。

loader: internal resolveSync mis-tagged v2 on Node 24.11 — client boot graph composes empty (fix ready)
threads.bodyText:
"# Bug: loader mis-tags the internal resolveSync on Node 24.11 — client boot graph composes empty (fix ready)

## Environment

- Node 24.11.1 (win32-x64)
- @cordisjs/plugin-loader 1.0.0-rc.5 (vendored at 56b3d4f7 in deepseek-harness; current main has the same code)

## Symptom

With dsh web on Node 24.11.1, the web UI fails with:


client-modules: HTML did not preload @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules/client.js


The server composes an empty client boot graph (__DSH_BOOT__ has zero entries and zero batches) because every client package's manifest resolution fails and is silently dropped.

## Root cause

ModuleLoader.fromInternal() in packages/loader/src/internal.ts tags the Node internal ESM loader by major version — Node ≥ 24 is tagged v2, whose resolveSync(parentURL, request) takes a request object. On Node 24.11.1 the private resolveSync still has the v1 argument order (specifier, parentURL, importAttributes) — the order earlier Node 24 releases had replaced — so the v2-shaped call passes the request object into the parent-URL position and Node's sync-hook resolution throws TypeError: e.indexOf is not a function.

Consumers (hmr, client-modules) classify any such resolution failure as "this name is not a client row" and skip it silently. The private signature has churned within the Node 24 line, so a major-version check cannot identify it.

Dependency-free repro:

sh
node --expose-internals -e "
const raw = require('internal/modules/esm/loader').getOrInitializeCascadedLoader();
try { raw.resolveSync('file:///', { specifier: 'node:path', attributes: {} }); console.log('v2-order OK'); }
catch (e) { console.log('v2-order throws:', e.message); }
try { console.log('v1-order OK:', raw.resolveSync('node:path', 'file:///', {}).url); }
catch (e) { console.log('v1-order throws:', e.message); }
"


On 24.11.1 the v2 order throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE (under a host that registers module.registerHooks, it surfaces as TypeError: e.indexOf is not a function); the v1 order resolves node:path.

## Fix

Detect the parameter order behaviorally instead of trusting the major version: probe one builtin resolution with the v1 order first (a v1 loader short-circuits any first argument that already parses as a URL, which would mask a v2 probe), then the v2 order, keep the version that returns a URL, and throw when neither matches.

A complete patch is on my fork branch — wuxuzhilu:fix/loader-probe-resolve-sync-version (vendor probe + vendor/README.md local-modification ledger entry + bilingual agent note). I tried to open a PR but this repository has pull requests disabled, so I am sharing the change here; happy to open a PR if that becomes possible, or feel free to take the change.

## Verification

- Focused suites (app-boot, webserver): 137 tests pass.
- Full pnpm run build passes.
- Live: the dsh web boot graph went from 0 entries to 46; the bootstrap batch serves 200 with the __ModuleLoader__.load registration the queue script waits for.
"

threads.title: Client diff card disappears for edit calls with redundant sandbox fields
threads.bodyText:
Summary
The Web UI does not render an inline diff for completed edit tool calls when the call contains redundant sandbox escalation fields, even though the persisted result contains valid diff metadata. The issue appears to be a client-side validation mismatch introduced by the raw-event card derivation refactor.
Environment

DSH version shown by the local Web UI: 0.1.2-alpha.1-cd5ef81
Current source branch includes commit 482b9e9e62 fix(sandbox): tolerate stale escalation fields
Browser: Edge 151 on Windows
Web UI: local dsh web

Reproduction

Run the Web UI with a full-access session.
Ask the agent to edit an existing file.
The generated call includes:

{
  "file_path": "dsh-page-demo.md",
  "old_string": "- 状态：已创建",
  "new_string": "- 状态：已编辑",
  "replace_all": false,
  "sandbox_permissions": "danger-full-access",
  "justification": ""
}

The operation succeeds, but the row shows only:

The file ... has been updated successfully.
Creating a new session reproduces the behavior.
Evidence
The raw session events contain the expected result metadata:

tool/call at seq 633: name = edit
tool/result at seq 634: data.meta.diffs is present and contains the applied hunk with oldText and newText.

The current client code in packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/models/diff-card-model.ts calls validEscalationFields(parsed.args) before reading settled block.meta. With sandbox_permissions: "danger-full-access" and blank justification, this returns false, so intendedDiff() returns null and the client never reaches appliedDiffs(block.meta). The UI therefore falls back to the model-facing success text.
Why this is inconsistent
The Runtime fix in 482b9e9e62 intentionally treats a target already covered by the standing policy as redundant metadata and allows it without approval or a non-empty justification. The Client validator still treats the same argument pair as malformed. This creates a cross-layer mismatch:

Runtime: valid redundant/inherited fields
Client card model: invalid fields, suppressing a valid diff card

Proposed minimal fix
For settled root calls, prefer trusted applied result metadata before validating call-time escalation presentation fields. For example, do not let validEscalationFields() block the settled path when block.meta.diffs is a valid non-empty diff array. Keep strict validation for running calls and keep validation for actual malformed/unknown cases.
A regression test should cover:
sandbox_permissions: 'danger-full-access',
justification: '',
meta: { diffs: DIFFS }
and assert that diffCardModel(settled(...)) returns the applied diff.
Additional question
Was 482b9e9e62 intended to be included in the next release? If so, should the Client raw-event card model be updated in the same change to honor the redundant-field semantics?

threads.title: [Bug] In-process subagents cannot write under inherited workspace-write because escalation fields remain exposed
threads.bodyText:
Summary
In DeepSeek Harness 0.1.1-rc.2 on Windows, in-process delegated subagents created through the built-in spawn / fork providers can read and analyze the inherited workspace, but cannot reliably call write, edit, or pwsh for ordinary workspace-local mutations.
The child correctly receives an inherited workspace-write sandbox override and the documented non-interactive approval=never policy. However, the model-facing tool surface still exposes the registry-global escalation arguments sandbox_permissions and justification. With GPT/Codex-compatible providers, ordinary calls are generated with those fields. The call is then rejected before the workspace-local operation executes.
This makes workspace-write + never children effectively read-only even though the inherited sandbox should permit workspace writes without approval.
Environment

OS: Windows
DSH: @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.1-rc.2
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh 0.1.1-rc.2
Web profile
Parent workspace: D:\CF15
Parent permission preset during reproduction: workspace-write + ask
Subagent tools: built-in subagent / subagent_fork
Providers used by those tools: in-process spawn / fork, not the optional product codex provider

Reproduction

Start a parent session with workspace-write + ask and workspace D:\CF15.
Verify the parent can create a file under D:\CF15\.tasks.
Create a child with the built-in subagent or subagent_fork tool.
Ask the child to read files under D:\CF15\Client\Assets.
Ask the same child to write D:\CF15\.tasks\subagent-write-probe.md.
The child can complete the reads, but its write is rejected before file mutation because its delegated approval policy is never and the call includes escalation fields.

We reproduced this with multiple existing children and a newly created foreground fork. A probe successfully enumerated 50 assets, and another child analyzed 92 assets, but neither could save its Markdown result.
Observed errors
Depending on the parent/child sandbox snapshot and generated arguments, the pre-execution errors include:
invalid justification: expected a non-empty sentence

and:
sandbox escalation to "danger-full-access" is not strictly wider than this call's current "danger-full-access" mode

A delegated child also reported:
The delegated session's write tool forces sandbox_permissions;
approval is disabled and the permission cannot be escalated,
so the write is rejected before execution.

Confirmed delegated-policy behavior
The documented child policy itself appears intentional. The installed implementation matches the repository design:
function captureDelegatedPolicyOverrides(parent) {
  return {
    sandboxMode: parent.ctx.get("sandboxPolicy")?.overrideOf(parent.session),
    approvalPolicy: parent.ctx.get("approval") === void 0 ? void 0 : "never"
  };
}
Installed location:
node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent/lib/index.js

The relevant official notes are:

https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-08-10-continuable-subagent-policy-inheritance.md
https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-08-15-product-subagent-noninteractive-permissions.md
https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/subsystems/permission-presets.md

Therefore, the issue is not that the child has approval=never. The issue is that unavailable escalation arguments remain visible/generated even though the child should perform ordinary writes inside its inherited sandbox without escalation.
Failure chain
parent explicit workspace-write sandbox override
→ copied into the in-process child at delegation time
→ child approval policy pinned to never
→ registry-global tool schema still exposes escalation arguments
→ model generates sandbox_permissions / justification for an ordinary call
→ escalation validation runs before the workspace-local operation
→ child cannot write

Expected behavior
For an in-process child with workspace-write + never:

Ordinary writes under the inherited workspace should execute without approval.
The model-facing schema should expose no escalation fields when the effective approval policy is never; or the bridge should otherwise omit unavailable optional fields.
True out-of-workspace elevation must remain denied.

A session-aware model-facing schema would ideally behave as follows:



Effective policy
Escalation fields visible to the model




read-only + ask
workspace-write, danger-full-access


workspace-write + ask
danger-full-access only


danger-full-access + ask
none


any sandbox + never
none



Impact
This prevents delegated subagents from independently completing:

code changes and patches;
test creation;
documentation writes;
contract/result files;
work logs;
build/test commands that need writable cache or temporary output.

The only current workaround in our workflow is:
child performs read-only analysis
→ child returns the complete patch/document in chat
→ parent mechanically writes it

That weakens role isolation, auditability, independent branch ownership, and multi-agent development workflows.
Related report and community workarounds

Related Discussion #468: #468
Community plugin with session-aware schema projection: https://github.com/HakureiMonika/dsh-sandbox-escalation-fix
Community compatibility plugin that strips only provably redundant escalation arguments: https://github.com/YaoaY/dsh-gpt-compat

No third-party compatibility plugin was installed during this reproduction.
Questions

Is workspace-write + never an officially supported effective policy for in-process spawn / fork children, with workspace-local writes expected to succeed?
Should escalation fields be removed from the child-visible tool schema whenever the effective approval policy is never?
Is the registry-global escalation schema planned to become session-aware / exact-scope projected?
Is there a core fix version or milestone associated with Discussion #468?
Is there a supported profile-level workaround that preserves workspace-write + never without installing a third-party compatibility plugin?


中文摘要
当前内置 spawn/fork 子 Agent 会继承父会话显式的 workspace-write，同时按官方设计固定为 approval=never。它本应无需审批即可写入父工作区，但工具 Schema 仍暴露 sandbox_permissions 和 justification，GPT/Codex 兼容模型在普通写操作中生成这些字段，导致执行器先进入升级校验并拒绝调用。因此子 Agent 可以只读调查，却不能把结果写回工作区。
