threads.title: source launch (`pnpm dsh`): first tool call crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')" — @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools loads twice (src + lib) and TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER Symbol splits
threads.bodyText:
Summary
The documented run-from-source vector breaks on first tool invocation. pnpm dsh
launches apps/cli/src/bin.ts through tsx, but the profile/bundle layer resolves
@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools and @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop from Node's default
resolution (lib/index.js) while the application-side src/*.ts graph resolves
the same bare specifier through tsx's tsconfig paths projection
(src/index.ts). Both copies load in the same process.
TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER is a non-global Symbol()
(packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:463) used as the registry key for the tool
runtime scheduler. With two module instances there are two distinct Symbols, so
the consumer's lookup returns undefined and the first tool call throws. The
failure surfaces only as:
dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')

which does not reveal a duplicate module instance.
This breaks both documented surfaces: pnpm dsh <profile> "<task>" and
pnpm dsh web (README.md:38, and the "Web browser automation" recipe in
AGENTS.md:117). The built artifact vector (node apps/cli/lib/bin.js ...) is
unaffected because tsdown inlines the dependency graph into a single instance,
which is why the two vectors diverge.
Environment

OS: Ubuntu, Linux x64
Node: v22.23.2 (within the declared engines range ^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0)
tsx: 4.22.4
pnpm workspace install, pnpm run build completed (all lib/ artifacts present)
dsh 0.1.6-alpha.2, commit ddefc45fbc (master, clean tree)

Steps to reproduce
Requires a valid DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. --profile headless is used because it runs
one task to completion and needs no GUI or port.
git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git
cd deepseek-harness
pnpm install
pnpm run build

# A — source launch (documented): crashes
pnpm dsh --profile headless "Read package.json and report its name field. Use the read tool."

# B — built launch (control): completes normally
node apps/cli/lib/bin.js --profile headless "Read package.json and report its name field. Use the read tool."
Observed:
A) dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
   exit=1

B) The `name` field is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-root`.
   exit=0

The same failure reproduces on the Web surface: pnpm dsh web, then a blank
session and any tool call.
Complete stack trace
The CLI suppresses the underlying stack and reports only the fail-loud summary
line:
dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')

The throwing expression is:
packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:170
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)
siblings tool-calls.ts:153-154 and :174 index the same Symbol for
finalize / finish / dispatch. ctx.tools is a valid ToolRuntime; only the
Symbol-keyed scheduler slot is missing, which is the signature of a Symbol
identity mismatch rather than a missing registration.
Evidence
1. Both module instances load in one process
Traced with module.registerHooks during a failing run (Node 22.23+):
LOAD .../packages/core/tools/lib/index.js        <- registry (ToolRuntime) created here
LOAD .../packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js
LOAD .../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts        <- consumer resolves against this instance
.../packages/core/tools/src/{json-schema,ptc,ts-types,py-types,schema,testing}.ts

packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:486 mounts @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools and
:498 mounts @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop as bare plugin names, so both modules
enter through the loader rather than through the application's import graph.
Symbol identity under the same vector:
import.meta.resolve('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools')
  -> packages/core/tools/src/index.ts

createRequire(apps/cli/src/bin.ts)('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools')
  -> packages/core/tools/lib/index.js

TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER identity (src instance vs lib instance): false

2. The anchor decides which copy wins
Instrumenting the resolver in the failing run shows the split is decided by the
importing anchor, not by the specifier:
LIB  spec=@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop  parent=apps/cli/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-base/package.json
LIB  spec=@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools       parent=node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions/package.json
SRC  spec=@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools       parent=packages/core/agent-loop/lib/index.js
SRC  spec=@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools       parent=packages/fs/tool-fs/src/read.ts
SRC  spec=@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools       parent=packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts
SRC  spec=@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools       parent=packages/goal/tool-goal/src/index.ts
   ...  (every src/*.ts consumer maps to src)

apps/cli/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-base is a symlink to
packages/bundle/base, so bundle-layer packages are resolved from a package.json
anchor and take Node's default resolution, while the application's own .ts
sources are subject to tsx's paths projection. The two routes never meet.
3. Minimal reproduction without the repository (tsx semantics)
A three-file fixture reproduces the resolution split on its own. Package
@t/pkg-b exposes exports: { ".": "./lib/index.js" } with distinct src and
lib copies; the root tsconfig maps @t/pkg-b -> ./pkgB/src/index.ts.
D: import { WHO } from "@t/pkg-b"   (from a src-side .mjs)
   -> B_SRC        # tsx applies the tsconfig paths projection

C: createRequire('<...>/node_modules/@t/pkg-b/package.json').resolve('@t/pkg-b')
   -> <...>/pkgB/lib/index.js
   -> B_LIB        # absolute path, no bare specifier left for tsx to remap

The mechanism: tsx's paths projection applies to a bare specifier it is
asked to resolve. Once the profile/bundle layer turns a package name into an
absolute file path (via its own CJS-anchored lookup), there is no bare specifier
left to remap, so the default resolution result wins. The source-launch contract
(2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm)
notes that tsx "applies the paths map unconditionally" once the deleted runtime
rule was removed, but that projection evidently does not reach this route.
Impact

Every documented source-launch surface is broken at first tool call:
TUI, pnpm dsh web (README.md:38, AGENTS.md:117), and --profile headless.
The dsh-source-launch-smoke gate
(apps/cli/tests/source-launch.compat.spec.ts) is a keyless piped-stdio
launch asserting a non-zero-exit TTY refusal. It never issues a tool call, so
this regression passes CI.
The error text gives no signal that the cause is a duplicated module instance.
Any other package that uses a non-global Symbol() as a service/registry key
across the same boundary is exposed to the same class of failure.

Suggested fix direction
Reconcile the two resolution routes in the profile layer so that a source launch
resolves one instance. packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts
already maintains both routes — internalModules() pulls
internal/modules/esm/loader and internal/modules/cjs/loader, and
nativePackageDir() uses createRequire(parent).resolve.paths(name). Under
pnpm dsh only the ESM route can produce a module instance consistent with the
application's tsx-projected graph; the CJS-anchored route yields the lib/
instance and silently reintroduces the second copy.
Concretely, the ESM route needs to agree with the entry tsx would select for the
same specifier (or the two routes' results need to be reconciled and a
disagreement surfaced loudly rather than resolved in favor of one), so the loaded
module set stays single-instance under source launch. Whatever the shape, the
invariant worth asserting is that the same package resolves to exactly one
module instance per process in both launch modes.
Two things that should not be the fix:

Pointing packages/core/tools/package.json exports["."].default at
./src/index.ts. That makes the packaged lib/bin.js load TypeScript under
plain Node and breaks the shipped artifact path, which currently works.
Widening the smoke gate only. The gate should gain a real tool-call assertion
(the actual regressed behavior), but the resolution split itself needs fixing.

What I did not verify

I did not run the node-compat matrix (pnpm run check:node-compat) or the
dsh-source-launch-smoke gate; verification was on Node v22.23.2 only.
I did not bisect to the commit that introduced the split. The
source-launch note
records that the loader's runtime rule "mapping a workspace import only for
declared runtime dependencies" was deleted together with
scripts/tspath-loader.ts and apps/cli/src/tsconfig-paths-loader.ts, and
states that the projected paths map applies unconditionally. Whether the
split predates that removal or dates from it was not established.
I did not verify the tested behavior on the Web surface end to end (no browser
session); the Web failure is inferred from the headless reproduction of the
same launch vector.
The mechanism attribution in "Evidence 2" is from traced resolve hooks. I did
not step through resolver.ts route selection with a debugger, so the exact
branch that selects the CJS-anchored result is inferred rather than observed.

repro.sh
Minimal repro — tsx paths projection vs. package.json-anchored resolution
What this demonstrates
Under node --import tsx/esm, a package name imported as a bare specifier
is resolved through tsx's tsconfig paths projection, while the same package
name resolved to an absolute path from a package.json anchor (the
profile/bundle resolution route) falls back to Node's default resolution and
lands on a different file. Both load in one process.
This is the mechanism behind the pnpm dsh first-tool-call crash, where
TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER (Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler'), a
non-global Symbol used as a registry key) exists twice, so the consumer's lookup
returns undefined and reports only
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare').
Run
From any directory that has node_modules/tsx in its ancestry (e.g. a
deepseek-harness checkout):
sh repro.sh
Or point it at a tsx install explicitly:
sh repro.sh /path/to/checkout      # uses /path/to/checkout/node_modules/tsx
The script creates a throwaway fixture via mktemp -d and removes it on exit.
Expected output
node: v22.23.2
tsx:  4.22.4

D src-consumer (bare specifier)   -> B_SRC

C anchor-consumer resolved to     -> ./pkg-b/lib/index.js
C anchor-consumer (absolute path) -> B_LIB

via bare (tsx paths projection)   -> B_SRC
via absolute anchor               -> B_LIB
single module instance            -> false

Verified on Node v22.23.2 with tsx 4.22.4 and tsx 4.23.13 (same result on both).
Fixture
repro.sh generates the whole fixture; it is reproduced here for reference. One
package @t/pkg-b with intentionally divergent src/ and lib/ copies:
pkg-b/package.json
{
  "name": "@t/pkg-b",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "exports": { ".": "./lib/index.js" }
}
pkg-b/lib/index.js
export const WHO = "B_LIB"
pkg-b/src/index.ts
export const WHO = "B_SRC"
tsconfig.json — maps the bare name to the source copy:
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": { "@t/pkg-b": ["./pkg-b/src/index.ts"] }
  }
}
node_modules/@t/pkg-b — symlink to ./pkg-b (the equivalent of pnpm's
workspace link).
Three consumers:
src-consumer.mjs — mirrors an application-side .ts file importing the bare name:
import { WHO } from '@t/pkg-b'
console.log('D src-consumer (bare specifier)   ->', WHO)
anchor-consumer.mjs — mirrors the profile/bundle route: resolve from a
package.json anchor, then import the absolute path:
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
const require = createRequire(new URL('./node_modules/@t/pkg-b/package.json', import.meta.url))
const resolved = require.resolve('@t/pkg-b')
console.log('C anchor-consumer resolved to     ->', resolved.replace(process.cwd(), '.'))
const mod = await import(resolved)
console.log('C anchor-consumer (absolute path) ->', mod.WHO)
identity.mjs — both routes in one process, so the duplicate module instance is
observable directly:
import { WHO as viaBare } from '@t/pkg-b'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
const absolute = createRequire(new URL('./node_modules/@t/pkg-b/package.json', import.meta.url))
  .resolve('@t/pkg-b')
const viaAnchor = (await import(absolute)).WHO
console.log('via bare (tsx paths projection)   ->', viaBare)
console.log('via absolute anchor               ->', viaAnchor)
console.log('single module instance            ->', viaBare === viaAnchor)
Mapping to the harness



fixture
harness




pkg-b with exports -> lib/index.js
packages/core/tools (exports["."] -> ./lib/index.js)


pkg-b/src/index.ts

threads.title: [Bug] workspace-write Seatbelt profile blocks new PTYs (posix_openpt: EPERM) — nested sessions and PTY-based tools fail
threads.bodyText:
Summary
Under the default workspace-write sandbox policy on macOS, a command executed by the harness cannot allocate a new PTY. posix_openpt() needs a read-write open of /dev/ptmx, and the Seatbelt profile built in packages/sandbox/sandbox-local grants file writes only to /dev/null plus the writable roots, so that open is denied and node-pty reports posix_openpt failed: Operation not permitted.
I could not capture the sandbox-exec wrapper argv directly (see What I did not verify), so the attribution to that profile is an inference from the source plus the matching denial set below — not an observed command line.
Environment

macOS, Darwin 25.5.0, arm64
@deepseek-ai/dsh-* 0.1.5-rc.2
sandbox policy: workspace-write
backend mounted: @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local (mounted by @deepseek-ai/dsh-base/cordis.patch.yml)

Reproduction
Run inside any command the harness executes (for example the persistent bash tool). No extra setup:
node -e "require('fs').openSync('/dev/ptmx','r+')"   # EPERM: operation not permitted
node -e "require('fs').openSync('/dev/ptmx','r')"    # OK — read-only is allowed
node -e "require('node-pty').spawn('/bin/sh',['-c','true'],{name:'xterm-color'})"
#   -> Error: posix_openpt failed: Operation not permitted   (3/3 attempts)
touch ~/probe                                        # EPERM — expected under the policy, shown for contrast
Control: with confinement removed (the documented danger-full-access escape hatch, or running the same harness outside any sandbox), all of the above succeed and PTY-dependent work completes.
Impact
Any command that allocates a PTY fails, for example:

running a nested dsh / agent harness from inside a session,
tmux, expect, script, ssh -t,
test suites that spawn a PTY.

Concrete case in a downstream wrapper: its doctor integration probe spawns a child agent whose persistent shell needs a PTY. The probe dies with Child shell did not start in its worktree, while the real error returned in the tool result is the posix_openpt failed line above. The same probe passes when the harness runs unconfined.
Relevant code
In packages/sandbox/sandbox-local, seatbeltProfileArgs() produces:
(version 1)(allow default)(deny file-write*)
(allow file-write* (literal "/dev/null"))
(allow file-write* (subpath <workspace>) (subpath /tmp) (subpath <tmpdir>))

/dev/ptmx is not among the grants, and posix_openpt() opens it O_RDWR.
Suggested direction

If PTY allocation is meant to work under workspace-write: add (allow file-write* (literal "/dev/ptmx")) (or (allow pseudo-tty)) next to the existing /dev/null grant. This does not widen path writes; the file-write policy stays as it is.
If the current behavior is intended: one line under "Known Limitations and Deferred Work" in sandbox-local (or in bash-sandbox, which already documents "Confinement covers file effects only") would save the next person this debugging session.

Secondary observation
/bin/ps cannot be executed under the confinement (spawnSync /bin/ps EPERM, bash exit 126); it is a setuid root binary. This may be the same rule or a related one — flagging it mainly because it means a confined command cannot inspect the process tree at all.
What I did not verify

I did not capture the actual sandbox-exec -p ... wrapper argv, and /bin/ps cannot run inside the confinement, so the profile attribution rests on the source above plus the matching denial set (HOME writes denied; /tmp and workspace writes allowed; /dev/null allowed; /dev/ptmx denied).
Non-macOS backends were not tested (bwrap / Landlock paths may differ).


Reported with AI assistance; every command above is reproducible, and the inference in "What I did not verify" is flagged as unverified.

threads.title: [0.1.6-alpha.2] 含 jsdom 的插件树无法启动：CJS 解析路由在 require("punycode/") 处崩溃（同 profile 在 alpha.1 正常）
threads.bodyText:
TL;DR (EN) — On 0.1.6-alpha.2 a profile whose plugin tree pulls in jsdom (→ whatwg-url → tr46 → require("punycode/")) cannot boot: the plugin tree aborts inside ResolutionRouter.routeScoped, the host exits, and launchd restarts it forever. The identical profile boots and runs for days on 0.1.6-alpha.1 / 0.1.5-rc.1. Locally adding the ?? [] guard that the same file already uses elsewhere moves the failure one step further, to Cannot find module 'punycode/' inside resolveRoutedCjs.
环境









DSH
0.1.6-alpha.2（npm alpha tag 直装，失败）／对照 0.1.6-alpha.1（同机同 profile，正常）


OS / Node
macOS 27.0 (arm64) / Node v22.22.3


profile
web，18 个第三方 bundle



其中 4 个插件都依赖 jsdom（所以这不是很偏门的组合）：



插件
版本
jsdom




dsh-web-search-pro
0.1.12-alpha.5
^29.0.0 ← 第一个炸的 entry


dshmarket
1.46.1
^29.1.1


dsh-univer-office
0.2.14
^26.1.0


@a9i5k4/dsh-literature
0.3.6
^24.1.3



依赖链版本：jsdom 29.1.1 → whatwg-url 16.0.1 → tr46 6.0.0 → require("punycode/")。
punycode@2.3.1 已装在 profile 自己的 node_modules 里（这一步很关键，见第二层）。
复现

任一 profile 装上会拉 jsdom 的插件（例如 dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-web-search-pro）；
用 0.1.6-alpha.2 启动该 profile；
现象：插件树加载失败 → 宿主退出 → KeepAlive 拉起 → 无限循环。

一个容易误判的点：循环期间服务偶尔能回 401/200（webserver 早于插件树绑定），所以「HTTP 通」不能当健康证据；真正的判据是 launchctl print 的 runs 计数在持续增长（本次从 1 涨到 24+）。
第一层错误
dsh: plugin tree failed to load: failed to apply loader entry include (cordis:include):
failed to import loader entry web-search-pro (dsh-web-search-pro):
createRequire.resolve.paths is not a function or its return value is not iterable
TypeError: createRequire.resolve.paths is not a function or its return value is not iterable
    at ResolutionRouter.routeScoped (…/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1327:58)
    at ResolutionRouter.routePath (…:1447:15)
    at Function.wrappedFilename [as _resolveFilename] (…:1747:24)
    at Module.require (node:internal/modules/helpers:147:16)
    at Object.<anonymous> (…/profiles/web/node_modules/tr46/index.js:3:18)

tr46/index.js 第 3 行是 require("punycode/")。Node 的 require.resolve.paths("punycode") 对核心模块名返回 null，而 routeScoped 直接
for (const searchPath of createRequire(parent).resolve.paths(name)) {
→ TypeError: … is not iterable。
值得注意的是：同一个文件里官方自己在另一处已经写了这个守卫（alpha.2 第 882 行：createRequire(anchor).resolve.paths(packageName) ?? []），但另外三处漏了——alpha.2 的第 1189 / 1327 / 1927 行（alpha.1 对应 1129 / 1267 / 1867）。
第二层错误（补上守卫之后暴露出来的）
本地把那三处补成 ?? [] 之后，崩溃点前移到路由本身：
failed to import loader entry web-search-pro (dsh-web-search-pro):
Cannot find module 'punycode/'
Require stack:
- …/profiles/web/node_modules/tr46/index.js
- …/profiles/web/node_modules/whatwg-url/lib/url-state-machine.js
- …/profiles/web/node_modules/whatwg-url/index.js
- …/profiles/web/node_modules/jsdom/lib/api.js
    at resolveRoutedCjs (…/@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js:1705:28)
    at Function.wrappedFilename [as _resolveFilename] (…:1785:16)

也就是说：这个 punycode/（带尾斜杠的裸标识符）被路由接管后没能解析成功，而原生解析本应成功——…/profiles/web/node_modules/punycode/ 确实存在（2.3.1）。
为什么判断这是 alpha.2 的回归

同一 profile、同一批插件、同一 Node 版本：alpha.1 连续跑了 3 天无异常，换 alpha.2 后 60 秒内进入崩溃循环（首次拉起时还能 serve，随后即死）。
那三处未守卫的 resolve.paths 调用在 alpha.1 里也存在，说明变化点不是这行代码本身，而是这条 require 在 alpha.2 走到了这段路由。两版 dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js 有 563 行差异（alpha.2 新增了 dsh-lazy-require、dsh-atomic-write、dsh-plugin-manager、dsh-hmr 等包，并移除了 cordis-plugin-hmr）。

建议

补守卫：createRequire(parent).resolve.paths(name) → … ?? []（1189 / 1327 / 1927 三处，与 882 行保持一致）。核心模块没有搜索路径，空迭代即回落到原生解析，语义正确。
路由回退：resolveRoutedCjs 对「核心模块名」或「带尾斜杠的裸标识符」应直接交回原生解析；或在路由目标不存在时回退到原生解析，而不是抛 Cannot find module。
可选：插件树加载失败时给出可判定的错误信号（错误码或 --json 字段），便于自动回滚——本次是靠 runs 计数才及时发现的。

附：如何确认是不是同一个问题
# 崩溃循环的判据（HTTP 不可信）
launchctl print gui/$UID/com.dongyue.dsh-web | grep -E "runs|last exit code"

# 判定性错误串
grep -m1 "createRequire.resolve.paths is not a function" ~/.dsh/web.err.log
grep -m1 "failed to import loader entry" ~/.dsh/web.err.log
当前已回滚到 0.1.6-alpha.1（vendor 整树回滚 + 服务恢复，三个 profile 均正常）。alpha.2 里那些新特性（插件管理页、HMR、文件改动卡片）很想用，等这条修好再上。

threads.title: [BUG]: Host-backed settings (Settings > Models/General) are impossible behind any reverse proxy — isLoopback gate tests the hostname string only, with no deployment override
threads.bodyText:
Summary
DSH gates host-backed settings (Settings > Models, Settings > General — i.e. everything that persists to $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml / .credentials.yaml) on the browser page's origin being loopback. The check is a pure string test on location.hostname, so any deployment that serves the web UI through a reverse proxy — even one that terminates on the same machine and resolves to 127.0.0.1 — permanently loses the ability to edit providers/keys from the browser. There is no server-side or config-file override to restore it.
This makes the gate effectively "loopback-origin-only", which excludes a common, legitimate class of deployments: containerized setups (Docker/DDEV/Dev Containers), SSH-tunnel setups where the printed loopback URL belongs to the remote host, and LAN deployments that already pass the server-side Host/Origin trust fence via --trusted-host.
Environment

dsh: 0.1.5-rc.1 (installed globally, web mode: dsh web --port 3080 --no-open --trusted-host …)
OS (host): macOS 26.6.2 arm64; OS (container): Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 (Docker/podman via DDEV)
Node: v22.23.2
Deployment: dsh web inside a container, bound to 127.0.0.1:3080, relayed to 0.0.0.0:3081 (socat), published to the host, and reverse-proxied by the DDEV router at https://<project>.ddev.site:8144 with a trusted TLS cert. The proxy forwards Host unchanged; the server-side Host/Origin fence accepts it via --trusted-host.

Reproduction

Serve dsh web behind any proxy with a non-loopback hostname that the server trust fence accepts (here: https://xxxx.ddev.site:8144, which resolves to 127.0.0.1).
Open the UI in a browser, authenticate with the token.
Open Settings → Models.

Actual: "Loading the provider directory failed: settings are unavailable in this browser". Every settings scope is silently in memory mode; writes are refused.
Expected: host-backed settings work — the deployment already authorized this authority on the server side via --trusted-host, and the page is the operator's own browser on the same machine.
Opening the same server directly at http://127.0.0.1:<port> in the same browser works, which isolates the cause to the origin check alone.
Root cause (from the installed source)
The decision is made client-side in @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings:
const persistence = ctx.remote.$host.isLoopback ? "host" : "memory";
isLoopback comes from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection:
isLoopback: transport?.ownsHost === true || pageLocation === void 0 || isLoopbackHostname(pageLocation.hostname)

function isLoopbackHostname(hostname) {
    if (hostname === "localhost" || hostname === "[::1]") return true;
    const parts = hostname.split(".");
    return parts.length === 4 && parts[0] === "127" && parts.every(
        (part) => /^\d{1,3}$/.test(part) && Number(part) <= 255);
}
Consumers of the same flag (all degrade on non-loopback origins):

dsh-client-ui-settings — describe mirror + all scope persistence (memory = read/write refused)
dsh-client-ui-settings-general — SettingsDocumentStore is only constructed when isLoopback
dsh-client-ui-settings-models — Models page fails with the error above

Notes:

I understand why the check is a string test: a browser page cannot verify where a name resolves, and "hostname literally reads loopback" is a cheap proxy for "the operator's own browser" that DNS rebinding cannot forge. That rationale is sound for the default.
The only escape hatch, __DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost, is reserved for shells that assemble their own transport (the worker preview); a served page behind a proxy cannot use it, and per the type docs "served pages never carry the global at all".
The server-side fence (isTrustedApiRequest) already has the right concept — explicit, deployment-declared trusted authorities (--trusted-host, exact host:port or port-less) — but the settings gate never consults it.

Impact

In container/proxy deployments, provider and key management is only possible by editing $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml / .credentials.yaml by hand (or docker cp), losing the Models UI workflow the docs recommend.
The failure mode is silent and confusing: the UI shows a generic "settings are unavailable in this browser" with no hint that the origin is the reason.

Feature request
Provide a deployment-level way to mark a non-loopback authority as "operator-equivalent" for the settings gate. Options, in order of preference:

Derive the gate from the existing trust fence: if the page's origin matches a --trusted-host authority, treat isLoopback as true for settings persistence. This reuses an existing, explicit, admin-controlled concept — no new surface.
A dedicated web-app config field (e.g. trustedSettingsHosts: ["myhost.example:8144"]) consumed the same way.
At minimum, a UX fix: make the "settings are unavailable in this browser" message state the cause ("host-backed settings require a loopback origin (localhost / 127.x.x.x); open the UI via http://localhost:") so users can self-recover.

Security considerations: option 1/2 still requires the server-side Host/Origin fence and token auth on every request (unchanged), and the authority must be explicitly declared by the deployment — the same trust decision the fence already makes for reachability. If the concern is a proxy that terminates TLS elsewhere, that's already out of trust scope today (the fence accepts declared authorities).
Workarounds tried

--trusted-host <host>:8144 — accepted by the /api fence, but does not affect the settings gate (it's client-side).
Opening https://…ddev.site:8144 from a host where it resolves to 127.0.0.1 — no effect; the check is on the hostname string.
Routing http://localhost:<router-port> through the proxy — fails earlier (no Host-based route match for localhost).


Two notes before you post it:

Repo/labels: I don't know dsh's actual issue templates or whether the repo is public — paste the body as-is and adapt the title to their template (this one fits "Bug / Feature request" hybrid; if forced to pick one, feature request is the more accurate frame, since the behavior is documented-by-design and the ask is an override).
I kept it to one issue. If you'd rather split it, the UX message fix (option 3) stands alone nicely as a tiny second issue — the "unavailable in this browser" message genuinely never tells the user the loopback requirement, which is half the pain you experienced.

threads.title: Switching away from a running session and back stops the view from updating (host keeps producing)
threads.bodyText:
Summary
Switching away from a session that is actively streaming, then switching back to it, leaves the conversation view frozen at the state it had when I left. The host keeps producing the whole time — the missing output is only missing on the client.
Steps to reproduce

Start a turn so a session is actively streaming.
Switch to another session.
Switch back to the still-streaming session.
The view no longer updates. New output never appears.

Reproduces reliably for me.
What makes it clear the host is fine

Restarting the app recovers the view, and it then shows more tokens than were on screen before the restart. The host had been producing all along; the client simply never received or rendered it.
Reloading the page also recovers it — but not every time.
Identical behaviour in a regular browser at http://127.0.0.1:3080 and in a Tauri WKWebView shell, so this is not a webview or rendering-layer issue.

So the host side looks healthy; what does not survive is the client's event subscription for that session across the switch.
Environment

@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.6-alpha.2, web profile
Node via Homebrew, macOS 26 (arm64)
~35 sessions in ~/.dsh/sessions/, 38 MB compressed; largest single session 5.0 MB compressed / 18.2 MB decompressed / 4325 records
Reproduced both in Firefox and in a WKWebView host

Notes (offered as leads, not as a diagnosis)
I looked through the shipped bundles but could not pin the cause with confidence, so please treat the following as observations only:

The view sits at openState === "loading" in dsh-client-ui-chat while this happens, i.e. await events.open(...) in SessionController.doOpen has not settled.
doOpen's catch has if (!isRemoteFailure(error)) throw error before it can set openState = "error". Any error that is not a normalised remote failure is rethrown and the state stays at loading — the user then sees neither a result nor an error. Whatever the root cause turns out to be, this path seems worth tightening: a failure that cannot present itself as a failure is hard to diagnose from the outside.
SessionEventStream.follow requires assistant-stream revisions to be strictly contiguous and throws RemoteStreamCarrierError on a gap. Carrier errors are swallowed and retried without limit. Since the revision keeps advancing while I am away from the session, I wondered whether the reopened snapshot baseline and the following frames can disagree — but I could not confirm this, and it may well be unrelated.

Happy to collect whatever runtime evidence would help (WS frames, host CPU, logs) — just say what would be useful.

threads.title: [Bug] Tool call fails on Windows: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare') — TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER unimplemented, ptc-runtime absent from all bundles
threads.bodyText:
Environment

OS: Windows 11 (win32, x64)
Node.js: v24.12.0
pnpm: 11.7.0 (pinned via packageManager in root package.json)
dsh version: dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2 (tag dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2, commit ddefc45fbc)
Install method: source build (git clone → pnpm install → pnpm run build)
Profile: web (via pnpm dsh web)

Steps to reproduce

Fresh clone at tag dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2
pnpm install
pnpm run build
pnpm dsh web — startup succeeds, zero failed plugins
Open a new session, send any prompt that triggers a tool call (e.g. a Glob file search)

Actual behavior
Every tool call fails with two cascading errors:
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')

DeepSeek Messages tool calls need immediate results   (400 INVALID_REQUEST)

The UI shows "本轮运行失败" (turn failed) with UNKNOWN / INVALID_REQUEST status tags.
Root cause analysis
The failure originates at:
// packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:170
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)
Grepping the whole repo, TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER appears only as a declaration — there is no implementation assigned to it anywhere:
packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:448   export interface ToolRuntimeScheduler { ... }
packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:463   export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER: unique symbol
packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:798   readonly [TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]: ToolRuntimeScheduler
packages/core/tools/src/ptc.ts:550     const scheduler = registry[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]   // consumer
packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:153,154,170,174  // consumers
packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts:6797,6800,6801  // API doc catalog only

So ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER] resolves to undefined, and .prepare(...) throws immediately.
Because the tool never executes, no tool result is produced. DeepSeek's API strictly requires each assistant.tool_calls entry to be followed by a matching tool message, so the next request is rejected with 400 INVALID_REQUEST / tool calls need immediate results. The second error is a consequence of the first, not an independent issue.
Suspected missing provider (needs maintainer confirmation)
packages/ptc-runtime/ exists in the tree and is the most likely provider of this scheduler. However:
Select-String -Path D:\dsh-fresh\packages\bundle\*\*\package.json -Pattern "ptc-runtime"
# → no matches
ptc-runtime does not appear in the package.json of any of the six bundles:
packages/bundle/{base, web-app, headless, acp-app, sdk-app, sdk-minimal}.
I am not certain that ptc-runtime is the intended provider — this is my inference from the package name. If another package is supposed to register TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER, please correct me.
Important: startup is clean
This is not a dependency or build problem. I verified:

pnpm run build completes successfully (all lib/ produced)
pnpm dsh web starts with zero failed plugins (no new Failed plugins entry in .dsh/logs/startup-*.log)

The failure happens at runtime, during tool dispatch, not at plugin activation.
Things already ruled out

✅ Corrupted node_modules — fully removed (\\?\ prefix to bypass MAX_PATH) and reinstalled from scratch; also cleared the pnpm store
✅ Wrong build entry — the correct entry is pnpm run build (tsx scripts/build.ts); note that packages/*/* have no build script, so pnpm -r build is a no-op for them
✅ Port conflict (EADDRINUSE on 3080) — killed stale node processes
✅ Poisoned session transcript — reproduced in a brand-new session
✅ Platform-specific native addon — @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run (landlock) is Linux-only, but sandbox-local failing is non-blocking and unrelated to this stack

Impact
Every tool call fails, so the agent cannot do anything requiring tools on Windows. The session transcript also becomes permanently poisoned once an unpaired tool_call is written: all subsequent messages in that session return the same 400, and a restart does not repair it (the broken transcript is reloaded as-is).
Questions for maintainers

Which package is supposed to provide the TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER implementation?
Should ptc-runtime be included in the web / headless bundles? If so, its absence looks like a packaging omission.
Is there a supported Windows path here, or is web profile unsupported on win32 at this version?
Can the runtime emit a clear error (e.g. "tool runtime scheduler not registered") instead of a raw undefined dereference?

Additional context
Happy to provide the full startup diagnostic log (~/.dsh/logs/startup-*.log) after redacting credentials, plus a screenshot of the failing turn.

threads.title: 本地提交回显在持久节点落地前就被退役 —— 任何耗时的 `agent/pre-step` 监听器都会变成可见的消息延迟
threads.bodyText:
现象
发送消息后，自己刚发出的那条消息要等 0.5–2 秒才出现在聊天记录里；在这段时间里，聊天区只显示 turn 状态指示器。消息不会丢，只是晚到。
这个窗口的宽度等于 agent/pre-step 瀑布上消耗的总时间。
机制
ISession.beginSubmission() 会同步创建一条本地提交回显，它存在的唯一目的就是：不管下游发生什么，你自己发的消息都应立刻可见。有两处把「prompt 送到了 host inbox」当成「持久节点已经渲染出来了」，从而破坏了这个不变量：

@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller —— observeSubmissionQueue() 一旦在队列镜像里看到该 rpcId 就调用 scheduleObservedRetirement()，这会把回显从 pendingSubmissions 里移除。
@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat —— observedRpcIds() 里有 for (const item of queue) if (item.rpcId !== void 0) observed.add(item.rpcId)，而 ChatView 会把 requestId 落在该集合里的回显全部过滤掉。

但队列行（inbox.nextTurn）不是聊天记录里的节点。持久化的 user 节点只能在 agent/pre-step 瀑布返回之后才追加 —— pre-step 可能返回 reject 或改写这一批消息，所以宿主无法更早地落盘。结果就是：回显已经消失，持久节点还没到，留下一个宽度恰好等于 pre-step 耗时的空窗。
用户观察到的顺序也由此直接推出：turn/start 把 running 置为真，于是 TurnStatus 先渲染，消息气泡要等持久节点落地才出现。
observedRpcIds 自己的文档注释写着这个交换是 atomic — no duplicate, no gap，这显然就是设计意图。队列来源那两行正是制造 gap 的地方。
最小复现
不需要桌面端，也不需要任何插件。在任意插件里：
ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async (payload, next) => {
  if (payload.step === 1) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))
  return next()
})
然后发一条消息。它会晚大约一秒出现，而这一秒里聊天记录只显示 turn 状态指示器。
真实案例：dsh-tauri-turnrewind 在 agent/pre-step 的 step 1 上跑一次工作区快照（git add --all → write-tree → ls-tree -r -l）。在一个 1223 个文件的工作区上，我们实测冷启动 2.77 秒、稳态约 1.1 秒，几乎精确复现了报告中的 0.5–2 秒延迟。
建议的修法
只有持久的 user / steering 节点才应算作 observed。队列来源只应退役「提交时这一轮已经在跑」（placement === "queued"）的那些回显 —— 那类回显本来就不在聊天记录里渲染，因为队列条接管了它们，而队列条已经按 rpcId 与宿主队列行做了去重。
具体来说：

observeSubmissionQueue：把退役条件收紧到回显自身的 placement === "queued"
observedRpcIds：整个删掉队列来源（ChatView 已经有 placement !== "queued" 这个条件了）

两处都必须改。只改 store 层，回显虽然还在 pendingSubmissions 里，但会被渲染层过滤掉；只改渲染层，store 层早就把它删掉了，渲染层没东西可渲染。
已知代价
如果一条消息在提交的瞬间恰好被排进了队列，它会在很短一段时间内（约等于 pre-step 的耗时）同时出现在聊天记录的回显和队列条的宿主队列行里。这是「让回显活到持久节点落地」无法避免的代价。上游目前是靠隐藏聊天记录那一份来避免重复的，而正是这个隐藏制造了空窗。
背景
我是在 dsh-tauri/deepseek-harness-desktop（一个打包了 dsh 的桌面壳）上遇到这个问题的。我们目前把它作为一个幂等补丁，在启动时打到活动核心上，症状完全消失。如果相比下游补丁你们更希望走 PR，我很乐意直接对 core 提一个。

threads.title: 长会话被输入审核整段熔断（400 Content Exists Risk / INVALID_REQUEST）：能否提供历史定位与会话级旁路？
threads.bodyText:
### 现象

一次普通的技术调研中，工具抓取了一个第三方 GitHub raw 页面（约 8 KB 中文正文，含一对 U+1F1E6–U+1F1FF 区间的区域指示符，即显示为国旗图形的符号）。该正文进入对话历史后，**该会话的所有后续请求**都返回：

    HTTP 400  {"message":"Content Exists Risk","code":"INVALID_REQUEST"}

### 关键判据：判定的是历史，不是新输入

- 同会话中把新消息缩短成两个字符（`test`）→ 仍然 400；
- 新建会话只发 `test` → 正常。

### 后果

1. 该会话不可恢复：报错不指明是哪条历史、哪个 token 区间、哪一类规则；也没有任何 API 层面的会话恢复出口，只能整段删除会话。
2. 排查过程本身会复现故障：为定位原因而读取旧会话转录 / 页面副本的会话，会立刻以同一原因失效——本次共 **6 个会话**依次熔断。
3. 一次无害的第三方文本抓取即让整段工作上下文作废，属单点不可逆故障。

### 复现（建议在隔离的调试环境）

1. 在全新会话中抓取该页面正文并写入会话（页面地址可私下提供；**请勿在生产会话里抓取**）；
2. 在同一会话继续发送任意新消息（如 `test`）→ 此后全部 400；
3. 对照：新会话只发 `test` → 正常。

### 请求

1. `INVALID_REQUEST` 的响应体附带**历史定位元数据**（触发消息序号/时间戳、触发类别），不回显敏感原文；
2. 提供**会话级旁路**（按序号截断/删除历史后重试），而不是永久 400；
3. 文档补充该错误码的触发条件与恢复路径（当前官方错误码页只列 400 格式错误/401/402/422/429/500/503，未收录它）。

### 环境

DSH Desktop 0.6.4（内核 `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.5-rc.2），Windows，2026-09-19。

> 附：脱敏后的完整报告（已移除本机路径、用户名、账号标识与第三方页面地址，不含任何触发字符）。如需页面地址用于复现，请告知，我可私下提供。
两点提醒

勾选「我搜索过类似的讨论」前先真的搜一次（关键词：Content Exists Risk、INVALID_REQUEST），命中同题就在那帖回复。
附件要用脱敏版（ContentExistsRisk-事件报告-公开版.md）重新上传；旧附件若已含本机路径，删除草稿里的引用并不能收回那个已上传的 URL。

ContentExistsRisk-事件报告-公开版.md

threads.title: web-search-deepseek 丢弃 usage：联网搜索的模型 turn 被计费，却不计入任何 token 统计
threads.bodyText:
现象
dsh-web-search-deepseek 的每次联网搜索都是一次真实的模型调用（Anthropic 兼容 Messages 端点 https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1 + 原生 web_search 工具，复用同一个 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY，会被计费），但响应只经 mapAnthropicResponse() 取搜索结果、usage 被丢弃，会话里仅 session.append("web/deepseek-search-llm-request", request) —— 只记请求，不记用量。

实测对账（2026-09-19，单 key，DSH 0.1.5-rc.1，Windows）

threads.bodyText:
上下文注入
@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt
上下文注入
skill-catalog
思考
User asks current time. Run pwsh Get-Date.
已停止
Pwsh
Show current date and time
本轮运行失败Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
层级
助手消息
状态
失败
{
command:"Get-Date -Format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss dddd (zzz)"",
description:"Show current date and time"
}
Interrupted: interrupted
pwsh
Execute a PowerShell command (pwsh -Command) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass workdir instead of using cd. Paths use native Windows form (C:\...); read environment variables with $env:NAME. Non-zero exits are reported as [exit code: N]. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed $env:DSH_* variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as [sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode] — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as [exit code: 1] without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Set run_in_background: true for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with job_output and stop it with job_kill. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types ([string], [datetime], [regex], [guid]); .NET static calls ([System.IO.*]::, [math]::), Add-Type, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. -f formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js child_process.spawn/exec with the default stdio: 'pipe') fails with EPERM, while stdio: 'inherit' and stdio: 'ignore' spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with sandbox_permissions (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence justification. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set sandbox_permissions. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

threads.title: [Bug] Since dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2 every tool call fails under `pnpm dsh` source launch: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`
threads.bodyText:
Summary
On a clean checkout of master (ddefc45fbc, release dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2), any pnpm dsh --profile headless "<task>" that triggers a tool call aborts with:
dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')

Introduced by PR #4471 (9ddef327a4, "feat: resolution mode link to runtime"), which changed the plain-Node source-launch default resolutionMode from 'link' to 'runtime'.
Environment

Windows 11 (10.0.26200), Node v24.16.0, pnpm 11.7.0
Source launch (pnpm dsh → node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts)
master ddefc45fbc, real DEEPSEEK_API_KEY

Repro (deterministic)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "Use the shell tool to run 'echo hello' and report its output."
The model emits a tool call, tool/call is appended to the session log, then the turn ends with the error above and exit code 1. Any task that triggers a tool call fails; tasks without tool calls complete normally.
Root cause
Under the tsx source launch, tsconfig paths project workspace bare imports to src/. The runtime profile resolver routes plugin imports through the declaring package manifest (entry.declarer, e.g. apps/cli/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-base/package.json); resolution from that parent follows package exports into built lib/, bypassing tsx's paths projection. The same workspace package then loads twice from different planes in one process (verified with module-evaluation probes: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools and @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent load from both src and lib; @deepseek-ai/dsh-headless only src; @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop only lib).
TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER is a Symbol(...) (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:463), so the two dsh-tools copies hold distinct symbol identities. Tool dispatch looks the scheduler up by symbol — ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(...) (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:170) — and when the registry instance and the lookup come from different copies, the lookup is undefined and every tool call crashes.
Verified fix (one line)
Restore the 'link' default for plain Node launches in apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts:
-  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'runtime'
+  const resolutionMode = packaged ? 'runtime' : options.resolutionMode ?? 'link'
After this change tool calls work again end to end (shell + read verified in one session). Packaged executables and the Electron Host still force runtime explicitly, so they are unaffected. Longer term, runtime routing would need to honor tsconfig paths (or otherwise keep one module plane) before it can be the source-launch default; a keyless source-launch e2e that performs at least one real tool call would have caught this regression.
中文摘要
0.1.6-alpha.2 起，源码启动的 dsh 一调用工具就报 UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare') 并退出。根因是 #4471 把普通启动的默认解析模式从 link 改为 runtime：runtime 路由以声明方 manifest 为父上下文重新解析插件 import，绕开了 tsx 的 tsconfig paths，同一个工作区包被同时从 src 和 lib 加载两份；TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER 是 Symbol，两份副本符号身份不一致，agent-loop 派发工具时取到 undefined。把 apps/cli/src/profile-boot.ts 的默认值改回 'link' 即恢复（打包产物与 Electron Host 强制 runtime 的路径不受影响，已端到端验证）。

threads.title: 客户端插件 bundle 被拼接成一个脚本 —— 同名顶层声明会让两个插件静默串包
threads.bodyText:
摘要
当两个客户端插件 bundle（插件包里的 lib/client.js）声明了同一个顶层函数名时，它们会在下发前被拼接成一个脚本。函数声明提升使得批次里最后一个定义覆盖全部：A 插件的模块被应用两次，B 插件的模块一次都没运行，页面永久卡在启动失败卡片上。串包本身不报错，服务端所有诊断也都是干净的。
环境

DSH 0.1.5-rc.2，web profile，Windows 11
同时核对过 0.1.6-alpha.2：未修复。它的 buildComboScript() 仍然是
for (const resource of resources) source += \${prepareSource(resource).source};\n` —— 纯拼接，没有逐模块作用域。（prepareSource只是0.1.5-rc.2里comboSource` 的改名，逻辑一致。）

症状

页面只显示失败卡片：
Failed to load plugins / dsh-pet-plus / failed to apply loader entry <8位十六进制> (dsh-pet-plus): locale namespace "pet.config" already has locale "zh"
那串 8 位 id 每次刷新都变 —— 它是前端启动时自己生成的，不是磁盘上的条目。
--dump-config 干净、宿主日志干净、依赖审计干净。

根因
客户端模块以 combo 脚本形式下发（/plugins/??a/client.js,b/client.js&rev=…）。我们两个 bundle 的结尾都是：
function makeFactory() { /* 本插件的模块 */ }
window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id: "<插件 id>", factory: makeFactory() });
拼接后，排在后面那个 makeFactory 被提升并覆盖了全部，于是：

B 插件那条条目拿到的是 A 插件的模块；
A 插件被应用两次、B 插件零次；
第二次 ctx.locale.register() 抛 already has locale；
runPluginBoot() 中断，mountApp() 没机会执行 → 界面永远挂不上，刷新和重启都不可能好。

最小复现
同一 profile 下装两个客户端 bundle，各自声明同名顶层 function makeX() 并各自注册一个 locale 命名空间，第二次注册即抛错。
为什么排查成本极高

串包本身不报错；
报出来的错（"locale 已注册"）离根因（重名）非常远；
服务端工具（--dump-config、宿主日志、依赖审计）全部干净 —— 故障只活在浏览器里；
那串随机 8 位 id 看起来像磁盘上某个东西的指纹，实际不是；
把其中一个插件"卸掉"会让报错消失，但那只是因为受害者不再被加载 —— 极容易误判成"修好了"。

建议修法
下发前给每个模块各自包一层作用域（例如每个 bundle 一个 IIFE），或者在组合阶段检测跨 bundle 的顶层声明冲突并点名两个 id 报错。哪怕只是一条警告，也能省掉一整晚的排查。

附：我们的临时处置（供参考，不影响上游修复）

两边工厂函数改名带插件前缀（makePetPlusFactory / makeUiAnimationFactory）；
客户端单例注册（locale 等）一律 try/catch 幂等；
一条插件只保留一个挂载路径（bundle 层 或 insert，不并存）。

threads.title: [Bug][Windows] workspace-write sandbox: every spawned console app dies with 0xC0000142 and raises a modal Windows error dialog on each tool call
threads.bodyText:
Version @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 · @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl 0.1.5-rc.2 OS Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9457 · Node v24.19.0 · Executor shell Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444 (no PS7 on this host) Mode workspace-write (default, sandbox confirmed active) · launched with npx dsh from an interactive PowerShell with a console · zh-CN localeSymptomConsole children started inside a Pwsh tool call raise a modal Windows "Application Error" dialog and die with STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED (0xC0000142) — but only on some spawn paths. Because agent activity constantly reaches cmd.exe-dependent tooling (.cmd/.bat shims = the npm.cmd/npx.cmd/pnpm.cmd path), the user gets a popup on essentially every conversation turn. GUI processes are unaffected.The decisive matrix (all inside ONE sandboxed Pwsh call)
Spawn method | Result
-- | --
Start-Process cmd.exe (PS 5.1 default = ShellExecute) | -1073741502 + popup ❌
.NET ProcessStartInfo, UseShellExecute=$true (WindowStyle Normal or Hidden) | -1073741502 + popup ❌
.NET ProcessStartInfo, UseShellExecute=$false, CreateNoWindow=$true | -1073741502 + popup ❌
Start-Process -NoNewWindow | throws Access is denied ❌
UseShellExecute=$false + CreateNoWindow=$false + WindowStyle=Normal | cmd /c "echo OK" prints OK, exit=0 ✅
… same path | where.exe node → prints path, exit=0 ✅
… same path | node.exe -e "console.log(...)" → prints output, exit=0 ✅
… same path | python.exe -c "print(1)" → prints 1, exit=0 ✅
… same path | _probe_shim.cmd (exit /b 5) → prints SHIM-RAN, exit=5 ✅
… same path via cmd /c | _probe_shim.cmd → runs, exit=0 ✅
CREATE_NO_WINDOW (either direct or via cmd /c) | _probe_shim.cmd → -1073741502 + popup ❌ (never runs)
GUI (notepad.exe) | exit=0 ✅
A .cmd child that writes a probe file succeeds on the direct path and never executes on the CREATE_NO_WINDOW path — a real execution difference, not a reporting artifact. -WindowStyle Hidden still allocates a console, so window visibility is not the factor.InterpretationThe restricted token is not the blocker: the same token runs cmd.exe/node.exe/.cmd fine when the child gets a console. The failing paths are exactly those where the caller does not create a console (CREATE_NO_WINDOW, and the ShellExecute route through Explorer), leaving cmd.exe to AllocConsole() itself and fail. Note this contradicts a literal reading of the documented boundary ("CREATE_NO_WINDOW/CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE children die during DLL initialization"): in my tests CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE works and CREATE_NO_WINDOW alone is sufficient to kill.The host console is not the trigger — this host is launched from a console-attached PowerShell, and a sandboxed CreateProcess that creates a console succeeds, so #810's "console-less host" does not describe this machine.Sandbox is demonstrably active复制Set-Content C:\Users\28139\_dsh_sandbox_probe.txt      → Access to the path ... is denied.
Set-Content D:\Deepseek Harness\_dsh_sandbox_probe.txt → success
TMP = C:\Users\28139\AppData\Local\Temp\dsh-wT3NhX     (private per-session temp)Outside the sandbox (user's own terminal) the identical command returns 0.Windows System log, provider Application Popup (ID 26), one entry per failure: Application popup: cmd.exe - Application Error : 应用程序无法正常启动(0xc0000142)。请单击“确定”关闭应用程序。Popup census by day: 0 cmd.exe/node.exe popups from 08-25 to 09-07 (before DSH was ever launched; the ~19 entries there are SakuraCat.exe/audiodg.exe/steamwebhelper.exe), then 188 on the first DSH session day (cmd.exe×122, node.exe×27, where.exe×19, ipconfig×4, whoami/HOSTNAME/python/tasklist×3 each, attrib×2, PING×1, powershell×1). 53 of them (cmd.exe×30, node.exe×23) occurred in the first 27 minutes, before any of my own bulk testing — plain agent activity is enough.Ruled out hereValid Microsoft signature on cmd.exe; no malicious/unknown DLLs in System32; AppInit_DLLs empty + LoadAppInit_DLLs=0 (both bitnesses), no AppCertDlls, no cmd AutoRun; no IFEO hijack; Huorong 6.0 AV very likely irrelevant (its hipsdaemon.log shows no interception of cmd.exe/node.exe; disabling hardening, whitelisting the binaries and a reboot changed nothing); no console/terminal delegation misconfiguration; 32-bit and 64-bit console apps behave identically; CRT DLLs present.QuestionsWhy does the spawn path use CREATE_NO_WINDOW/ShellExecute for command execution when CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE/inherited-console spawns work under the same token? Relaxing that flag appears to fix both the popups and the outright failure of .cmd-based tooling.Failing that, can the modal dialog be suppressed (STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW + SW_HIDE, or SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS))? A silent failure beats a modal box on every turn (cf. #1344).Should console-dependent spawns be surfaced as a structured SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE/denial fact instead of a bare Access is denied?Related: dsh-win32 compatibility notes list this signature (0xC0000142 / STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED associated with restricted-token launch) and point at Desktop PR #266 — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjh9714/dsh-win32/refs/heads/master/docs/windows-first-run.mdHappy to run any diagnostic on this machine — it reproduces 100% of the time. Environment is stock: no packaged runtime files modified, AV not disabled, permissions not widened.

Version @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 · @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl 0.1.5-rc.2 OS Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.9457 · Node v24.19.0 · Executor shell Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444 (no PS7 on this host) Mode workspace-write (default, sandbox confirmed active) · launched with npx dsh from an interactive PowerShell with a console · zh-CN locale
Symptom
Console children started inside a Pwsh tool call raise a modal Windows "Application Error" dialog and die with STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED (0xC0000142) — but only on some spawn paths. Because agent activity constantly reaches cmd.exe-dependent tooling (.cmd/.bat shims = the npm.cmd/npx.cmd/pnpm.cmd path), the user gets a popup on essentially every conversation turn. GUI processes are unaffected.
The decisive matrix (all inside ONE sandboxed Pwsh call)
Spawn method	Result
Start-Process cmd.exe (PS 5.1 default = ShellExecute)	-1073741502 + popup ❌
.NET ProcessStartInfo, UseShellExecute=$true (WindowStyle Normal or Hidden)	-1073741502 + popup ❌
.NET ProcessStartInfo, UseShellExecute=$false, CreateNoWindow=$true	-1073741502 + popup ❌
Start-Process -NoNewWindow	throws Access is denied ❌
UseShellExecute=$false + CreateNoWindow=$false + WindowStyle=Normal	cmd /c "echo OK" prints OK, exit=0 ✅
… same path	where.exe node → prints path, exit=0 ✅
… same path	node.exe -e "console.log(...)" → prints output, exit=0 ✅
… same path	python.exe -c "print(1)" → prints 1, exit=0 ✅
… same path	_probe_shim.cmd (exit /b 5) → prints SHIM-RAN, exit=5 ✅
… same path via cmd /c	_probe_shim.cmd → runs, exit=0 ✅
CREATE_NO_WINDOW (either direct or via cmd /c)	_probe_shim.cmd → -1073741502 + popup ❌ (never runs)
GUI (notepad.exe)	exit=0 ✅
A .cmd child that writes a probe file succeeds on the direct path and never executes on the CREATE_NO_WINDOW path — a real execution difference, not a reporting artifact. -WindowStyle Hidden still allocates a console, so window visibility is not the factor.
Interpretation
The restricted token is not the blocker: the same token runs cmd.exe/node.exe/.cmd fine when the child gets a console. The failing paths are exactly those where the caller does not create a console (CREATE_NO_WINDOW, and the ShellExecute route through Explorer), leaving cmd.exe to AllocConsole() itself and fail. Note this contradicts a literal reading of the documented boundary ("CREATE_NO_WINDOW/CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE children die during DLL initialization"): in my tests CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE works and CREATE_NO_WINDOW alone is sufficient to kill.
The host console is not the trigger — this host is launched from a console-attached PowerShell, and a sandboxed CreateProcess that creates a console succeeds, so #810's "console-less host" does not describe this machine.
Sandbox is demonstrably active
复制
Set-Content C:\Users\28139_dsh_sandbox_probe.txt      → Access to the path ... is denied.
Set-Content D:\Deepseek Harness_dsh_sandbox_probe.txt → success
TMP = C:\Users\28139\AppData\Local\Temp\dsh-wT3NhX     (private per-session temp)
Outside the sandbox (user's own terminal) the identical command returns 0.
Windows System log, provider Application Popup (ID 26), one entry per failure: Application popup: cmd.exe - Application Error : 应用程序无法正常启动(0xc0000142)。请单击“确定”关闭应用程序。
Popup census by day: 0 cmd.exe/node.exe popups from 08-25 to 09-07 (before DSH was ever launched; the ~19 entries there are SakuraCat.exe/audiodg.exe/steamwebhelper.exe), then 188 on the first DSH session day (cmd.exe×122, node.exe×27, where.exe×19, ipconfig×4, whoami/HOSTNAME/python/tasklist×3 each, attrib×2, PING×1, powershell×1). 53 of them (cmd.exe×30, node.exe×23) occurred in the first 27 minutes, before any of my own bulk testing — plain agent activity is enough.
Ruled out here
Valid Microsoft signature on cmd.exe; no malicious/unknown DLLs in System32; AppInit_DLLs empty + LoadAppInit_DLLs=0 (both bitnesses), no AppCertDlls, no cmd AutoRun; no IFEO hijack; Huorong 6.0 AV very likely irrelevant (its hipsdaemon.log shows no interception of cmd.exe/node.exe; disabling hardening, whitelisting the binaries and a reboot changed nothing); no console/terminal delegation misconfiguration; 32-bit and 64-bit console apps behave identically; CRT DLLs present.

Why does the spawn path use CREATE_NO_WINDOW/ShellExecute for command execution when CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE/inherited-console spawns work under the same token? Relaxing that flag appears to fix both the popups and the outright failure of .cmd-based tooling.
Failing that, can the modal dialog be suppressed (STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW + SW_HIDE, or SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS))? A silent failure beats a modal box on every turn (cf. #1344).
Should console-dependent spawns be surfaced as a structured SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE/denial fact instead of a bare Access is denied?
Related: dsh-win32 compatibility notes list this signature (0xC0000142 / STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED associated with restricted-token launch) and point at Desktop PR #266 — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjh9714/dsh-win32/refs/heads/master/docs/windows-first-run.md

threads.title: Bug: web sidebar lists no workspaces and no sessions after upgrade (0.1.5-rc.2)
threads.bodyText:
Bug: web sidebar lists no workspaces and no sessions after upgrade — persisted store shape changed without bumping the persist key (0.1.5-rc.2)

Environment









DSH
0.1.5-rc.2 (global npm install, dsh web)


OS
Windows (also reproduced by reading the shipped client bundles)


Node
v24.18.0


Browser
<fill in: e.g. Chrome/Edge xyz>


Origin
http://127.0.0.1:3080


Trigger
Upgrade via npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh over an earlier 0.1.5-rc build



Symptom
The left sidebar shows no workspaces and no sessions at all — the list is completely empty. Everything else in the GUI works normally: chat, attachments, model selection, settings, and the session transcript. A hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) does not help, and the state survives browser restarts.
Console evidence
TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at Object.entries (<anonymous>)
    at retainAccountKeys (client.js:218:1)
    at index-BKQ_L1z6.js:56:69359
    at index-BKQ_L1z6.js:56:68694
    at produce (index-BKQ_L1z6.js:56:66201)
    at Object.update (index-BKQ_L1z6.js:56:68674)
    at a.<computed> [as retainAccountKeys] (index-BKQ_L1z6.js:56:69348)
    at client.js:2017:1

client.js:526 slot entry crashed in 'sidebar.workspaces': TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object
    at Object.entries (<anonymous>)
    at retainAccountKeys (client.js:218:1)

Root cause


@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace persists its view store in localStorage under the literal key dsh.workspace.view.v5:
init: () => ({
  groupBy: "workspace",
  orderBy: "updated",
  groupExpansion: {},
  sessionOrderByAccount: {},
  sessionUpdatedAtByAccount: {}
}),
persist: "dsh.workspace.view.v5",


The client store helper hydrates by replacing the state with the stored JSON — it does not merge init() defaults, so a field absent from the stored record stays undefined:
// dsh-client-store helper bundled in the shell (index-*.js), function Tc(t, r)
const i = localStorage.getItem(r);
if (i !== null) t.setState(M6(JSON.parse(i)), true);


A record persisted by an earlier 0.1.5-rc build uses the same key v5 but predates the sessionUpdatedAtByAccount field. retainAccountKeys then dereferences the missing field:
retainAccountKeys: (d, workspaceKeys) => {
  const retained = new Set(workspaceKeys);
  d.groupExpansion = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(d.groupExpansion).filter(([key]) => retained.has(key)));
  d.sessionOrderByAccount = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(d.sessionOrderByAccount).filter(([key]) => retained.has(key)));
  d.sessionUpdatedAtByAccount = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(d.sessionUpdatedAtByAccount).filter(([key]) => retained.has(key))); // ← throws here
},


The call happens in an effect the moment the workspace projection becomes ready (lib/client.js:2015-2021), i.e. exactly when the list is about to render:
useEffect(() => {
  if (workspacePhase !== "ready") return;
  actions.retainAccountKeys(["", FLAT_SESSION_ORDER_KEY, ...workspaces.map((w) => w.workspaceId)]);
}, [actions.retainAccountKeys, workspacePhase, workspaces]);


The throw escapes into the sidebar.workspaces slot entry, its error boundary catches it (client.js:526) and renders nothing. Result: a permanently empty sidebar in that browser, on every load, with no visible error and no way to recover from the UI.


Minimal reproduction


Open the web GUI and go to DevTools → Application → Local Storage for the GUI origin.


Set dsh.workspace.view.v5 to a pre-sessionUpdatedAtByAccount shape:
{"groupBy":"workspace","orderBy":"updated","groupExpansion":{},"sessionOrderByAccount":{}}


Reload. The sidebar lists no workspaces and no sessions, and the console shows the trace above.


Run the workaround below: the sidebar returns immediately, with every workspace and session intact.


Workaround
localStorage.removeItem('dsh.workspace.view.v5');
location.reload();
Only browser-local view preferences are lost (which groups were expanded, manual row order). Workspaces and sessions live in $DSH_HOME/storages/workspace.json and the session store, and are untouched.
To keep those preferences, repair the record instead of dropping it:
const k = 'dsh.workspace.view.v5', s = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(k) || '{}');
s.groupExpansion ??= {}; s.sessionOrderByAccount ??= {}; s.sessionUpdatedAtByAccount ??= {};
localStorage.setItem(k, JSON.stringify(s)); location.reload();
Note: localStorage is per origin, so a browser that reaches the GUI on a different origin (e.g. localhost vs 127.0.0.1, or a LAN address) holds a separate record and needs the same fix there.
Suggested fixes

Guard the dereferences (d.groupExpansion ?? {}, etc.) so an already-poisoned browser recovers on the next reload instead of losing the whole sidebar. This is the fix that unbreaks existing users.
Bump the persist key (or add a version field with a migration) whenever the persisted shape changes — the shape grew while the key stayed dsh.workspace.view.v5.
Merge on hydrate ({...init(), ...stored}) in the store helper, so a field added in a later build can never be undefined.
Surface slot crashes: today a crashed sidebar.workspaces entry renders as a silently empty sidebar, which reads as "my conversations are gone".

Diagnostic notes

dsh --profile web --dump-config shows all 53 web client plugins mounted and enabled, including ui-sidebar, ui-workspace and workspace-controller; the profile composition is not at fault.
session_diagnose reports all 6 stored sessions as ok, and the workspace registry/directories resolve correctly under realpath — the data is intact. This is purely client-side persisted-state handling.
The reporter's web profile additionally mounts a third-party plugin (dsh-sessions-diagnosis, added with dsh plugin --profile web add .). It is unrelated to the trace, and the crash reproduces from the persisted value alone with no plugin involved.

threads.title: [Bug] dsh causes massive macOS Swap explosion (300GB+ System Data / 191GB kernel_task) even when using API-only mode
threads.bodyText:
### Describe the bug
I am experiencing a catastrophic memory and disk space explosion when running `dsh` (DeepSeek Harness) on my 2020 13-inch Intel MacBook Pro. 
The critical issue is that I am only using the API, not running local models, yet the local resource consumption is extreme. The harness (specifically its local mysqld process) exhausts my physical RAM, forcing macOS to heavily use virtual memory (Swap). This has bloated my "System Data" to over 300GB and caused kernel_task to write 191GB to my SSD.
Note: I have used OpenAI's Codex for similar tasks before, and it never caused this level of resource exhaustion.

threads.title: Every tool call fails with: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare') — dual dsh-tools instance / per-instance Symbol() for TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER
threads.bodyText:
Summary
On DSH 0.1.6-alpha.2 (commit ddefc45fbc, running from a source checkout via pnpm dsh / node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts), every tool call aborts the turn with:
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')

The tool never executes (session log shows tool/call followed immediately by turn/end with reason: { kind: 'error', ... }). This makes any session that calls a tool completely non-functional — no bash, no plugin tools, nothing runs.
Environment

DSH version: 0.1.6-alpha.2 (source checkout at ddefc45fbc, master)
OS: Rocky Linux 10.1 under WSL2, Node v22.22.2, pnpm
Running mode: source checkout — zdsh.service runs dsh web from /opt/.../deepseek-harness via node --import tsx/esm apps/cli/src/bin.ts; profiles (~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/*) symlink back into the repo's workspace node_modules

Reproduction
cd /path/to/deepseek-harness
pnpm dsh --profile headless --json 'use the bash tool to run: echo hello'
Output:
{"type":"tool_call","callId":"call_...","tool":"bash","input":{"command":"echo hello", ...}}
{"type":"status","phase":"turn_end","turn":1,"reason":{"kind":"error","error":{"message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')","code":"UNKNOWN"}}}
dsh: UNKNOWN: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
No tool_result is ever emitted. The same failure occurs for every tool in every turn (hindsight tools, bash, etc.).
Root cause
The failing call site is packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)
TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER is declared as a per-instance unique symbol in packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:
export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER: unique symbol = Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')
In this deployment, the @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools package ends up loaded twice:

The CLI app itself runs from TypeScript sources via tsx → resolves packages/core/tools/src/index.ts.
Profile plugins resolve through ~/.dsh/profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop (symlinked into the repo workspace), whose package.json main points at the built lib/index.js copy of the same package.

Each copy evaluates Symbol('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler') independently, producing two symbols with identical descriptions that are not === to each other. The ToolRuntime service registers its scheduler on the instance it sees, while the agent loop looks it up with the symbol from the other instance:
// ctx.tools is a ToolRuntime and DOES own a symbol with the same description:
own: [
  'Symbol(cordis.tracker)',
  'Symbol(@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler)'
],
expected: 'Symbol(@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler)'
// ...but ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER] === undefined
(The diagnostic above was produced by temporarily logging Object.getOwnPropertySymbols(ctx.tools) at the call site.)
So the error is a classic dual-package-instance / symbol-identity hazard: the "scheduler is missing" symptom is misleading — it is registered, just under a symbol the consumer cannot see.
Suggested fix
Use the global symbol registry so the symbol is identical across module instances:
// packages/core/tools/src/index.ts
export const TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER: unique symbol = Symbol.for('@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools.scheduler')
(and the corresponding lib/index.js build output).
I can confirm this resolves the issue: after patching both copies (src/index.ts:463 and the built lib/index.js:2526) from Symbol(...) to Symbol.for(...), the same headless reproduction succeeds — the tool executes, a tool_result is emitted, and the turn ends with {"kind":"completed"}.
Alternative/complementary hardening options:

Deduplicate the package instance (e.g. ensure profile plugin resolution and the tsx-run app resolve to the same module file), though this is harder to guarantee across arbitrary profile layouts.
Fail with an actionable message at the call site when the scheduler symbol lookup misses (the current generic TypeError took a while to track down; a hint like "tool runtime scheduler symbol not found — possible dual instance of @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools" would help).

Happy to open a PR for the Symbol.for change if the approach looks right.

threads.title: dsh-ears imports TypertLookupFailure from @deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol, but no published protocol version exports it
threads.bodyText:
Summary
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web fails at boot because dsh-ears still imports TypertLookupFailure, which @deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol no longer exports.
Reproduction
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web

Fails with:
Error: dsh: plugin tree failed to load: failed to apply loader entry include (cordis:include): failed to import loader entry dsh-ears (dsh-ears): The requested module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol' does not provide an export named 'TypertLookupFailure'

file:///C:/Users/jackdai/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-ears/lib/index.js:5
import { TypertLookupFailure, TypertRemoteService } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol";
         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
SyntaxError: The requested module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol' does not provide an export named 'TypertLookupFailure'

Versions involved



Package
Version




@deepseek-ai/dsh (CLI, latest)
0.1.5-rc.2


@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol (resolved by the above)
0.1.5-rc.2


dsh-ears (loaded into the web profile)
0.2.2



Evidence


dsh-ears@0.2.2 lib/index.js:5 imports the removed symbol:
import { TypertLookupFailure, TypertRemoteService } from "@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol";


@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol@0.1.5-rc.2 has zero occurrences of LookupFailure across lib/ (grep -r LookupFailure lib/ → 0 matches). Its value exports are:
RemoteError, remoteErrorOf, Remote, RemoteScope, TypertRemoteService, bindTypertRemote, isTypertRemoteSegment, remoteMethods, typertOwnedValue, isTypertOwnedValue, TYPERT_OWNED_VALUE (plus type-only exports).


The failure vocabulary was collapsed: TypertLookupFailure and TypertRemoteFailure were replaced by RemoteError<Code> — see packages/typert/protocol/src/index.ts and the design note .agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-28-ctx-remote-failure-vocabulary.md (status: implemented). Neither 0.1.5-rc.2 nor the also-published 0.1.6-alpha.2 exports TypertLookupFailure.


Expected
dsh-ears@0.2.2 was published against the older failure vocabulary and is incompatible with the latest dsh release. Either:

republish dsh-ears against the RemoteError API, or
have @deepseek-ai/dsh@latest pin a compatible dsh-ears version.

Environment

OS: Windows 11
Node: v24.14.1
