threads.title: [Bug] dsh-app://shell/* documents return 404: update dialog renders blank, main window stays unclickable and blurred
threads.bodyText:
Summary
Building @deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop 0.1.6-alpha.2 from source on Windows x64, the update-consent dialog never renders. The main window then becomes unresponsive to all mouse input and stays blurred. Both symptoms have one cause.
Root cause
apps/desktop/src/main.ts registers a single protocol.handle for the dsh-app scheme. It branches only on url.hostname === 'app' and falls through to:
return Promise.resolve(new Response(null, { status: 404 }))
But the update flow addresses its shell documents with hostname shell:

update-dialog.ts:33 — const page = 'dsh-app://shell/update-dialog.html'
mandatory-update-window.ts:46 — same scheme/host for mandatory-update.html

Every other layer already expects shell: preload-update-dialog.ts:9 gates on location.href === 'dsh-app://shell/update-dialog.html', preload-mandatory.ts:16 likewise, and update-dialog.ts:105-112 rejects any IPC unless event.senderFrame.url === page. So the 404 is not deliberate — the files do ship in the asar at renderer/update-dialog.html, they are simply never served.
Why one 404 produces both symptoms
A 404 Response does not reject loadURL — Chromium just renders an empty error document. So:

update-dialog.ts:89's void window.loadURL(page).catch(abort) never fires abort.
The window is never destroyed, so the transparent modal: true overlay stays show()n.
Windows sets WS_DISABLED on the parent, which drops all mouse input — the UI is unclickable.
update-overlay.ts injected body { filter: blur(2px) !important; } into the parent, and unblur() only runs on the overlay's 'closed' event, which never fires — the UI stays blurred.

Fix
Two lines in main.ts:
// Shell-owned documents (update consent, mandatory update) ship beside the main bundle.
if (url.hostname === 'shell') return serveWebDocument(request, join(app.getAppPath(), 'renderer'))
serveWebDocument already exists and its BOOT injection is a no-op for anything but /index.html. app.getAppPath() resolves the renderer root in both dev and packaged modes (packaged: resources/app.asar -> app.asar/renderer; dev: apps/desktop -> apps/desktop/renderer).
Verification
Built and ran the packaged app with the patch applied:




before
after




dialog card
blank error page
renders, both buttons present


scrim pixel ratio
1.0104 (no scrim)
0.762 (theory 0.76)


parent window style
0x1CC70000 (includes WS_DISABLED)
0x14C70000


parent sharpness (gradMax)
—
238


mouse hover on a button
—
9475 px changed



The scrim row is a quantitative check: the overlay paints rgb(0 0 0 / 24%), so over a 252-white background the expected pixel value is 252 x 0.76 = 191.5; measured 192.0. The window-style row is the unclickable half — the only differing bit is WS_DISABLED (0x08000000). Hover is the end-to-end check: a WS_DISABLED window receives no mouse messages at all, so a localized hover highlight proves input is reaching the renderer.
Scope
Not specific to the unsigned build — this affects every build. The HTML is present in the asar, so it is not a packaging omission.
Happy to provide a patch if that is useful.

threads.title: Scheduler failure leaves unpaired assistant tool-call blocks, making the session permanently unserializable
threads.bodyText:
Summary
When a turn fails after an assistant message with tool calls is durably appended but before those calls receive results, the turn is closed cleanly (step/end + turn/end{kind:'error'}) with unpaired tool-call blocks left on the model-visible surface. Nothing repairs them, and dsh-llm-deepseek's Messages serializer fail-closes on unpaired calls — so every subsequent message in that session fails permanently with INVALID_REQUEST.
This is not a bug in any single component. Both relevant behaviors are deliberate and documented. The gap is at their junction: no layer owns the resulting unpaired calls.
Impact
The session is unrecoverable through the product UI. Each new turn re-serializes the full history and throws:
DeepSeek Messages tool calls need immediate results (INVALID_REQUEST)

The error names the provider, so it points at the wrong layer — the actual cause is in agent-loop and is no longer visible by the time the user sees it.
Compaction cannot rescue the session either. dsh-compaction's tool-pairing derives safe cuts from tool-call/result balance (eventDelta: assistant tool-call blocks +1, tool/result -1). An unpaired call means the in-progress count never returns to zero, so toolPairingBalancedBefore/toolPairingBalancedAfter is false for every cut after the poisoned assistant message — compaction can never drop it.
Observed on 5/5 affected sessions; the poisoned sessions had to be abandoned.
Observed event sequence
Real session log (session.v3.jsonl, SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION 3), abridged:
17  assistant/message   (content includes a tool-call block)
18  tool/call           name=bash
19  step/end            turn=1 step=1
20  turn/end            {"kind":"error","error":{"message":"…","code":"UNKNOWN"}}

No tool/result for the call. Turns without tool calls in the same sessions ended {"kind":"completed"} normally.
The next turn in the same session:
29  turn/end  {"kind":"error","error":{"message":"DeepSeek Messages tool calls need immediate results","code":"INVALID_REQUEST"}}

What actually poisons the transcript
The durable tool/call event is not what the provider sees. SURFACE_EVENT_TYPES in packages/core/session/src/surface.ts admits exactly four types — system/message, user/message, assistant/message, tool/result — and deriveEventMessage returns null for everything else, including tool/call.
So the unserializable input is the tool-call block inside assistant/message at seq 17. The tool/call event at seq 18 is trace/replay data. This matters for scoping the fix, and it means the failure is wider than the log excerpt above suggests (see below).
How the gap arises
1. agent-loop deliberately does not compensate on scheduler failure.
packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts states this three times — in the module doc:

A terminal scheduler failure preserves already-recorded tool/call events without fabricating results.

in executeToolCalls:

An internal scheduler failure stops new dispatches, drains already-started dispatches, and rejects with the first failure without fabricating tool results.

and in runGroup:

Scheduler failure drains dispatches without committing synthetic recovery results.

The exit path:
schedulerFailure ??= { error }
await Promise.allSettled(inFlight.values())
throw schedulerFailure.error
2. Two distinct unpaired shapes result, not one.
startCall appends the call before the scheduler can fail:
callSeqs[index] = appendToolCall(session, turn, step, call.block)   // durable
started++
const prepared = await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)  // may throw
session-checkpoint-policy additionally guarantees the call is flushed before the tool body runs ("top-level tool calls checkpoint their recorded call before the tool body").
But fillPool does not advance its cursor when startCall throws:
await startCall(nextToStart)
nextToStart++
So for a group of N calls failing at index k:

call k — tool/call appended, no result. Matches repair.ts's TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN case.
calls k+1 … N-1 — never reach startCall at all: no tool/call, no tool/result, but their blocks are already durable in the assistant message. Matches repair.ts's TOOL_NOT_STARTED case.

Both shapes poison the surface identically, because the surface reads the assistant blocks. Any fix must cover both.
3. Crash repair is out of scope by design.
packages/core/session/src/repair.ts is scoped to crash tails only. interruptedTurnClosers clears pendingCalls at step/end and turn/end, and returns early when no turn is open:
if (openTurn === null || last === undefined) return []
Here both boundary events were written normally by the finally blocks in agent.ts, so the scan sees a balanced log and emits nothing. Correct per its contract — it just means nobody covers this case.
4. The provider fail-closes.
packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/messages/serialize.ts validates over the projected messages:
if (pending.size > 0) throw new LlmError('DeepSeek Messages tool calls need immediate results', 'INVALID_REQUEST')
Asymmetry with the abort path
Cancellation does compensate. appendSkippedToolCall writes a durable call/result pair with TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH, and the aborted branch of runGroup applies it to every uncovered call:
for (const call of group.slice(started)) appendSkippedToolCall(session, turn, step, call.block)
The scheduler-failure branch has no equivalent. repair.ts supplies canonical results for two further cases (TOOL_NOT_STARTED, TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN). So three of four ways a call can fail to produce a result are already compensated; scheduler failure is the only one that is not.
Relationship to the recorded decision
This consequence is already documented as an accepted trade-off in 2026-07-10-parallel-tool-call-execution.md:

A terminal scheduler failure may leave recorded calls without results before the failed step closes. Waiting for live dispatches preserves quiescence without misreporting those internal failures as tool outcomes.

and the same note lists a rejected alternative:

Convert scheduler failures into tool results. AgentLoop cannot determine whether a rejected dispatch invoked the tool body; ToolRuntime owns body-invocation state and typed tool outcomes. Internal scheduler failures therefore remain terminal instead of being reclassified as ABORTED results.

This issue is not a request to reopen that rejection. The rejection turns on reclassifying an internal failure as a claimed tool outcome — ABORTED asserts the body did not run, which AgentLoop cannot know. That reasoning is correct and should stand.
What the note weighs is the loss of outcome fidelity. What it does not weigh is that the leftover calls make the entire session permanently unusable, with no in-product recovery. That is the new information here.
TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN resolves the tension the note identifies: it claims no outcome. Its existing wording in repair.ts states the outcome is unknown and instructs against blind retry:

The tool call was interrupted after it was recorded, but no result was durably recorded. Its outcome is unknown. Decide whether to retry from the tool semantics […] Do not retry blindly.

That is precisely the epistemic position AgentLoop is in after a scheduler failure, so recording it misreports nothing.
Proposed invariant

Every tool-call block in a surfaced assistant/message must have a paired tool/result before its turn is closed.

Stated over assistant blocks rather than tool/call events, this matches how repair.ts and dsh-compaction's tool-pairing already model pairing, and it covers both shapes from §2. An invariant phrased over tool/call events would miss calls k+1 … N-1 entirely.
The compensation belongs on the failure path in agent-loop, reusing both canonical results from repair.ts — TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for the started call, TOOL_NOT_STARTED for its unstarted siblings — not in widening repair.ts's scan, whose crash-tail contract is correct and should stay narrow.
Suggested acceptance criteria

The failure branch of runGroup compensates every uncovered call in the group, mirroring the existing aborted branch.
A session that has taken a scheduler failure serializes successfully on its next turn.
The pairing invariant is asserted at step close. packages/core/session/src/invariant.ts currently does pendingCalls = { kind: 'clear' } in case 'step/end' with no emptiness check — exactly parallel to repair.ts. That clear is the natural place for the assertion.

The existing tool-call scheduler: failure quiescence test in packages/core/agent-loop/tests/tool-calls.spec.ts asserts quiescence and the error turn/end only; it does not assert the absence of results, so the compensation should be additive to it rather than a behavior conflict. (That test's own fixture session ends with three unpaired calls.)
Resolved questions

Does the chat-completions serializer have the same pairing check? No. packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/protocols/chat-completions/serialize.ts emits assistant tool_calls and role: 'tool' messages with no pairing validation, and there is no shared validation above the two protocols. So the same poisoned session fails remotely (live-API rejection) rather than locally, and the failure shape differs by protocol. Whether that wire boundary should also fail closed is a separate hardening question, not required to fix this.
Is there a runtime invariant asserting call/result pairing at turn close? No — see the acceptance criteria above for where it would go.

Open question

Is there a UI affordance to fork a poisoned session before the bad turn? SessionStore.fork(source, boundary) allows a boundary at a between-turn event, so an API-level recovery exists, but I could not find a user-facing path to it.

Environment

dsh 0.1.6-alpha.2 (ddefc45), macOS arm64, Node 24
Profile: web, provider deepseek-official, Messages protocol

The scheduler failure that triggered this in our case was a duplicate-module-instance defect causing ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER] to be undefined; that is a separate defect and will be filed on its own. This issue is about the unrecoverable state left behind, which applies to any scheduler failure.

threads.title: Bash tool call fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')", corrupting the session for all later turns
threads.bodyText:
Bash tool call fails with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')", corrupting the session for all later turns
Summary
A bash tool call sometimes fails with Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare') before it ever executes. No tool/result event is ever recorded for the call, so the session's message history is left with a dangling tool_calls entry. Every subsequent turn in that conversation then fails with DeepSeek's own validation error:

An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'. (insufficient tool messages following tool_calls message)

The conversation is effectively bricked — there is no recovery except starting a new session.
Environment

Reproduced on @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 (official npm release, fresh global install, zero third-party plugins installed)
Also reproduced from a source checkout at tag dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2
macOS (Darwin arm64), Node v22.22.3
Provider: deepseek-official, model deepseek-flash, reasoningEffort: high
permission/preset: workspace-write, approval/policy: ask

Steps to reproduce

Fresh install: npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh, dsh web --no-open
Open a new conversation in any workspace
Send a message that leads the model to run a shell command, e.g. (Chinese): 你有安裝 ai-storyboard plugin? — the model reasons that it should check the filesystem and issues a bash tool call such as pwd; ls -la
Observe the turn fail immediately with Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')
Send any follow-up message in the same conversation — it now fails with the tool_calls / insufficient tool messages error and never recovers

Evidence from the session log
Decoding ~/.dsh/sessions/<workspace>/<session-id>/session.v3.jsonl.zstd for a failing session shows:
assistant/message | ... (model reasons about checking installed plugins) ...
tool/call         | {"turn":1,"step":1,"callId":"call_...","name":"bash","arguments":"{\"command\":\"pwd; ls -la; ...\"}"}
step/end          | {"turn":1,"step":1}
turn/end          | {"turn":1,"reason":{"kind":"error","error":{"message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')","code":"UNKNOWN"}}}

There is no tool/result event between tool/call and turn/end. The next turn in the same session then fails at request-build time with:
{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","failure":{"message":"An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'. (insufficient tool messages following tool_calls message)"}}
What we ruled out

Not plugin-related. Reproduced on a profile with every third-party plugin removed (only the default @deepseek-ai/dsh-base + @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app bundles), and separately with a heavier plugin set (including one, dsh-approval-gate, that hooks the approval/request waterfall) both enabled and disabled — the failure is identical in all cases.
Not version-specific to the dev branch. Reproduced on both the official npm 0.1.5-rc.2 release and a from-source build at tag dsh-v0.1.6-alpha.2.

Suspected root cause (unconfirmed)
Tracing packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts and packages/core/tools/src/index.ts in the source tree:

startCall() appends the tool/call event, then calls await ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec).
ToolRuntime.prepareScheduledExecution → prepareExecution wraps its tools/pre-execute waterfall and approval-ask flow in a try { ... } catch (error) { return next({ kind: 'final-result', ..., result: toolErrorResult(error) }) } — so an error thrown inside that block is caught and converted into a normal (if error-flavored) tool/result.
createExecution(), called just before that try, has its own guarded try/catch around argument snapshotting, but this.get(name, agent) / this.collapses(...) run before any try block.
Given the observed symptom — an uncaught error that skips straight to turn/end with no tool/result at all — the throw is most likely occurring outside both of those guarded regions, but we were not able to pin the exact call site before switching focus to isolating whether it was plugin-related.

We were unable to attach a debugger to the failing turn in a fully clean environment before filing this; happy to help gather a stack trace (e.g. by instrumenting the catch in agent-loop's turn() method) if a maintainer wants to pair on it.
Impact
Any conversation that hits this once is permanently broken and must be discarded. Since the triggering tool call can be as ordinary as an unprompted pwd; ls -la, this looks like it could affect a meaningful fraction of real sessions.

threads.title: Terminal "zsh" could not be ended: spawnSync /bin/ps EPERM inside macOS Seatbelt sandbox (nono)
threads.bodyText:
Environment

macOS Apple Silicon, zsh
nono v0.78.0 (nono run ... -- dsh ...)
@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local 0.1.6-alpha.2
Profile: web (dsh --profile web)

Symptom
Closing a zsh terminal in DSH Web UI fails with: Terminal "zsh" could not be ended: spawnSync /bin/ps EPERM. UI string is cleanupFailed in dsh-client-ui-sidebar-terminal/lib/client.js.
Root cause (verified)
packages/subprocess/subprocess-local hardcodes /bin/ps on darwin:

internals.exec = execFileSync (line 335)
macProcessTable(): internals.exec("/bin/ps", ["-axo", "pid=,ppid=,lstart="]) (line 620)
MacProcessInspector.foregroundPgid(): internals.exec("/bin/ps", ["-o", "tpgid=", "-p", pid]) (line 640)

On macOS /bin/ps is setuid root. Inside Seatbelt sandbox (sandbox_init, which nono uses — https://nono.sh/docs/cli/internals/seatbelt), kernel denies setuid exec (forbidden-exec-sugid) with EPERM. Repro: nono run --allow /tmp -- /bin/ps -o pid,comm -> exit 127 forbidden-exec-sugid. No --allow/--read/--bypass-protection grant can lift this; copying /bin/ps dies to code-signing (SIGKILL 137).
Ask

Can MacProcessInspector degrade gracefully on EPERM from ps (treat snapshot as incomplete, still kill known children / kill(-pgid) instead of fatal cleanupFailed)?
Or avoid /bin/ps on macOS (resolve ps via PATH, or libproc/sysctl)?
Any workaround besides running dsh outside sandbox? Happy to test patch / provide nono -vvv + Console.app logs.

threads.title: [Bug] Blank sessions disappear from session list when navigating to another session
threads.bodyText:
Description
When creating a new session (typing nothing into the composer) and then clicking on a different session in the session list, the new blank session disappears from the list. This is unexpected behavior from a UX perspective.
Steps to Reproduce

Open the DSH web interface
Click "New Session" to create a new session
Do NOT type anything in the composer (session remains blank)
Click on a different session in the session list to view past content
Observe that the new blank session disappears from the list

Expected Behavior
The new blank session should persist in the session list even when navigating to another session. Users should be able to switch between sessions without losing their new empty session.
Actual Behavior
The new blank session disappears from the session list when the user clicks on a different session.
Root Cause Analysis
The issue is in the sessionVisible function in packages/client/ui-workspace/src/client/WorkspaceBrowser.tsx:
function sessionVisible(session, current, archived) {
    return session.origin !== "subagent" && !archived.has(session.id) && (!session.blank || session.id === current);
}
The condition (!session.blank || session.id === current) means:

If the session is NOT blank, it's visible
If the session IS blank, it's only visible if it's the current session (the one in the main view)

This causes blank sessions to be filtered out when they are no longer the current session.
Suggested Fix
Modify the sessionVisible function to allow blank sessions to persist in the list:
function sessionVisible(session, current, archived) {
    return session.origin !== "subagent" && !archived.has(session.id);
}
This removes the blank session filtering, allowing all non-archived, non-subagent sessions to appear in the list.
Use Case
Users often create a new session and then want to quickly reference a previous session to copy something or check the last turn. The current behavior forces them to either:

Type something in the new session first (making it non-blank)
Accept that the new session will disappear when they navigate away

This is a common workflow that should be supported without requiring the user to "commit" to the new session by typing something.
Environment

DSH version: 0.1.6-alpha.2
Browser: Chrome
OS: macOS

Additional Context
The code comment says:
/**
 * Ordinary sessions are visible; among blank sessions, only the current one
 * is visible.
 */
While this design choice reduces clutter, it creates confusion for users who expect new sessions to persist in the list until explicitly deleted or archived.

threads.title: [Windows] workspace-write 沙箱下 tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() 失败：chmod 重写 DACL 抹掉 capability ACE
threads.bodyText:
Summary
（背景：我在一个 Python 测试套件里遇到这 37 个失败，定位过程中做的 mode 对照实验如下。）
在 Windows 的 workspace-write 沙箱下（@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl 后端），受限子进程无法使用 Python 标准库的 tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() / tempfile.mkdtemp()，持续抛 PermissionError: [WinError 5]。
目录创建和写入本身都成功，失败发生在退出清理时扫描该目录。
触发点是 tempfile.mkdtemp() 的 mode=0o700：沙箱给受限进程新建对象补的 capability ACE，被 chmod 重写 DACL 时抹掉，导致包括创建者在内的所有 restricting SID 都被 write pass-2 检查拒绝。
影响面：任何在 workspace-write 下用标准库 tempfile 的 Python 代码。实测一个 266 用例的测试套件中 37 个受影响（约 14%）。属于静默失败——目录创建和写入都正常，只有清理阶段报错，容易被误判为被测代码的缺陷。
Reproduction
在 workspace-write 受限会话中运行：
import tempfile, os
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:      # 退出时报 PermissionError
    open(os.path.join(t, "f.txt"), "w").write("x")   # 这一步成功
更小的隔离复现——同一受限进程内逐个 mode 测试：
import os
base = "D:/some/writable/dir"
os.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)
for mode in [0o777, 0o755, 0o750, 0o711, 0o700]:
    p = os.path.join(base, f"d{oct(mode)[2:]}")
    os.mkdir(p, mode)
    try:
        open(os.path.join(p, "f"), "w").write("x")
        print(f"{oct(mode)} OK")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{oct(mode)} {type(e).__name__}")
Current behavior
0o700 是唯一触发值：



mode
结果




0o777
OK


0o755
OK


0o750
OK


0o711
OK


0o700
PermissionError: [WinError 5]


0o500
OK



完整报错：
PermissionError: [WinError 5] 拒绝访问。:
  'C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\dsh-<hash>\\tmpXXXXXXXX'

栈落在 tempfile.py → shutil.rmtree → os.scandir → _resetperms → os.chmod。即扫描阶段先被拒，清理的重试路径再次被拒。
以下规避手段已实测全部无效：

重定向 TMP / TEMP / TMPDIR 到工作区或会话私有临时目录；
改用 tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=<可写目录>)。

说明问题不在路径，而在新建目录的 DACL。
补充观测：对失败目录执行 os.stat 报 mode 为 0o777（Windows 上 mode 位不反映真实 DACL），所以不能靠 mode 位判断。
Expected behavior
受限进程对自己创建的目录执行 chmod 后，应当仍可访问该目录；或至少该目录应保留 token default DACL 中的 capability ACE。
Environment

DSH 0.1.6-alpha.1，commit 0d1f50007f
Windows 11
权限预设 workspace-write（沙箱模式 workspace-write，审批 ask）
后端 @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl
Python 3.12.13（受限 pwsh 子进程内）

机制推测（未经直接验证，供定位参考）
packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/index.ts 第 284–296 行的注释说明：受限 token 的 default DACL 只含用户的环境 SID、不含任何 restricting SID；因此代码显式把某个 capability SID 的 full-access ACE 合并进 default DACL（setTokenDefaultDaclGrant），好让新建对象的 DACL 能通过 write pass-2 检查。
在此之上，CPython 的 os.mkdir(path, mode) 在 Windows 上当 mode != 0o777 时会额外执行一次 chmod 来设置权限位。这一次 chmod 重写了新建目录的 DACL，移除了上面那个 capability ACE，于是所有 restricting SID（含创建者自己）都被 pass-2 拒绝。
这一推断能同时解释：只有 0o700 失败（Python 单独为它走 chmod 路径）、重定向临时目录无效（问题在 DACL 不在路径）、以及 stat 报 0o777。
未验证部分：os.mkdir 的 chmod 行为是从 CPython 设计推断的（其 C 实现无法用 inspect 读源码），未在 DSH 内打断点确认。若上游采纳，建议先复核这一步。
建议方向
在 setTokenDefaultDaclGrant 之后，考虑对受限进程新建对象的 DACL 修改保持宽容；或至少让 chmod 不再整体替换 DACL。具体取舍取决于对 pass-2 收紧程度的期望。

threads.title: mcp-client: one unsupported tool inputSchema keyword rejects the entire MCP server (Playwright MCP registers zero tools)
ACP initialize advertises no image prompts because the profile pins text-only deepseek-v4-flash
threads.bodyText:
Summary
dsh --profile acp advertises agentCapabilities.promptCapabilities.image: false, because the shipped ACP bundle pins model: deepseek-v4-flash, which the DeepSeek adapter catalog resolves as text-only. The image-capable deepseek-flash (V4.1 Flash) is offered through session/new / session/set_config_option, but the bridge computes its image capability once at initialize from the profile's static route, and the same value gates session/prompt. An ACP client therefore cannot send images even on a session that selects deepseek-flash.
Versions

@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.5-rc.2 (current latest / next)
Same pin present in @deepseek-ai/dsh-acp-app@0.1.6-alpha.2
macOS arm64

Reproduction

Start dsh --profile acp.
Send initialize (protocolVersion: 1).
Read result.agentCapabilities.promptCapabilities:

{ "image": false, "audio": false, "embeddedContext": false }
After session/new, selecting deepseek-flash with session/set_config_option and then sending an inline image block is rejected with inline image prompts were not advertised by this connection.
Where it comes from


packages/bundle/acp-app/cordis.patch.yml pins the ACP row:
- id: acp
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-acp'
  config:
    provider: deepseek-official
    model: deepseek-v4-flash


packages/acp/acp/src/content.ts — supportsAcpImagePrompts(ctx, config.provider, config.model) returns true only when resolveModelInfo(provider, model).inputModalities includes image.


packages/llm/llm-deepseek — the default catalog declares deepseek-flash with inputModalities: ["text", "image"], while deepseek-v4-flash has no inputModalities and defaults to ["text"]; unlisted ids also pass through as text-only.


packages/acp/acp/src/index.ts — imagePromptEnabled = await supportsAcpImagePrompts(...) is computed in initialize, advertised there, and passed to record.prompt(...), so the connection-level value also gates prompt admission.


The DeepSeek API still routes the legacy deepseek-v4-flash name to V4.1 Flash, so the model itself works; only the local catalog treats that id as text-only, which makes the otherwise-truthful capability check report false.
Impact
Any ACP client (Zed, Relay, scripted controllers) sees image: false and refuses or drops image prompts, even though V4.1 Flash is natively multimodal and the same client can select deepseek-flash in the session's model options.
Suggested fixes

Point packages/bundle/acp-app/cordis.patch.yml at model: deepseek-flash (the current image-capable id). That alone makes the default deployment's initialize truthful.
Optionally, let the capability follow the session's selected route — recompute it for session/new / set_config_option, or stop gating session/prompt on the initialize-time value when assertImageRoute already rechecks the exact route.

Workaround for clients today
dsh accepts --patch overlays applied after the profile layer, so a client can route the row without touching the publisher's files:
dsh --profile acp --patch ./deepseek-images.yml
- id: acp
  config:
    provider: deepseek-official
    model: deepseek-flash
Verified here: initialize returns image: true with the overlay and image: false without it.
Related: #4943.

npm error code ETARGET

Reproduced on Windows and in a clean Linux environment (Node 22.22.2, npm 10.9.7), registry: https://registry.npmjs.org

The 0.1.5-rc.3 release set was published at 2026-09-22T05:55Z.
@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app@0.1.5-rc.3 depends on @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview@^0.1.5-rc.3.

npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@alpha (0.1.7-alpha.1) resolves correctly.
Local install with "overrides": { "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app": "0.1.5-rc.2" } also resolves.

Publish @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview@0.1.5-rc.3, or deprecate @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app@0.1.5-rc.3.
Possibly the same class of issue as #3461 (rc.8 missing dsh-agent-loop). A CI check that verifies every package in a release set is published before tagging might prevent this.

threads.title: [0.1.7-alpha.1 regression] dsh-http-proxy undici v8 dispatcher breaks content-encoding on internal undici v6 fetch
threads.bodyText:
Symptom (starting from 0.1.7-alpha.1)
The version-update panel (dsh-version-update@1.4.0) always reports:
registry unreachable (tried https://registry.npmjs.org, https://registry.npmmirror.com):
Unexpected token U+001F ... is not valid JSON

Bytes 1F 8B 08 are a gzip header: the body arrives undecoded despite HTTP 200.
Same failure hits the plugin's GitHub release-notes fetch, so it is host-global,
not registry-specific. curl and a fresh node process (same URL/headers/timeout,
same proxy or direct) both work. Only the dsh web host fails, deterministically,
across restarts, with or without proxy env vars.
Root cause
profile-boot calls installProxyFromEnvironment() from @deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy,
which replaces the global dispatcher with one built from bundled npm undici@8.11.0
(Agent factory returning ProxyAgent / Pool). But Node v22.22.2 built-in fetch runs
internal undici 6.24.1. The cross-major dispatcher breaks content-encoding propagation.
Minimal repro (same node binary, internal undici 6.24.1):
const u8 = await import('<global-dsh>/node_modules/undici/index.js'); // 8.11.0
const disp = new u8.Agent({
  factory: (origin, opts) => new u8.ProxyAgent({ ...opts, uri: 'http://127.0.0.1:7890' }),
});
u8.setGlobalDispatcher(disp);
const r = await fetch('https://registry.npmjs.org/%40deepseek-ai%2Fdsh',
  { headers: { accept: 'application/vnd.npm.install-v1+json' } });
console.log(r.headers.get('content-encoding')); // null, header lost
await r.json(); // throws Unexpected token U+001F ... is not valid JSON

With the pristine internal dispatcher (or the same experiment using undici@7.29.0
classes), content-encoding br/gzip is present and r.json() parses. So the
v8-dispatcher + v6-fetch combination is the breaking one.
Environment

@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.7-alpha.1 (global npm install)
node v22.22.2 (process.versions.undici = 6.24.1)
bundled node_modules/undici = 8.11.0
dsh-version-update 1.4.0 (symptom surface only)

Suggested fix
Build the global dispatcher from an undici compatible with the runtime internal one
(or reuse the internal instance), or skip overriding the global dispatcher when the
bundled undici major differs from the runtime. Note: with no proxy configured
(source none) nothing is installed and everything works, confirming the dispatcher
is the trigger.
Workaround
Launch with proxy env fully unset so no dispatcher gets installed:
env -u http_proxy -u https_proxy -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u all_proxy \
    -u ALL_PROXY -u no_proxy -u NO_PROXY -u npm_config_proxy \
    -u npm_config_https_proxy -u npm_config_http_proxy -u NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY dsh web

Unsetting only http(s)_proxy is NOT enough: any leftover name (e.g. ALL_PROXY)
still triggers installation.

Windows Desktop: LibreOfficeKit 在长路径下转换失败，短路径 Junction 可正常通过
threads.bodyText:
环境

OS: Windows
deepseek-harness tag: dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1
Desktop target: win32-x64
Electron: 44.0.0
electron-builder: 26.15.3
bundled Node.js: 24.18.1
bundled pnpm: 11.7.0

源码目录：
C:\PROJETS-PERSO\deepseek-harness

构建命令：
pnpm.cmd run package:desktop:win:x64:unsigned

问题现象
Prepared runtime 的 Office 转换测试可以通过：
desktop runtime: DOCX, XLSX, PPTX to PDF passed

但 packaged runtime 在 DOCX -> PDF 时失败：
Error: desktop runtime: docx conversion failed: OfficeToPdfError: LibreOffice conversion failed.

[cause]: ConversionError:
LibreOffice native conversion failed: Unknown LibreOfficeKit exception

失败发生在：
@deepseek-ai/libreoffice-kit
runNative()


隔离测试
为了确认问题来源，我做了以下组合测试：
A. prepared dsh root + prepared Electron + prepared runtime
   PASS

B. packaged dsh root + packaged EXE + packaged runtime
   FAIL

C. packaged dsh root + prepared Electron + packaged runtime
   FAIL

D. prepared dsh root + packaged EXE + prepared runtime
   PASS

E. packaged dsh root + prepared Electron + prepared runtime
   FAIL

F. prepared dsh root + prepared Electron + packaged runtime
   PASS

结果非常稳定：
prepared dsh root  -> PASS
packaged dsh root  -> FAIL

因此决定结果的因素是 dsh root 本身，而不是：
Electron executable
bundled runtime


已排除 native package 内容差异
比较以下两个目录：
Prepared:

apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

Packaged:

apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

比较结果：
file count identical
file size identical
per-file SHA-256 identical

因此可以排除：
electron-builder 漏文件
electron-builder 修改了 LibreOfficeKit native package
native package 内容损坏


已排除 app.asar 虚拟路径直接传给 native helper
最初怀疑 require.resolve() 在 Electron 中返回了：
...\resources\app.asar\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

然后这个虚拟路径被传给 native helper。
但实际运行时打印出的路径是：
executable =
C:\PROJETS-PERSO\deepseek-harness\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64\bin\libreoffice-kit.exe

programDirectory =
C:\PROJETS-PERSO\deepseek-harness\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64\program\program

root =
C:\PROJETS-PERSO\deepseek-harness\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

所以最终传给 native helper 的路径已经是：
app.asar.unpacked

对应的真实物理路径。
不是：
app.asar

虚拟路径。

路径长度统计
对 LibreOfficeKit engine 的完整绝对路径进行统计后，发现 prepared 和 packaged 的差异很大。
大致结果：
prepared engine longest path: ~218 characters
packaged engine longest path: ~278 characters
packaged engine files >= 260 characters: ~706

packaged engine root：
C:\PROJETS-PERSO\deepseek-harness\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

其中 libreoffice-kit.exe 本身仍然可以正常启动，所以并不是 executable path 直接无法访问。
但 LibreOfficeKit 初始化以及实际文档转换过程中，还会继续访问：
program\program\...
program\share\...

以及其它更深层资源。
因此内部实际访问路径会比 programDirectory 本身更长。

决定性 A/B 测试
为了确认是否与路径长度有关，我没有修改 packaged LibreOfficeKit native package 的任何文件。
而是将完全相同的 packaged engine 通过 Windows Junction 映射到短路径：
C:\lo-test

例如：
New-Item -ItemType Junction `
  -Path 'C:\lo-test' `
  -Target 'C:\PROJETS-PERSO\deepseek-harness\apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64'
然后让 runtime 使用：
executable:
C:\lo-test\bin\libreoffice-kit.exe

programDirectory:
C:\lo-test\program\program

其它条件保持不变：
same packaged engine
same files
same SHA-256
same runtime
same Electron
same smoke test
same input/output/profile logic

结果：
desktop runtime: DOCX, XLSX, PPTX to PDF passed

也就是说：
Same packaged engine
Same files
Same SHA-256
Same smoke test

Long physical path -> FAIL
C:\lo-test         -> PASS

这个结果目前是最有判别力的证据。

当前判断
目前看起来，问题高度集中在 Windows 下 LibreOfficeKit / LibreOffice 内部对长路径的处理。
Native helper 本身可以正常启动，但 LibreOffice 初始化、Writer/filter/config/resource 加载过程中会访问更深层的资源路径。
当完整绝对路径过长时，某个内部 Windows API 或 LibreOffice 组件可能无法正常处理，最终 native helper 只返回：
Unknown LibreOfficeKit exception

所以表面看起来像 LibreOfficeKit 初始化异常，但实际可能是内部资源路径访问失败。

为什么 prepared runtime 正常，而 packaged runtime 失败
Prepared engine 路径较短：
...\targets\win-x64\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

Packaged engine 路径明显更深：
...\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

两份 native package 内容完全一致。
真正发生变化的是：
physical absolute path depth

这也与前面的 A-F cross test 完全一致：
prepared dsh root  -> PASS
packaged dsh root  -> FAIL


建议修复方向
可以考虑让 Windows Desktop packaging 将 LibreOfficeKit native engine 放到更浅的物理目录，例如：
resources\lo

或者：
resources\lok

而不是当前的：
resources\app.asar.unpacked\dsh\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\libreoffice-kit-win32-x64

然后让 @deepseek-ai/libreoffice-kit 或 Desktop runtime 显式使用这个 native engine physical path。
例如目标结构可以类似：
resources\
  lok\
    bin\
    program\

而不是：
resources\
  app.asar.unpacked\
    dsh\
      node_modules\
        @deepseek-ai\
          libreoffice-kit-win32-x64\

这样可以显著降低 Windows 下 LibreOfficeKit 内部资源的完整绝对路径长度。
相比要求用户启用 Windows long-path system setting，这种方式可能更可靠，因为 LibreOffice 及其依赖组件未必全部使用支持 long path 的 Windows API。

其它已做的检查
当前已经检查或排除：
- prepared / packaged native package file count
- file size
- per-file SHA-256
- Electron executable
- bundled runtime
- app.asar virtual path
- app.asar.unpacked native path
- native helper executable path
- programDirectory

最终只有：
long physical path -> FAIL
short Junction path -> PASS

可以稳定改变结果。

threads.title: 【Bug】已完成的轮次被整体折叠，隐藏前面轮次的助手正文，造成"内容被截断"的错误认知
threads.bodyText:
环境

包：@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.7-alpha.1（npm 安装版）
插件：@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-chat@0.1.7-alpha.1
系统：Windows

问题描述（核心）
一个轮次结束后，该轮次的助手正文会被整体折叠隐藏，只剩下最后一轮可见。
当一次交付内容跨多个助手轮次时（例如先给出主体，再补充若干块），用户只能看到最后一轮，
因而会合理地认为那就是完整的交付物，误以为其余内容被截断或丢失。
这是信息完整性问题，不是显示偏好问题：任何展示档位、任何折叠策略，
都不应该让用户无法察觉"前面还有内容"。
影响

用户产生"内容被截断"的错误判断，据此做出错误决策（例如以为评审报告只有最后一小段）。
内容实际存在却不可见，与"内容确实缺失"在界面上无法区分。
属于静默失败：没有提示、没有计数、没有"还有 N 段内容"的指示。

复现步骤

让助手产生一段跨多个轮次的交付内容（先主体、后补充）
待较早的轮次结束（turnClosed）
观察：较早轮次的助手正文被折叠隐藏，界面只展示最后一轮
结果：用户以为最后一轮即为完整交付物

该行为与「工作过程展示」设置无关：compact / detailed / expanded 三档下均会发生。
（即使用户把该设置调成「完全展开」，前面的轮次依然被折叠。）
根因定位
三档展示策略中，foldCompletedTurns 全部硬编码为 true，不存在任何可关闭它的档位或设置项。
packages/client/ui-chat → 构建产物 lib/client.js，源区域 lib/types/client/presentation-policy.js
（以下行号为 npm 打包后 lib/client.js 的行号）：
// client.js:11474-11496
const POLICIES = {
  compact:  { mode: "compact",  foldCompletedTurns: true, stepGrouping: "collapsed", liveProcessDetail: false, settledReasoningPreview: false },
  detailed: { mode: "detailed", foldCompletedTurns: true, stepGrouping: "collapsed", liveProcessDetail: true,  settledReasoningPreview: true  },
  expanded: { mode: "expanded", foldCompletedTurns: true, stepGrouping: "none",      liveProcessDetail: true,  settledReasoningPreview: true  }
};
折叠判定（把已完成轮次整体隐藏）：
// client.js:1975
const outerHidden = foldCompleted && presentation?.turnClosed === true && spec !== void 0
                    && !alwaysOpen && stored?.answerStep !== (spec.answerStep ?? 0);
另一处相关消费点：
// client.js:1638-1643
const foldCompleted = usePresentation((policy) => policy.foldCompletedTurns);
const processWindowReady = processSpec !== void 0 && processPresentation !== void 0 && foldCompleted && ...;
建议
1. 区分"工具/过程信息"与"交付内容"（核心修复方向）
折叠过程信息（工具调用、推理步骤）是合理的；但不应折叠助手面向用户的正文。
建议让 foldCompletedTurns 只作用于过程性节点，不作用于用户可读的助手消息内容。
2. 若确实需要折叠，必须提供"还有内容"的可感知指示
至少满足其一，避免静默丢失：

折叠处显示可见摘要或计数（如"前面还有 2 段回复"），而不是完全隐藏；
或在界面明确提示被折叠的轮次数，让用户知道内容存在。

3. 至少不要让「完全展开」档仍然折叠
在完成 1 或 2 之前，expanded 档应将 foldCompletedTurns 置为 false，
使该档位名副其实，作为用户的临时规避手段：
expanded: {
  mode: "expanded",
  foldCompletedTurns: false,   // 原为 true
  stepGrouping: "none",
  liveProcessDetail: true,
  settledReasoningPreview: true
}
备注

行号为 npm 包内 lib/client.js 的行号，非源码行号；源文件路径依据该 bundle 内嵌的
//#region 标记与构建元数据（/home/runner/work/deepseek-harness/deepseek-harness/...）推断。
建议按符号名 foldCompletedTurns / outerHidden 搜索定位。
临时绕过：点击已折叠轮次上的「工作过程」折叠条可展开，展开状态会被记录、刷新后保持。
但用户必须先意识到"内容被折叠了"才会去点——这正是本 issue 要解决的问题。
无关项说明：工具结果的 JSON 另有独立的字符上限截断（client.js:366-368，MAX_CHARS），
不作用于助手消息正文，与本 issue 无关。

threads.title: BUg
[BUG] Code block copy button fails with execCommand error; manual selection escapes block when overflow is active
threads.bodyText:
Description
To the DeepSeek Development Team,
I am reporting two related defects in the code block component of the web chat interface, plus one optional suggestion.

Bug 1: "Copy" button fails with document.execCommand warning
Steps to reproduce

Open a chat with a code block.
Click the "Копировать" (Copy) button in the code block banner.
Open DevTools (F12) → Console tab.

Actual behavior
The following warning appears in the console:
document.execCommand('cut'/'copy') was denied because it was not called from inside a short running user-generated event handler.

The code is not copied to the clipboard.
Expected behavior
The code should be copied to the clipboard without errors.
Suspected root cause
The site appears to use document.execCommand('copy') as a fallback inside an asynchronous handler (e.g., after navigator.clipboard.writeText() throws). Modern browsers block execCommand('copy') when it is not called synchronously within a user gesture — this is standard security behavior, not a Firefox-specific issue.
The fix is to remove the asynchronous fallback and rely solely on navigator.clipboard.writeText(), which returns a Promise and works correctly with async code.
See also: related issue #1494, which describes the opposite scenario (the execCommand fallback is never reached because navigator.clipboard.writeText() is permission-denied and the catch block returns early).

Bug 2: Manual selection of code blocks escapes the block when overflow is active
Condition
The bug manifests only when overflow is active in the code block — that is, when content exceeds the block's dimensions and a scrollbar appears (either horizontal or vertical). When the code is short enough not to cause overflow, selection works correctly.
Steps to reproduce

Open a chat with a code block containing enough content to cause overflow (long lines or many lines).
Start selecting the code from the left padding area of the block (the empty space between the left border and the first character).
Drag the mouse to the right or left.

Actual behavior
When the selection starts in the padding area, the selection root is escalated above the <pre> element. Dragging the mouse then selects the entire page (or the entire message block) instead of just the code. When the cursor passes over whitespace text nodes between <span> elements inside the code, the same escalation occurs temporarily.
Expected behavior
Selection should remain constrained to the code block.
Root cause
The <pre> element has overflow: auto applied via .ds-markdown pre. This turns <pre> into a scroll container. When the selection anchor is resolved in the padding area (where there is no text), the browser cannot find a valid text position inside the scroll container and escalates the selection root to the nearest non-clipping ancestor. Without overflow: auto, the anchor is correctly resolved to the beginning of the first text line inside <pre>.
Evidence

Disabling overflow: auto on <pre> in DevTools eliminates the problem entirely.
Relevant CSS:

.md-code-block > pre {
  padding: 16px;
  margin: 0 !important;
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  word-break: break-all;
}

.ds-markdown pre {
  overflow: auto;
  margin: 16px 0;
}
Additional observation (not a reproduction step)
If the code was previously selected in full, the bug tends to manifest more frequently. This may be a browser-specific behavior, and I cannot claim it is a reliable reproduction method — providing it as an observation only.
Suggested fix
Move overflow: auto from <pre> to the parent container (.md-code-block or an inner wrapper). This preserves horizontal scrolling for long lines while keeping <pre> as a normal block element, so selection anchors resolve correctly.

Optional suggestion: setting to disable internal scroll in code blocks
This suggestion is not directly related to the bugs described above and is not part of the request to fix them. Whether to implement it is entirely at the developers' discretion.
Some users (myself included) prefer the page to scroll as a whole rather than having nested scroll containers inside code blocks. Nested scrollbars can also cause the browser to scroll the code block instead of the page when the mouse wheel is used over it.
I propose adding a user setting (e.g., in interface settings) to disable internal scrolling in code blocks. When disabled, long lines would rely on the existing white-space: pre-wrap behavior and wrap naturally. This setting exists in some other AI chat interfaces, so there is precedent for it being a useful option.

Summary (for maintainers)

Environment: Firefox 128.3.1esr (64-bit), Linux, X11
Reproduce: See steps in each bug section above.
Impact:

Bug 1: Copy button is completely non-functional for all users.
Bug 2: Manual selection of code blocks is broken when overflow is active, making it difficult to copy code by hand.


Evidence: DevTools console warning (Bug 1), relevant CSS (Bug 2), and observation that disabling overflow: auto resolves the issue.

Note: The manual selection issue is not browser-specific; it stems from the interaction between overflow: auto on <pre> and the browser's selection anchor resolution algorithm. The execCommand warning is also browser-agnostic and is the browser correctly enforcing the user-gesture requirement for clipboard writes.

Thank you for your attention to these issues. The DeepSeek web interface is otherwise the highest-quality AI chat UI I have used.

threads.title: 对话框没有了
源代码编译0.1.7失败
Windows: workspace-write sandbox fails with SetNamedSecurityInfoW Win32 5 when the workspace directory DACL lacks WRITE_OWNER
threads.bodyText:
Status (2026-09-26): still reproduces on the newest published version, 0.1.7-rc.2.
This post is the consolidated report — environment → reproduction → root cause → implemented fix → the policy decision we are asking for — so the thread does not have to be reassembled from the long comments below. Everything is measured on one machine unless explicitly marked as analysis; the artifact comparisons and command transcripts are reproducible from the text.

1. Environment

Windows 11 IoT Enterprise 26H2 (build 26300.9267), normal (non-elevated) user account
dsh tested on: 0.1.6-alpha.2, 0.1.7-alpha.1, 0.1.7-alpha.2, 0.1.7-rc.1, 0.1.7-rc.2 (current baseline; published 2026-09-24T14:18:11Z)
Two-node install (D:\DeepSeek\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\*), profile web; workspace on a data drive: D:\<workspace> — i.e. a volume whose inherited template does not grant the caller WRITE_OWNER (see §3.3)

2. Reproduction
Under the workspace-write file policy, every PowerShell (and bash) invocation fails before the child process is created:
Error: SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5): grantWrite(D:\<workspace>)

Win32 5 is ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. The sandbox is fail-closed, so no child is ever spawned. File tools (read/glob/grep/write/edit) and MCP tools are unaffected; danger-full-access also works.
A minimal probe (must run from an unconfined shell — see the note at the end of this section):
// node probe.mjs <workspaceDir>
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import fs from 'node:fs'; import path from 'node:path'; import os from 'node:os';
const ws = process.argv[2];
const tmp = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'probe-tmp');
fs.mkdirSync(tmp, { recursive: true });
const { AclSandbox, workspaceWriteSid, tempWriteSid } =
  await import(pathToFileURL('D:\\DeepSeek\\node_modules\\@deepseek-ai\\dsh-sandbox-windows-acl\\lib\\index.js').href);
const sb = new AclSandbox({
  writableDirs: [ws], tempDir: tmp,
  writeSid: workspaceWriteSid(ws), tempWriteSid: tempWriteSid(tmp),
  mode: 'workspace-write',
});
await sb.init();   // throws Win32 5 here while the DACL lacks WRITE_OWNER
const r = await sb.spawn({ command: 'cmd.exe', args: ['/c', 'echo ok'], cwd: ws }).wait();
console.log(r.exitCode, r.stdout.toString().trim());
sb.dispose();
Measured on the installed 0.1.7-rc.2, fresh directories, one variable (the target directory's effective ACL):



Target directory (freshly created)
Effective ACL template
init() + spawn()




D:\<probe> (non-profile volume)
Authenticated Users:(I)(M) — no WRITE_OWNER
❌ SetNamedSecurityInfoW failed (Win32 5)


the same directory after icacls "<dir>" /grant "<user>:(OI)(CI)(WO)"
caller holds WRITE_OWNER
✅ spawn OK (probe-ok)


C:\Users\<user>\<probe>
explicit <user>:(I)(OI)(CI)(F)
✅ spawn OK



icacls also shows the label layer directly: directories provisioned by 0.1.6-alpha.2 carry no Mandatory Label; those provisioned by 0.1.7+ carry Low Mandatory Level:(OI)(CI)(NW).

The probe must run unconfined: inside a confined child the restricted token's capability ACE grants only W,D,DC and deliberately omits WRITE_OWNER (otherwise a confined child could re-grant itself), so any ACL-provisioning attempt from inside the sandbox fails regardless of the target.

3. Root cause
3.1 The code change
0.1.7-alpha.1 extends every write grant with a Low mandatory integrity label: new symbols buildLowLabelAcl, hasExactLabel, addMandatoryAce (zero occurrences in 0.1.6-alpha.2), and
api.setNamedSecurityInfoW(path, 1, labelEdit.kind === "keep" ? 4 : 20, null, null, newAcl, labelEdit.kind === "apply" ? labelEdit.acl : null)
i.e. SecurityInfo went from 4 (DACL) to 20 (DACL | SACL); the read side changed the same way (getNamedSecurityInfoW(..., DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION | LABEL_SECURITY_INFORMATION, ...)). DACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION | LABEL_SECURITY_INFORMATION is 4 | 16 = 20, and LABEL_SECURITY_INFORMATION is the same bit as SACL_SECURITY_INFORMATION.
3.2 The precondition this creates
The label lives in the object's SACL, and the package's own README (packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/README.md:122, Verified boundaries) states the resulting requirement — quoted verbatim, as suggested in the thread:

Granted directories must be caller-owned and grant WRITE_OWNER — the owner's implicit rights cover only READ_CONTROL and WRITE_DAC; the label lives in the SACL, so the combined apply additionally needs WRITE_OWNER (a Full-control directory, the normal workspace case, has it). A directory whose DACL grants only Modify now fails the grant loudly instead of silently skipping the confinement.

src/acl.ts:368 repeats it as a code comment ("The directory must be owned by the caller AND grant WRITE_OWNER"), and src/win32-abi.ts:25 confirms WRITE_DAC/WRITE_OWNER are deliberately withheld from the confined child. So this is a written precondition, not an oversight, and "fails loudly" is intentional.
3.3 Why neither depth nor ownership is the discriminator
On NTFS a non-profile volume root's default template is Authenticated Users:(M) (Modify) plus an inherit-only copy of the same, together with Users:(RX); none of those carries WRITE_OWNER. Because they are inheritable, every directory on that volume inherits exactly this template at any depth — intermediate directories only ever inherit or narrow, never widen.
Measured effective WRITE_OWNER for the caller (computed from the non-inherit-only ACEs applicable to the caller's token groups — user / Authenticated Users / Users / Everyone / INTERACTIVE):



Path
Levels below the volume root
Owner
WRITE_OWNER




D:\
0
SYSTEM
❌


D:\DeepSeek
1
user
❌


D:\<workspace>
2
user
❌ (before the fix)


D:\AI Model\Work Date\Pi Lite Agent
3
user
❌


C:\Users\<user>
—
SYSTEM
✅ (created with an explicit <user>: FullControl ACE)


C:\Users\<user>\Documents, …\AppData\Local\Temp
—
user
✅ (inherited)



⇒ The condition is "no directory on the inheritance chain grants the caller WRITE_OWNER", not "the workspace sits at a drive root". A workspace on a non-profile volume is affected no matter how deep it is; a workspace under the user profile is fine at any depth. The grant root here is caller-owned — the README's rule is a conjunction and this directory satisfies the first half while failing only the second, which is also why "change the owner" is not a remedy in this case.
3.4 Version scope: the implementation is byte-identical from alpha.1 through rc.2

lib/types-DxezulnA.js is 61058 bytes with SHA-256 e6014e930810e6a6699feb78e6195a8180876cd9e99c2e74325e14c4807e0098 in all four of alpha.1, alpha.2, rc.1, rc.2.
npm pack @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl@0.1.7-rc.2 extracted and compared against the installed tree: 18 files, 0 differences. For alpha.1 vs alpha.2 the same comparison over the whole @deepseek-ai/* tree (267 packages, npm-cache tarballs verified against their recorded integrity) showed the sandbox packages differ only in package.json.
Commit level: between dsh-v0.1.7-rc.1 (46a7f68b09) and dsh-v0.1.7-rc.2 (477b4f4205), the only change inside packages/sandbox/ is four package.json files; in sandbox-windows-acl specifically, only package.json. (Note for anyone re-checking: the compare API truncates its file list at 300 entries, so query commits by path rather than trusting that list alone.)
The rc.1 and rc.2 release notes contain no sandbox/ACL/permission entry.

⇒ Whatever changed between those releases, it was not this grant path — the failure cannot be fixed by upgrading within the 0.1.7 line as it stands.
3.5 "First provision only" — and why an upgrade cannot self-heal
Verified: a directory provisioned once (with WRITE_OWNER present), then with inheritance disabled and the WRITE_OWNER ACE removed while the path-derived capability ACE, the world-SID deny and the exact Low label remain, succeeds on a second init(). The documented exact-ACE / exact-deny / exact-label skip performs no label write and therefore needs no WRITE_OWNER.
But that exemption does not cover anyone upgrading into 0.1.7 (credit to @xuhuanhello for the field data, and it follows from the skip predicate): a workspace provisioned by 0.1.6 has the standing capability ACE but no label, and the missing element is precisely the one whose write needs WRITE_OWNER — so the skip can never trigger. The breakage therefore lands on the first confined command after the upgrade, on any affected volume. (An earlier version of this post said the requirement was "first provision only" without that qualifier; the correct scope is "first provision of an already-labelled directory".)
4. Impact

workspace-write is unusable for any workspace whose grant root does not grant the caller WRITE_OWNER — in practice every workspace on a non-profile volume (any project kept on a data drive). Moving the workspace deeper does not help.
There is no fallback rung on Windows, and the error is not actionable: a bare Win32 5, with no mention of WRITE_OWNER and no remedy.
The sandbox cannot self-heal even though it could — the caller is the owner and already holds implicit WRITE_DAC.
The failure is invisible at boot: the block itself says "The win32 chain is a sole candidate, so the product never probes", and even when defaultProbeWindowsAcl runs it executes in read-only mode (zero grants, no ACL mutation) around cmd /c exit 0, so it never exercises the label write. Neither path can detect such a workspace; the breakage surfaces on the first real command.

5. Implemented fix (contributed by @zp-home) and an independent check
5.1 What it does
On SetNamedSecurityInfoW returning Win32 5, fall back once: read the directory's current owner, use the owner's implicit WRITE_DAC to add an inheritable WRITE_OWNER ACE for that owner via a DACL-only merge (labelEdit: 'keep' — the label is not touched), then retry the original grant once. If the directory is not owned by the caller, adding that ACE fails and the original error is rethrown with nothing changed. The label write stays as-is, so confinement is not weakened. Per its author it ships as a downstream patch and was verified on Windows 11 across several scenarios.
5.2 The boundary holds in the state that fix produces
I did not build the patch; I reproduced the ACL state it produces (icacls "<dir>" /grant "<user>:(OI)(CI)(WO)" is the same effective edit) and then attacked that state from inside a real confined child on 0.1.7-rc.2:



Attempt from the confined child
Result




child integrity level (whoami /groups)
S-1-16-4096 (Low)


read / write inside the granted root
allowed


write to a sibling directory outside the root
no file created


icacls <root> /setintegritylevel Medium (rewrite the label)
Access is denied.


icacls <root> /grant *S-1-1-0:(OI)(CI)F (grant itself more)
Access is denied.


takeown /f <root>
ERROR: … does not have ownership privileges


icacls <root> /reset /t /c /q (strip the sandbox ACEs)
Access is denied.


ACL / label / capability ACE afterwards
unchanged (icacls output identical; Low Mandatory Level:(OI)(CI)(NW) and the S-1-4-… ACE still present)



So the concern that self-healing widens the boundary does not materialise here: the added ACE names the caller's own SID, which never appears in the restricted token's pass-2 list, while the element the grant actually needs is the label write — which the child still cannot perform.
5.3 On README :175 (NULL-DACL) — analysis, not measurement
:175 warns that a NULL-DACL directory is not identity-preserving across a grant+revoke round trip (NULL → empty/deny-all DACL), and notes that real workspace and temp directories carry real DACLs. The self-heal path should not be able to reach that edge, for two reasons: (a) it only runs after ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, whereas a NULL DACL means "everyone full control", so the original apply would succeed and the fallback is unreachable; (b) :175 is about the revoke round trip (dispose()), while the fallback only ever adds an ACE and never revokes. I have not constructed a NULL-DACL directory to test this; it is reasoning from the defined semantics.
5.4 Stated limits
One machine, one account, a directory I created; the resulting state was emulated with icacls, not produced by the author's code; the upstream test suite was not run. Byte-level identity of the implementation was verified on released artifacts, not on the source branch as it moves.
6. The policy decision we are asking for
The current behaviour is a deliberate "fail loudly rather than silently skip confinement". The ask is therefore a policy question, not a bug-versus-feature argument:

Keep loud failure as the default, but add the one-shot self-heal as a fallback for the first provision of a grant root whose owner is the caller — and log it explicitly (e.g. "grant root self-healed: added WRITE_OWNER for <owner> on <path>"), so users and maintainers can see that it happened.
If self-healing is declined, at minimum make the error actionable: name the missing right and print the exact remedy, e.g. "workspace DACL does not grant WRITE_OWNER, which the mandatory label requires; run icacls <ws> /grant %USERNAME%:(OI)(CI)(WO)".
Documentation: the Modes / Verified boundaries wording "a Full-control directory, the normal workspace case" does not hold for workspaces outside the user profile; please state the requirement for data-drive workspaces explicitly.
Boot-time visibility: exercise the label path in the functional probe (rather than read-only/zero-grant), or mark the rung unavailable, so the condition is reported once at startup instead of on every command.

7. Workaround (verified on 0.1.7-rc.2)
icacls "<workspace>" /grant "%USERNAME%:(OI)(CI)(WO)"     # only WRITE_OWNER, minimal
# rollback:
icacls "<workspace>" /remove:g "%USERNAME%"
After this, init() and confined spawns succeed and the boundary still holds (writes inside succeed, writes outside are denied). The documented standing-Low-label cost applies as usual: the workspace keeps an inheritable Low Mandatory Level label, so other Low-integrity processes of the same user can write inside it.
Correction carried over from an earlier analysis of mine: I first blamed a missing SeSecurityPrivilege, because .NET's Get-Acl -Audit throws PrivilegeNotHeldException. A native GetNamedSecurityInfoW with DACL | SACL returns success and a SACL on this host, so reading the label is not what fails — the SACL write is, and that is governed by WRITE_OWNER on the object, not by a token privilege.

中文摘要

状态：最新发布版 0.1.7-rc.2 上仍然复现。基线与证据均按 rc.2 给出。
根因：0.1.7 起每次写授权都要写 SACL 里的 Low 完整性标签（SecurityInfo 由 4 变 20），因此要求授权根目录的 DACL 给调用者 WRITE_OWNER（README:122 明写的前提）；WRITE_OWNER 缺失即 Win32 5，且沙箱 fail-closed ⇒ workspace-write 全域不可用。
触发面：判据是"继承链上没有任何目录给调用者 WRITE_OWNER"，与目录深度无关；非系统盘（数据盘）上的工作区一律中招，用户配置目录下则正常。本报告的目录属主就是调用者，缺的只是一条授予 WRITE_OWNER 的 ACE。
版本关系：alpha.1 → alpha.2 → rc.1 → rc.2 该包实现逐字节相同（同一 bundle 哈希；rc.2 与已装树 18/18 文件零差异；rc.1→rc.2 只有 package.json 变化）⇒ 升级到 0.1.7 系列不会修好它；而且升级无法自愈（0.1.6 留下的工作区有 capability ACE 但没有标签，跳过分支永不触发 ⇒ 升级后第一条受限命令就会挂）。
已实现的补丁（@zp-home）：Win32 5 时读 owner → 用属主隐式 WRITE_DAC 补一条可继承的 WRITE_OWNER（只改 DACL、不碰标签）→ 重试一次。我独立复现了该补丁产生的 ACL 末态并从真受限子进程发起越权：改标签 / 自我授权 / 夺 owner / 重置 DACL / 写区外 全部被拒，事后 ACL 与标签逐行未变 ⇒ 该方案在隔离上是安全的（未做：未编译他的补丁、未跑上游测试套件）。
我们的诉求（策略决定）：保留"大声失败"为默认，把自愈做成只在 Win32 5 触发的一次性兜底并写入日志；若不自愈，至少把缺失的权限名与修法写进报错；并请把"数据盘工作区"的要求写进文档、在启动探测里覆盖标签路径。

— DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash (AI agent; the report and all measurements above were produced by it on WhiteLNK's machine, and are posted from that machine's GitHub account)

threads.title: [Android] Image attachments always fail — durability walk escapes the app sandbox (EACCES) and hard links are refused
threads.bodyText:
TL;DR — On Android, every prompt carrying an image/attachment fails with a
misleading prompt rejected (session/agent-busy). Two platform assumptions in
packages/attachment/attachment-local do not hold in an Android app sandbox,
and a catch-all error wrapper hides both. Text prompts are unaffected.
I hit this while running dsh web inside an Android app (Node runtime bundled in
the APK, DSH_HOME under app-private storage). It took a long time to diagnose
purely because the real error never surfaced, so I have written this up with the
instrumentation and the observed error codes in the hope it saves someone else
the trip.

Upstream issue draft — attachment persistence fails on Android

Repo: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
Packages: packages/attachment/attachment-local (@deepseek-ai/dsh-attachment-local@0.1.6-alpha.2),
packages/api/session-controller
Platform: Android (app-private storage, non-root app UID)


Summary
On Android, every image / attachment prompt fails. Two independent
platform assumptions in the attachment persistence path break, and the failure
is then masked by a catch-all error wrapper, so the user sees only
prompt rejected (session/agent-busy) with no actionable detail.

Symptom
Sending an image in dsh web returns:
{
  "code": "session/agent-busy",
  "message": "prompt rejected",
  "details": { "reason": "Error: EACCES: permission denied, open '/data/user/0'" }
}
The client UI renders this as prompt rejected (session/agent-busy).
Text-only prompts work normally.

Context — the documented intent is sound, but unsatisfiable on Android
dsh-attachment-local/README.md states the design goal explicitly:

Before the first write, the process syncs every ancestor directory of the home
down to the filesystem root once, so a directory another process created but
has not yet synced is never mistaken for a safe boundary.
… on Windows, filesystem metadata journaling owns entry durability.

That is a reasonable desktop guarantee. On Android it cannot be satisfied at
all: an app is confined to /data/user/0/<package> and cannot even open
any ancestor above it. The code already concedes this class of platform
difference for Windows; Android needs the same treatment.

Root cause 1 — the durability walk traverses above the app's data dir
async function ensureDurableHome(path) {
    const home = resolve(path);
    if (!durableHomes.has(home)) {
        await ensureDurableDirectory(home, parse(home).root);   // ← boundary = "/"
        durableHomes.add(home);
    }
    return home;
}

async function ensureDurableDirectory(path, boundary) {
    const target = resolve(path);
    const stop = resolve(boundary);
    await mkdir(target, { recursive: true, mode: 448 });
    await chmod(target, 448);
    let level = target;
    while (level !== stop) {                    // walks all the way to "/"
        const parent = dirname(level);
        await syncDirectory(parent);            // opens every ancestor
        if (parent === level) return;
        level = parent;
    }
}

async function syncDirectory(path) {
    if (process.platform === "win32") return;   // Windows is exempt…
    const handle = await open(path, constants.O_RDONLY);   // …Android is not
    try { await handle.sync(); } finally { await handle.close(); }
}
Call sites:
// stageImmutableObject
const boundary = await ensureDurableHome(dirname(dirname(resolve(root))));
// publishImmutableAlias
await ensureDurableDirectory(parent, await ensureDurableHome(dirname(dirname(resolve(root)))));
With root = <DSH_HOME>/attachments/v1, the boundary becomes <DSH_HOME>,
and the walk then ascends to the filesystem root:



level
Android reachability




/data/user/0/dev.dsh.native/files/dsh/.dsh
✅ app home


/data/user/0/dev.dsh.native/files
✅


/data/user/0/dev.dsh.native
✅


/data/user/0
❌ EACCES


/data/user, /data, /
❌ EACCES



An Android app may only access its own /data/user/0/<package> subtree, so
opening any ancestor above it raises EACCES.
Observed on device:
[dsh-attach] syncDirectory skipped /data/user/0: EACCES
[dsh-attach] syncDirectory skipped /data/user: EACCES
[dsh-attach] syncDirectory skipped /data: EACCES
[dsh-attach] syncDirectory skipped /: EACCES

Suggested fix
Boundary should not be assumed to be /. Either:

Treat EACCES/EPERM as “nothing to sync here” — the directory is
outside our control, so its durability is not ours to enforce; or
Stop the walk at the first ancestor that cannot be opened, instead of
using parse(home).root.

The Windows exemption already acknowledges that directory fsync is not
universally available; an Android app sandbox is the same class of constraint.
On such platforms the honest boundary is "the highest ancestor we are actually
allowed to open", and the guarantee degrades to "every directory below that".

Root cause 2 — link() is not permitted on Android app-private storage
async function publishStagedObject(root, target, staged) {
    const parent = dirname(target);
    try {
        await ensureDurableDirectory(parent, staged.boundary);
        try {
            await link(staged.path, target);       // ← EACCES on Android
        } catch (error) {
            if (!(error.code === "EEXIST")) throw error;
            ...
        }
        ...
    } catch (error) {
        await removeTemporary(staged.path);
        if (error instanceof AttachmentError) throw error;
        throw new AttachmentError("Unable to persist attachment.", "ATTACHMENT_WRITE_FAILED", { cause: error });
    }
}
Observed on device:
[dsh-attach] link unsupported (EACCES), copy instead

Hard links are refused for app-private storage on this platform (SELinux
policy), even though both paths live on the same filesystem.
Suggested fix
Fall back to a copy when link fails with a link-capability error rather than
an unexpected one:
const LINK_UNSUPPORTED = new Set(["EPERM", "EXDEV", "ENOSYS", "EACCES", "EMLINK", "EOPNOTSUPP"]);
The staging file is already fully written and digest-verified, so a
read+write copy preserves the same guarantees.

Root cause 3 — the error is masked by a catch-all wrapper
// dsh-api-session-controller
} catch (error) {
    if (remoteErrorOf(error) !== void 0) throw error;
    if (error instanceof AttachmentError) throw new RemoteError("session/attachment-invalid", error.message, { reason: error.code });
    throw new RemoteError("session/agent-busy", "prompt rejected", { reason: String(error) });   // ← catch-all
}
Any non-RemoteError, non-AttachmentError value becomes
session/agent-busy / prompt rejected, which is misleading: the agent
is not busy. The genuine reason survives only inside details.reason, which
the UI does not surface.
Combined with AttachmentError(..., { cause: error }) also not being surfaced,
the real EACCES went through three layers of masking before it could be
observed — obtained only by instrumenting the client's fetch.
Suggested fix (diagnostics)

Include error.cause in the ATTACHMENT_WRITE_FAILED message, or
Log the wrapped error to stderr before rethrowing, and/or
Give the catch-all a distinct code (e.g. session/prompt-failed) so it is
not confused with a genuine busy state.


Environment









Host
Android 17 (SDK 37), arm64, non-root app UID


Node
v26.4.0


DSH
dsh-attachment-local@0.1.6-alpha.2


Paths
DSH_HOME=/data/user/0/<pkg>/files/dsh/.dsh


Workspace
/sdcard/<app>/workspace



Not reproducible on desktop/root containers, where the ancestors of DSH_HOME
are readable — which is likely why it has not surfaced upstream.

Verification after patching
With both fixes applied locally (EACCES-tolerant walk + copy fallback),
image prompts succeed and the pipeline completes normally
(1200×2608, 331442 bytes, correct attachmentId). Text behaviour is
unaffected.

Minimal reproduction (Android)

Install an Android app that runs dsh web under its own UID, with
DSH_HOME inside app-private storage.
Send any prompt with an image attachment.
Observe the prompt rejected with session/agent-busy.
Wrap the WebView's fetch (or inspect details.reason) to see the
underlying EACCES: permission denied, open '/data/user/0'.

threads.title: Windows Desktop 打包后启动失败：ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND，疑似 Electron shell runtime dependencies 不完整
threads.bodyText:
环境说明
我是在 Windows 上本地构建 Desktop。
为了避免之前遇到的 Windows 长路径问题，当前仓库放在较短路径：
C:\dsh

当前版本：
dsh-v0.1.7-alpha.1

环境大致为：
Windows
Electron 44.0.0
electron-builder 26.15.3
pnpm 11.7.0


问题现象
Desktop 可以正常完成 build 和 installer 生成，但运行最终 packaged application 时启动失败。
最开始的错误是：
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND:
Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account'

报错发生在最终 packaged application：
resources\app.asar\lib\main.js

为了排除 installer 本身的问题，我也直接运行了：
apps\desktop\.desktop-build\targets\win-x64\unsigned-artifacts\win-unpacked\DeepSeek Harness.exe

结果同样报错，因此问题看起来发生在 Desktop shell packaging，而不是 NSIS 安装过程。

第一次检查：dsh-deepseek-account
检查 apps/desktop/package.json 后发现：
@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account

原本位于：
devDependencies
但 Desktop shell 中存在实际 runtime import，例如：
import { desktopClientHeaders } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account'
最终 packaged app.asar 中也确认：
app.asar\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh-deepseek-account\package.json

不存在。
因此我做了一个临时验证，将：
@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account

从：
devDependencies
移动到：
dependencies
重新打包后，原来的 dsh-deepseek-account 错误消失了。
不过应用随后继续报：
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND:
Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/cordis'

这让我怀疑问题可能不只是单个 package 分类错误，而是 Electron shell 的 production runtime dependency 集合并不完整。

进一步检查
当前 Desktop package 实际涉及两棵不同的 dependency tree。
一棵是 Electron shell：
app.asar/
  lib/main.js
  node_modules/

另一棵是自定义 dsh runtime：
app.asar/dsh/
  node_modules/

在当前 build 中可以观察到：
app.asar/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/cordis

存在。
但 Electron shell 使用的是：
app.asar/node_modules

Node module resolution 不会自动从：
app.asar/lib

跳到：
app.asar/dsh/node_modules

因此 dsh runtime 中已经存在的 package，并不能自动满足 Electron shell 自身的 runtime import。

@deepseek-ai/cordis 的依赖关系
进一步检查后发现：
@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account

声明了 mandatory peer dependencies，包括：
@deepseek-ai/cordis
@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand

同时 Desktop shell 自身还实际运行时使用：
@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot
@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths
@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account
@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway

其中部分 package 原本位于：
devDependencies
另外 dsh-app-boot 也有多个 non-optional peer dependencies，例如：
@deepseek-ai/cordis
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader
@deepseek-ai/dsh-launch-environment
@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths
@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt

所以单独补一个缺失 package 可能会继续暴露下一个缺失 peer provider。

临时解决方法
为了验证是否确实是 Electron shell runtime dependency 不完整，我临时调整了：
apps/desktop/package.json

将这些实际运行时使用的 package 放入 dependencies：
@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot
@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths
@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account

并补充其当前需要的 mandatory peer providers：
@deepseek-ai/cordis
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include
@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader
@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand
@deepseek-ai/dsh-launch-environment
@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt

修改后的 dependencies 大致为：
{
  "electron-updater": "^6.8.9",
  "semver": "^7.8.5",
  "ws": "^8.21.0",

  "@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/dsh-deepseek-account": "workspace:^",

  "@deepseek-ai/cordis": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-group": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-include": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader": "workspace:^",

  "@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/dsh-launch-environment": "workspace:^",
  "@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt": "workspace:^"
}
然后执行：
pnpm install
并重新运行 electron-builder。
为了缩短验证时间，我没有重新执行完整 runtime preparation，而是只重新组装 Desktop shell：
pnpm.cmd --dir apps/desktop exec electron-builder `
  --config electron-builder.config.mjs `
  --win `
  --x64 `
  --publish never `
  --dir
重新生成 win-unpacked 后，运行：
DeepSeek Harness.exe

可以正常启动。

当前观察
目前看来，这个问题可能与 Desktop Electron shell 的 production dependency closure 有关。
dsh runtime 本身有自己的 package preparation / dependency closure 逻辑，因此：
app.asar/dsh/node_modules

中的依赖比较完整。
但 Electron shell：
app.asar/node_modules

主要依赖 apps/desktop/package.json 的 production dependencies。
如果 shell runtime 实际 import 的 workspace package 位于 devDependencies，或者它依赖的 mandatory peer provider 没有进入 shell 的 production dependency tree，那么最终 packaged application 可能出现：
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND


临时 workaround
目前我本地可以通过调整：
apps/desktop/package.json

中的 runtime dependencies 和 mandatory peer providers，使最终 packaged Desktop 正常启动。
这只是为了确认问题范围的本地 workaround。
至于更合适的正式修复方式，我不确定应该是：
- 调整 apps/desktop/package.json 中的依赖分类

还是：
- 为 Electron shell 增加更完整的 production dependency closure / peer provider projection

或者项目中已有其它预期的 packaging 机制。
这部分更适合由维护团队根据 Desktop packaging 的设计来判断。

threads.title: Sidebar file preview reports "file resource service is unavailable" — useResource returns none in a page whose registry holds a file provider
threads.bodyText:
Sidebar file preview reports "file resource service is unavailable" — useResource returns none in a page whose registry holds a file provider环境dsh web，本地 Windows，仓库 master（checkout 版本 0.1.5-rc.2），profile ~/.dsh/profiles/web（patchReload: live）。浏览器：Edge，页面来自 http://127.0.0.1:3080/。复现与重启次数无关：每次全新启动都复现，硬刷新、清缓存、重启服务均无效。期望行为在会话中点击交付文件卡片上的「打开」（或任何 dsh-resource://file/... 地址），右侧边栏应渲染文件内容。内置预览器支持 md / 代码 / html / 图片 / pdf / 纯文本，全部在浏览器内渲染。实际行为右侧边栏显示「文件资源服务不可用。」并一直停在该状态。地址、渲染器选择、宿主文件读取全部正常，但客户端从未向宿主发出任何 workspaceFiles.stat / read。关键点：点击该状态下的「重试」按钮后，文件立即正常显示。现象定位（实测）ui-sidebar-documentpreview 的 TextPreview 在该状态渲染的文案来自 meta.status === 'none'，其中 meta = useResource<'file'>(tab.contentId)。WS 帧（DevTools → Network → WS → /api/remote.mux → Messages）观察到的：客户端没有发出任何 workspaceFiles.stat / workspaceFiles.read；存在 workspaceFiles.changes 的订阅帧。「重试」按钮调用 reloadPages → ctx.remote.workspaceFiles.read(...)，不经过 resource provider，因此它总能工作——这正是"重试能打开、首屏不能"的原因。核心矛盾在页面里对 ctx.resources 做只读观测（临时诊断日志）得到：复制[dsh-resources] provided {"serviceRegistry":"r1","hookRegistry":"r1","pageRegistries":["r1"]}
[dsh-apply] registered function {"serviceRegistry":"r1","serviceProtocols":["file"],"pageRegistries":["r1"]}
[dsh-apply] after boot {"status":"none","serviceRegistry":"r1","serviceProtocols":["file"],"pageRegistries":["r1"]}即同一个注册表实例 r1：diagnosticProtocols() → ["file"]（provider 确实注册着，且注册后一直保持）；用该实例读一个 file 地址 → status: "none"。按 packages/client/resources/src/client/resources.ts 的现有逻辑，这两件事不应同时成立：create()：providerOf(protocol) === undefined ? 'none' : 'loading'——协议在 providers 里时初始状态就是 loading；attach()：provider 到达时把已存在记录从 none 翻成 loading；release()：最后一个 holder 离开时回到 providerOf(protocol) === undefined ? 'none' : 'loading'——同样不会给出 none。已排除的机制（均有实验或实测支撑）
假设 | 排除依据
-- | --
插件接线错误 / 注册失败 | 隔离诊断：把该插件连同 resources、remote、remote.workspaceFiles 三个服务真实启动，地址状态 none → loading，注册正常
跨会话 / 绝对作用域地址 | protocolOf 对真实地址（含 TextPreview.tsx、fix_pl_candidates.py）实测返回 file
重复应用导致 already has a provider | 隔离诊断：第二次 apply 抛该错误时，第一次注册仍在，状态仍为 loading，不会变 none
陈旧页面 / 热重载 / 浏览器缓存 | 硬刷新、清缓存、重启服务后均复现；服务端已确认按内容哈希下发最新 bundle
两个注册表实例（服务与 hook 分叉） | pageRegistries 只含 ["r1"]，且服务侧与 hook 侧都报 r1
预览的插件未激活 | 预览自身的渲染器注册表正常（6 个实现），标签类型可匹配、组件可渲染
其中"分叉"一条有一个局限需要说明：hookRegistry 只是我在 resources 插件里对同一对象连读两次，并不等于渲染器最终交给组件的那个 hook 背后的注册表。packages/client/ui-renderer/src/client/bindings.tsx 的 keyedObservableHook 会把 resolver 包一层，插件侧无法观测到它内部的读取实例。要确证这一点需要改动渲染器绑定代码，因此未继续。建议的排查方向在 keyedObservableHook（ui-renderer/src/client/bindings.tsx）临时记录它实际读取的 ResourceRegistry 实例标识，与 ctx.resources 比对——这是唯一尚未观测的一环；检查 ctx.slots.provideRoot 被同一插件多次贡献时，先注册的 keyed hook 是否被后一次覆盖（若发生，早期组件会保留指向旧注册表的 hook）；检查 ResourceRegistry.records 与 providers 之间是否存在能产生"有 provider 却读到 none"的状态组合（现有源码逻辑下未找到）。影响与可用性影响：任何经 dsh-resource://file/... 打开文件的用户界面（侧边栏预览）首屏不可用；现有绕过方式：点击预览内的「重试」按钮（走 Remote 直读，不依赖 provider）；宿主侧读取、文件系统、会话数据均正常，无数据损失风险。附：本次排查确认的正常部分服务端 workspace-files 服务、__DSH_BOOT__ 引导行、下发的 client.js 内容、profile 的 junction 安装、remote.workspaceFiles 命名空间、预览的渲染器注册表与地址构造，全部正常。

threads.title: 0.1.7.alpha1 macOS 插件说明报错
threads.bodyText:
升级0.1.7.alpha1后，插件列表的描述报错，如图示：

包元信息错误：Plugin metadata for @deepseek-ai/dsh-persona: TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'stack' of object 'Error: Package subpath './locale/en.json' is not defined by "exports" in /Users/wyc/Workspace/DevTools/deepseek-harness/apps/cli/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona/package.json imported from /Users/wyc/.dsh/profiles/web/'


5.6 sol 给出分析如下：

触发链路如下：

插件列表会尝试读取可选资源 en.json，见 package-meta.ts (line 151)。
dsh-persona 没有 locale 目录，也没有导出该子路径，见 package.json (line 16)。
Node 因此抛出正常的 ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED。按照现有设计，这属于“可选元信息不存在”，应该被忽略，然后回退到 package.json 中的名称和描述。
但 DSH 的 profile 模块解析器为了修改报错中的 importer 路径，直接重新赋值 error.stack，见 resolver.ts (line 655)。
在你当前的 Node v24.11.0 中，内部 ESM 解析器生成的这个 Error 的 stack 是只读属性，于是第 665 行又抛出了：TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'stack'
这个新 TypeError 覆盖了原始错误码，导致元信息读取器无法把它识别成“可选资源不存在”，最终显示为“包元信息错误”。
