threads.title: Desktop 0.2.1 fails to start: STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (0xC000001D / UD2) in electron::fuses::IsLoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8SnapshotEnabled on Windows 11
threads.bodyText:
Desktop crashes at startup with STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION (0xC000001D) in electron::fuses::IsLoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8SnapshotEnabled on Windows 11
Summary
After a successful in-app auto-update to 0.2.1-rc.2, the Windows desktop app became permanently unable to start. Every launch exits within ~1 second with code 0x80000003, before main.js executes at all.
A ProcDump capture reveals the real fatal exception is 0xC000001D (STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION) raised by an UD2 instruction inside electron::fuses::IsLoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8SnapshotEnabled, i.e. an immediate CHECK() failure.
The same crash reproduces on three different builds (0.2.0-rc.2, 0.2.1-rc.1, 0.2.1-rc.2), with completely clean installs (install dir, userData, and updater cache all deleted and recreated), and with the DSH home directory entirely absent.
Critically: the same 0.2.0-rc.2 installer ran fine on this machine before the update. Reinstalling that exact same build from the official CDN afterwards crashes identically. This points at a machine-level state change that the update introduced, not at a specific build.
Environment



Item
Value




OS
Windows 11 Pro, build 26200.9711 (25H2)


CPU
13th Gen Intel Core i5-13600KF (Raptor Lake, AVX2, no AVX-512)


Desktop version
0.2.1-rc.2 (also reproduced on 0.2.1-rc.1, 0.2.0-rc.2)


Electron
44.7.0


Chrome
152.0.7977.130


V8
15.2.124.28-electron.0


Node (bundled)
24.21.0


Install path
<DRIVE>:\<PATH WITHOUT SPACES ISSUES>\DSH DESKTOP (non-system drive, local fixed NTFS volume)


DSH_HOME
<USERPROFILE>\.dsh




Note: the install directory lives on a secondary local fixed NVMe NTFS volume, which was verified to be a plain fixed disk (DriveType 3), not a network/SUBST/VHD volume. ACLs on both install dir and userData are default (owner full control).

Exit code and stack
Launching the exe directly produces:
exit code: -2147483645  (0x80000003)   STATUS_BREAKPOINT

ELECTRON_ENABLE_STACK_DUMPING=1 gives:
Received fatal exception EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT
    DeepSeek Harness!electron::fuses::IsLoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8SnapshotEnabled [..+8e]
    DeepSeek Harness!v8::ScriptCompiler::CreateCodeCacheForFunction [..+1877]
    DeepSeek Harness!v8::SharedMemoryStatistics::SharedMemoryStatistics [..+1ec0]
    DeepSeek Harness!v8::SharedMemoryStatistics::SharedMemoryStatistics [..+1977]
    DeepSeek Harness!v8::SharedMemoryStatistics::SharedMemoryStatistics [..+13bd]
    DeepSeek Harness!uv_cond_signal [..+355e2]
    KERNEL32!BaseThreadInitThunk
    ntdll!RtlUserThreadStart

ProcDump (procdump64 -ma -e 1 -f 80000003) reveals the full exception sequence — the breakpoint is only the second-chance symptom:
[..] Exception: 406D1388                          (thread naming, benign)
[..] Exception: 406D1388
[..] Exception: 80000003.BREAKPOINT
[..] Exception: C000001D.ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION      <-- real fault
[..] Unhandled: C000001D.ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION

Dump analysis
From the minidump's MINIDUMP_EXCEPTION_STREAM:
ExceptionCode : 0xC000001D  (STATUS_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION)
ExceptionAddr : 0x00007FF7_02FAFE2F
Module        : "DeepSeek Harness.exe" (base 0x7FF6FFCB0000, size 0xEA7D000)
RVA           : 0x32FFE2F

Disassembly at that RVA:
RVA 0x32FFE2E  cc        int3
RVA 0x32FFE2F  0f 0b     ud2        <-- crash

UD2 is emitted by the compiler for IMMEDIATE_CRASH() / failed CHECK(). This is not a missing CPU instruction — the binary deliberately traps.
Strings referenced by the crashing function
Walking lea instructions in the ±512 byte window around 0x32FFE2F yields exactly two string references:
RVA 0x32FFD73  ->  "browser_v8_context_snapshot.bin"
RVA 0x32FFDED  ->  "no-sandbox"

The nearby control flow (decoded by hand) is:
call <init>
call <check>                 ; -> al
je   <return 0>              ; condition false -> return
lea  rdx, "no-sandbox"
call <argv contains no-sandbox?>
jne  <return>
...
call <internal>
test eax, eax
jne  <UD2>                   ; non-zero -> immediate crash
This matches fuses::IsLoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8SnapshotEnabled exactly: on the failing path the browser process either must load browser_v8_context_snapshot.bin or take the --no-sandbox branch.
Electron fuse wire — LoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot is disabled
The fuse sentinel in this kernel is dL7pKGdnNz796PbbjQWNKmHXBZaB9tsX (note: not the commonly documented ...B9fgd suffix). Immediately after it:
01 09 31 30 31 31 30 30 30 31 31        -> version=1, wireLen=9, wire="101100011"

Decoding with the Electron 44 fuse order:
[0] RunAsNode                                  ENABLED
[1] EnableCookieEncryption                     DISABLED
[2] EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable       ENABLED
[3] EnableNodeCliInspectArguments              ENABLED
[4] EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation      DISABLED
[5] OnlyLoadAppFromAsar                        DISABLED
[6] LoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot       DISABLED   <-- relevant
[7] GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges           ENABLED
[8] WasmTrapHandlers                           ENABLED

So the fuse is off, yet the code path still evaluates the browser-snapshot decision. The build ships only v8_context_snapshot.bin — there is no browser_v8_context_snapshot.bin in resources/. The embedded resource manifest in the binary does declare the expected digest:
browser_v8_context_snapshot.bin
883f08309bf436fb442d1903452a69c03747ed77c5f502e88667d9aa1b706556

which is byte-identical to the SHA-256 of the shipped v8_context_snapshot.bin. Renaming/copying that file to browser_v8_context_snapshot.bin does not fix the crash (digest matches, still traps), so the failing check is not simple file presence.
Reproduction matrix



#
Build
Install dir
userData
Updater cache
DSH_HOME
Result




1
0.2.1-rc.1 (auto-updated)
reused
reused
reused
present
0x80000003


2
0.2.1-rc.2 (official CDN)
reused
reused
reused
present
0x80000003


3
0.2.0-rc.2 (official CDN)
reused
reused
reused
present
0x80000003


4
0.2.1-rc.2
clean
clean
clean
present
0x80000003


5
0.2.1-rc.2
clean
clean
clean
absent (renamed away)
0x80000003


6
0.2.1-rc.2 + minimal 440-byte app.asar
clean
clean
clean
absent
0x80000003, main.js never executes



Reproduction #6 is the decisive isolation: replacing the entire 121 MB app.asar with a 440-byte app that only writes one file still traps identically, so no application code (Cordis, plugins, profiles, hooks) is involved — the failure is in the Electron browser-process bootstrap.
What was ruled out



Hypothesis
How it was tested
Result




App code / plugins / profile config
minimal 440-byte app.asar (#6)
still crashes, main.js never runs


User data corruption
userData deleted and recreated; DSH_HOME renamed away (#4, #5)
still crashes, zero files created


Install path / volume
copied whole install dir to another path; verified local fixed NTFS
still crashes


Corrupt installer / partial update
cached installer SHA-512 matches update-info.json exactly; app.asar size matches header offsets exactly
verified intact


Bad binary / snapshot
same exe runs fine under ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (prints Electron 44.7.0 / Node 24.21.0); snapshot header declares 15.2.124.28-electron.0, matching the binary
binary and snapshots intact


Missing ANGLE DLLs
libEGL.dll / libGLESv2.dll / chrome_crashpad_handler.exe are absent from the package (also absent on a clean official install), copying them in changes nothing
not the cause


GPU / display adapters
--disable-gpu, --disable-gpu-compositing, --use-angle=d3d11, --use-angle=swiftshader, --in-process-gpu, --single-process, --disable-gpu-sandbox, --disable-features=RendererCodeIntegrity, --disable-seccomp-filter-sandbox, --no-zygote
all still 0x80000003


Defender / WDAC
no detections on the install path; 13 active CI policies are Microsoft-signed defaults; AppInit_DLLs empty; no IFEO entries for the exe
not the cause


Shell env / PATH pollution
launched from a clean cmd with minimal PATH
still crashes


My own automation sandbox
launched via Task Scheduler in the interactive user session (outside the harness process tree) and via Explorer
still crashes


Third-party sandboxes / tools
stopped and disabled a third-party codex-windows-sandbox-service; exited Process Lasso; both reverted afterwards
still crashes


System files modified
C:\Windows\System32 file timestamps all predate the incident (last change was a Windows update 3 days earlier, when the app still worked)
nothing changed at crash time


Rebooting
full power cycle, no change
still crashes



The one switch that changes behaviour
Only --no-sandbox (or ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1) alters the outcome: with sandbox disabled the process no longer traps on 0xC000001D, it runs for a while and exits 0 — but still no window and no JS executed.
baseline                          -> 0x80000003
--no-sandbox                      -> exit 0 (no window, main.js never runs)
ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1        -> exit 0 (same)
--js-flags=--no-snapshot          -> 0x80000003
--disable-v8-idle-tasks           -> 0x80000003
--user-data-dir=<tmp>             -> 0x80000003

This suggests the failing CHECK() is reached through the sandbox-enabled path and is bypassed entirely under --no-sandbox, while a different early failure prevents the --no-sandbox path from completing.
Correlation with the update
The app worked normally until the in-app auto-update at ~19:27 local time. File CreationTimes in the install directory show the new payload being written at 19:27:29–19:27:38. The old build's userData last wrote Cookies at 19:27:28 — one second before. From 19:27:29 onward, every launch fails.
No Windows Update, driver install, or system service change occurred in that window; the System and Application logs are empty for 19:20–19:35 apart from unrelated Software Protection events. The most recent system-level change was a Windows update 3 days earlier, after which the app still ran.
Request
We would like to know:

Is LoadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot intended to be effective even though the fuse wire reads 0 for it? If the code path can still be taken, under what conditions — and should the package ship a browser_v8_context_snapshot.bin?
Is there a known CHECK() in that region that can fail when a supporting runtime precondition is not met (e.g. a specific Windows build, VBS/CI policy state, or an updated system component)?
What additional diagnostics would help — e.g. a debug build with the CHECK message retained, or a documented environment variable to dump the failing condition?

Attachments

A 293 MB full-memory minidump of the crash is available on request (it contains stack memory and may include user file paths, so it is not attached publicly). The essential extracted fields are reproduced above.
Extracted strings/disassembly around RVA 0x32FFE2F can be provided as a text file if useful.
